claudius_1.epilogue: Claudius receives you without witnesses, in a study full of maps. "I need a courier who doesn't exist," he says. "Letters that pass through no network. Not even your commander's." He studies you with those eyes that weighed you once before. "Your reputation for honesty is worth paying for. Come back tomorrow. There will be a letter." Outside, the Roman night seems to have more ears than torches.
claudius_1.intro: The note is brief and the paper very expensive: "To the messenger who doesn't lie. My villa, at sundown. Come alone." You remember the Senator: Varus's test, his chess-player questions. Senators don't invite messengers to their villas. They use them. And yet here you are, the note burning a hole in your pocket and a decision to make before you leave.
claudius_1.journal: Senator Claudius wants me as his private courier. Off the network. Off the books.
claudius_1.lore: A slave in patrician livery left you an unsigned note: Senator Claudius wants to see you. You. Without Varus.
claudius_1.package: Nothing. This time, you're the package.
claudius_1.title: Chapter I — The off-network job
claudius_2.epilogue: The temple priest takes the letter without opening it and drops it into a brazier. The black wax sputters green. "Tell the one who sent you that Saturn keeps silent," he recites, like someone repeating an old password. You leave the temple feeling you've delivered something much heavier than paper.
claudius_2.intro: The steward hands you the letter like a live coal: fast and without looking at it. A double seal of black wax. "The Senator says it doesn't exist, that you don't exist, and this letter even less." In the street, you notice a fig seller holding your gaze half a second too long. The trade of not existing begins.
claudius_2.journal: I delivered Claudius's first letter. They burned it unread in front of me. What kind of message is written for the fire?
claudius_2.lore: Claudius's first letter. Double seal, zero questions. Destination: a priest at the Temple of Saturn who "will know what to do."
claudius_2.package: A letter with a double seal and no sender
claudius_2.title: Chapter II — The price of curiosity
claudius_3.epilogue: What happened on the road keeps turning in your head while Tiro — a little man with ink-stained fingers — receives what's left of your delivery. Now you know what you carried: evidence against Senator Petro. The same Petro who, according to the letter, secretly funds Varus's messenger network. Your network. Your commander. Claudius isn't cleaning up Rome: he's sawing off the branch you're standing on.
claudius_3.intro: You've never seen Claudius nervous until today. "The scribe Tiro. Before midnight. And messenger..." — he holds you by the arm — "...if they stop you, burn it. Understood?" A scroll worth more burned than read. In your trade, such letters have a name: death sentences.
claudius_3.journal: The letter implicates Senator Petro: the secret patron of Varus's network. Claudius is going after him. And I chose my side on a dark road.
claudius_3.lore: The third letter is different: thick, urgent, and Claudius put it in your hand himself. "This one can't be dropped. This one can't get wet. This one can't exist."
claudius_3.package: A thick scroll, sealed three times
claudius_3.title: Chapter III — The letter that burns
claudius_4_claudius.epilogue: The presiding judge takes the dossier with eager fingers. By dawn, Rome has a fresh scandal and you, a powerful patron. Varus's network doesn't fall — Petro negotiated, patricians always negotiate — but it's wounded and knows it. At headquarters, nobody saves you a place by the fire anymore. At Claudius's villa, though, your cup is always full. You chose. It costs.
claudius_4_claudius.intro: "Petro falls tonight," says Claudius, handing you a leather tube sealed with his ring. "And with him, the clandestine network he funds. I know it was yours. That's why I trust you: you chose the future over nostalgia." The tube weighs like a gravestone. Varus's, perhaps.
claudius_4_claudius.journal: I carried the dossier that wounded the network that made me. Claudius calls me "my courier." Varus doesn't call me anymore.
claudius_4_claudius.lore: You delivered the letter as if nothing were wrong. Claudius noticed. "You're my courier now." Tonight everything is decided: the dossier must reach the judges.
claudius_4_claudius.title: Chapter IV — The night of knives
claudius_4_underworld.epilogue: The Widow reads, smiles, and slides you a purse you needn't count. "Neither Claudius nor Petro. Both will pay to keep this in the dark. And you, messenger..." — she studies you with professional respect — "...you've just learned that information weighs less than gold and is worth more." From tonight, the Subura knows you. And doors that open at night never close again.
claudius_4_underworld.intro: The password is "the crow drinks alone." The tavern has no sign and the man behind the counter has no questions. At the back, the Widow — nobody knows whose — collects secrets the way others collect amphorae. Your copy of the dossier can sink two senators at once. Or hold them both by the throat. That's worth gold. And enemies.
claudius_4_underworld.journal: I sold the secret to the Widow of the Subura. Now two senators sleep badly and I walk the night like it's home.
claudius_4_underworld.lore: You copied what needed copying before delivering. In the Subura, people pay fortunes for senators' secrets. Tonight, yours goes to auction.
claudius_4_underworld.title: Chapter IV — The night of knives
claudius_4_varus.epilogue: Petro reads your warning by the light of a single candle, and for a moment the unflappable patrician lets relief show. "Varus chose his people well." Before dawn, Claudius's witnesses change their testimony and his evidence changes hands. The network breathes. Claudius, somewhere in Rome, breaks something expensive.
claudius_4_varus.intro: Varus didn't thank you. Men like him thank with trust, not words. "Claudius will move his pieces tonight. Petro has to know before dawn or the whole network wakes up hanged. Run, messenger. Run like never before." Outside, Rome sharpens knives in the dark.
claudius_4_varus.journal: I ran all night to save the network. Petro is safe. Claudius knows it was me. Let him.
claudius_4_varus.lore: Varus read your copy in silence. Then he said three words: "Warn Petro now." Tonight, the whole network is at stake.
claudius_4_varus.package: The warning that can save the network
claudius_4_varus.title: Chapter IV — The night of knives
claudius_5_claudius.epilogue: You deliver at the Curia before scribes who write your name — your name — in the official register. On the way out, a Guild messenger passes you on the steps: he looks at the livery, then your face, and walks on without a greeting. That's what the price feels like. That night, Claudius's pay is generous and the wine at his table excellent. You drink alone. Senators' protégés always drink alone.
claudius_5_claudius.intro: The livery is good wool and the safe-conduct bears the big seal. "Walk down the middle of the street," says Claudius. "Let them see you. A senator is measured by the quality of the men he buys... forgive me, hires." His smile is a contract with fine print. The Senate awaits, and all of Rome watches who walks through that door.
claudius_5_claudius.journal: I entered the Senate in Claudius's livery. The pay is real, the power is real. The friends from headquarters, not anymore.
claudius_5_claudius.lore: Claudius sends you to the Senate itself with his official correspondence. In broad daylight, in his livery. The message is for all of Rome: this courier is mine.
claudius_5_claudius.package: The first letter of your new life
claudius_5_claudius.title: Chapter V — The Senator's protégé
claudius_5_underworld.ending: The one who knows too much
claudius_5_underworld.epilogue: Claudius goes pale as he reads. Petro, on the other hand, laughs — the short laugh of a gambler who recognizes the play. Neither touches you: killing the Widow's messenger means declaring war on the dark half of Rome. Back at the Golden She-Wolf, there's a table with your name and a new road on your map: the night post, the one off the books, the one that pays triple. You know too much to be innocent and too little to be dead. In the Subura, that's called "partner."
claudius_5_underworld.intro: Two letters, same hand, different recipients. "The art," the Widow explains, "isn't in the secret. It's in each knowing the other pays too." You get to be the visible face of an elegant blackmail against two of the most dangerous men in Rome. The Subura watches you walk into the light with its favorite cargo: the truth, carefully managed.
claudius_5_underworld.journal: I delivered the Widow's blackmail to two senators in a single day. Now Rome's night has a road with my name on it.
claudius_5_underworld.lore: The Widow has one last job: deliver the same message to Claudius and to Petro. The message reads: "We know. We collect at month's end."
claudius_5_underworld.package: Two identical letters for two enemy senators
claudius_5_underworld.title: Chapter V — The one who knows too much
claudius_5_varus.epilogue: Claudius reads Petro's letter standing up, without inviting you in. When he's done, he gives you a long look. "You chose the soldier over the senator. I hope his loyalty keeps you warm in winter." There's no threat in his voice; there's something worse: he's crossed you off his list. That night at headquarters, Varus raises his cup without a speech. No need. The whole network knows what you did. You're Varus's man. In Rome, that now means something.
claudius_5_varus.intro: Varus hands you Petro's letter with something very rare on his face: half a smile. "Claudius asked that it not be you. So it's you. In this trade, loyalty is paid in trust — and today you're the man I trust most." The Forum awaits, and on its steps, a senator with a fresh defeat.
claudius_5_varus.journal: The Claudius affair is over. I chose the network, I chose Varus. The Senator crossed me off his list and the Guild wrote me onto theirs.
claudius_5_varus.lore: One loose end remains: Petro's formal reply to Claudius. Varus wants you to carry it. "Let Claudius see the face of the one who stopped him."
claudius_5_varus.package: The last message of the Claudius affair
claudius_5_varus.title: Chapter V — Varus's man
evt_apennine_fog.description: A thick fog rolls down from the Apennines and in minutes you can't see your sandals. Cowbells ring in the distance. The road has a drop on one side, and you don't know which.
evt_apennine_fog.title: Fog in the Mountains
evt_aqueduct_works.description: A crew is repairing an arch of the aqueduct and has blocked the road with scaffolding and oxen. The foreman shouts figures; no one moves a stone without his say.
evt_aqueduct_works.title: Aqueduct Works
evt_bandit_grudge.description: At the bend by the pines, the same bandit from that time is waiting, now with four friends and a new grin. "Run once, run always," he says. He knows your legs.
evt_bandit_grudge.title: The One Who Got Away
evt_bandits.description: A group of bandits steps out from the trees. They know you carry something valuable. They surround you, unhurried.
evt_bandits.title: Ambush on the road
evt_bandits_revenge.description: Further on, the road narrows between two hills. There they are again: the same bandits, twice the men, and the leader in front with an unhurried smile. "He who runs passes this way again."
evt_bandits_revenge.title: They were waiting for you
evt_bees.description: A beekeeper's cart has overturned and the cork hives have rolled across the road. A furious swarm buzzes over the route. The beekeeper, swollen, waves from a ditch.
evt_bees.title: Overturned Hives
evt_bridge.description: The main bridge over the river is destroyed. The recent floods carried off half of it.
evt_bridge.title: Bridge out
evt_buyer_returns.description: The man you sold a peek at the seal sits across from you again, fatter and happier. "That was cheap. Now I want to read all of it. Or the Guild learns you already did it once."
evt_buyer_returns.title: The Buyer Returns
evt_cart_jam.description: Two ox carts locked wheels passing on the narrow bridge. Behind them piles a line of wagons, mules and shouting that helps no one.
evt_cart_jam.title: Jam on the bridge
evt_census.description: At the town gate, two census scribes record everyone who passes: name, father, tribe, property. The line is long and the older scribe writes very slowly.
evt_census.title: The Census Scribes
evt_charcoal_burners.description: The road enters a smoky forest. Charcoal kilns smolder among the trees and soot-blackened men watch you without a greeting. One plants himself in the middle of the path.
evt_charcoal_burners.title: Charcoal Burners
evt_child_family.description: As you pass through the village, a woman runs out of a house with the little girl you once led by the hand. "It's him!" The whole family wants you in for a meal. The road can wait.
evt_child_family.title: The Girl's Family
evt_compitalia.description: It's the Compitalia and the neighbors are honoring the Lares at the crossroads altar. They hang wool dolls, hand out watered wine and let no one pass without a toast.
evt_compitalia.title: Crossroads Feast
evt_contraband_call.description: On the dock, the same merchant from that time recognizes you and waves from behind a stack of amphorae. "I have another light load, messenger. Same price, same silence."
evt_contraband_call.title: Another Nameless Load
evt_counterfeit.description: At a money changer's stall, your change sounds wrong. You bite a denarius and copper peeks out under the silver. The changer smiles as if nothing's amiss.
evt_counterfeit.title: Plated Denarii
evt_deserter.description: Hidden among some rocks, a young man in legion uniform but unarmed quietly begs you not to say you saw him. He's shaking more from fear than cold.
evt_deserter.title: The deserter on the road
evt_dice_game.description: In the way station tavern, a group plays dice with more shouting than coin. They invite you to a hand. The man throwing has fingers that are too quick.
evt_dice_game.title: Dice at the Tavern
evt_fallen_milestone.description: At an unmarked fork, the milestone that should point the way lies face down in the grass. Both roads look equally wide and equally empty.
evt_fallen_milestone.title: The Fallen Milestone
evt_ferry.description: The only way across the estuary is an old barge a boatman runs according to his mood of the day. Today, by the look of it, the mood isn't good.
evt_ferry.title: The estuary ferry
evt_flood.description: Last night's rain has swollen a river you could wade yesterday. The ford vanished under fast brown water. On the other side, the road still waits.
evt_flood.title: Flood at the ford
evt_forge_fire.description: Passing through a way-station village, you see flames rising from the smithy's thatched roof. Inside someone is screaming, and outside no one seems able to act.
evt_forge_fire.title: Fire at the forge
evt_fugitive.description: Three mounted slave catchers block your way. They're after a runaway slave. You saw him a while ago, curled up in a ditch, with the eyes of a cornered animal.
evt_fugitive.title: The Slave Catchers
evt_ghost_road.description: The muleteers from the last village refused to go past the carved stone with you. "That stretch isn't named after dark," one said, and nobody argued.
evt_ghost_road.title: The Stretch No One Names
evt_gladiator_troupe.description: A wagon of chained gladiators sits sideways across the road with a broken axle. The lanista sweats and curses; one of his men, enormous, eyes you like a rival.
evt_gladiator_troupe.title: The Lanista's Men
evt_heatwave.description: The noon sun hits like a personal punishment. The road shimmers with heat and the water in your skin ran out two leagues back.
evt_heatwave.title: Heat wave
evt_horse_sick.description: At the mutatio, the only relay horse is lying down, staring at its belly. The keeper scratches his head. A fox-faced dealer offers a horse of his own, already saddled.
evt_horse_sick.title: Colic at the Station
evt_hostage_escort.description: A legionary escort guards a young Gallic noble, hostage for his tribe. They're camped by the road. The Gaul spots your courier bag and hisses at you in clumsy Latin.
evt_hostage_escort.title: The Gallic Hostage
evt_injured.description: A loose stone on the trail trips you. You fall hard. Your ankle hurts, but the package seems fine.
evt_injured.title: You trip on the road
evt_landslide.description: A rockslide buried the mountain pass this very morning. Stones the size of oxen block the road from side to side.
evt_landslide.title: Rockslide in the hills
evt_letter_bribe.description: At the inn, a man with clean hands and a northern accent sits at your table uninvited. "I know what you carry. I only want to read it. No one will know, and this..." — he slides over a pouch that clinks of silver — "...is yours."
evt_letter_bribe.title: The price of curiosity
evt_lost_child.description: At the crossroads, a girl of no more than six cries alone, no one in sight. Through her tears she repeats a name: a village's, or maybe her mother's.
evt_lost_child.title: The crossroads girl
evt_merchant_offer.description: A merchant with too many rings offers you a ride: "You'll get there in half the time. All I ask is, if anyone asks, you didn't see what's under the tarp." Under the tarp are amphorae with no customs seal.
evt_merchant_offer.title: The merchant's cart
evt_mute_boy.description: For three milestones a skinny boy has followed you at twenty paces. If you stop, he stops. If you speak, he looks down. He says nothing; it seems he can't.
evt_mute_boy.title: The Mute Boy
evt_old_soldier.description: A veteran of the Legions, more wine than man at this hour, blocks the bridge's narrow passage. "No one crosses without hearing how I lost this eye in Gaul!" The story doesn't look short. It doesn't look like a lie either.
evt_old_soldier.title: The veteran on the bridge
evt_omen.description: At the crossroads, a thin augur reads the flight of birds. He fixes you with his eyes: "Messenger. The crows flew against the sun. There's shadow on your road... unless the gods get their due."
evt_omen.title: The crossroads augur
evt_oracle.description: At the mouth of a cave, an old woman with white eyes whispers verses no one asked for. She points straight at you: "The message you carry is not the one you think." Then she holds out her hand.
evt_oracle.title: The Sibyl of Cumae
evt_patrol.description: A group of legionaries blocks the way. They're searching every traveler. Your cargo could raise suspicion.
evt_patrol.title: Roman patrol
evt_pickpocket.description: A sharp tug at your belt: a boy of no more than ten bolts off with your coin purse through elbows and baskets. The post is still on you. The money isn't.
evt_pickpocket.title: Quick hands
evt_pilgrims.description: Atia, the priestess of Mercury, is leading a group of pilgrims to the shrine of Fortuna. An old man has fainted by the roadside and she asks for your help.
evt_pilgrims.title: Fortuna's Pilgrims
evt_plague_village.description: A rope hung with black rags crosses the road at the edge of a village. Beyond it, an old man shouts that there's fever inside and no one goes in or out.
evt_plague_village.title: Fever Village
evt_poet.description: A young man in a worn toga, tablets under his arm, latches onto you on the road. He's writing a poem about couriers and needs to live one. He's already started reciting.
evt_poet.title: A Traveling Poet
evt_pontine_barge.description: In the Pontine Marshes, the Appia runs alongside a canal. A mule-drawn barge crosses by night. The boatman is drunk and the mosquitoes are sober and hungry.
evt_pontine_barge.title: Barge Through the Marshes
evt_rival_messenger.description: Sitting against a boundary stone, a messenger from another network clutches a swollen ankle. He knows your satchel at once. "Colleague... my delivery's due today in the same town you're headed to. Take it. I'll owe you more than you can imagine."
evt_rival_messenger.title: The fallen colleague
evt_rival_repays.description: At the crossroads, the rival courier you once helped catches up at a trot and falls in beside you. "I owe you one," he says, breathless. "And I pay my debts. Listen."
evt_rival_repays.title: A Debt Comes Back
evt_salt_road.description: Two salt carriers with a cart loaded to the brim offer you a ride if you'll guard their salt. They say on the next stretch they'd steal your teeth.
evt_salt_road.title: The Salt Cart
evt_shepherd_dispute.description: Two migrating flocks have mixed on the road and their shepherds are fighting over a ram both swear is theirs. Eight hundred sheep block your way. They ask you to judge.
evt_shepherd_dispute.title: A Shepherds' Quarrel
evt_sibyl_echo.description: At the door of a roadside shrine, a priest reads a scroll aloud and you recognize the words: they're the Sibyl of Cumae's. What she told you is starting to happen.
evt_sibyl_echo.title: The Verse Comes True
evt_smuggler_score.description: Three men smelling of the docks block your way on the bridge. "The merchant you handed to the legion spent a month in jail," says the tallest. "You owe him the month."
evt_smuggler_score.title: The Merchant's Friends
evt_spy_drop.description: In an empty square, someone drops a sealed scroll right in front of you and vanishes into the crowd without looking back. The scroll doesn't bear your name, but it's already in your hand.
evt_spy_drop.title: The wrong package
evt_storm.description: A brutal storm front covers the road. The wind fells trees and the rain turns the trail to mud.
evt_storm.title: Storm in the pass
evt_tax_collector.description: At the tollhouse, a collector with a wax tablet checks every load twice. Your package lacks the seal he wants to see, and he's in no hurry.
evt_tax_collector.title: The toll collector
evt_temple_theft.description: Outside the temple, a priest shouts that a silver offering is missing and points at the group of travelers where you happen to be standing.
evt_temple_theft.title: Accused at the temple
evt_temple_wanted.description: At the guard post, a watchman compares every traveler to a sketch in wax. The sketch is bad, but the nose is yours. It's for the temple theft you ran away from.
evt_temple_wanted.title: A Face on the Tablet
evt_traveler_remembers.description: The innkeeper serving you has a new scar on his leg and stares too long. He's the wounded traveler you left by the roadside. He survived, and now the inn is his.
evt_traveler_remembers.title: A Face at the Inn
evt_veteran_land.description: Some newly settled veterans are arguing with the land's former owner. They've laid ploughs across the road so no one passes until the surveyor arrives.
evt_veteran_land.title: Disputed Boundaries
evt_wedding_road.description: A wedding procession fills the whole road: torches, flutes and a crowd of happy guests in no hurry at all. The bride walks in the middle, veiled in orange.
evt_wedding_road.title: Wedding procession
evt_wolf.description: The sun sets and the howls sound closer than comfortable, on a stretch of forest with no villages in sight. Something big moves among the trees, in step with you.
evt_wolf.title: Howls near the road
evt_wounded_traveler.description: By the roadside, an old man lies beside his dead mule. He breathes with difficulty and raises a hand when he sees you. You have a delivery with a deadline. He has no one else.
evt_wounded_traveler.title: The fallen traveler
evt_wreck_salvage.description: A merchant ship broke up on the rocks overnight. The beach is strewn with amphorae and planks, and the locals are already looting. One chest bears the seal of a shipowner from Ostia.
evt_wreck_salvage.title: Wreckage on the Beach
flag.claudius_vetoed: Claudius won't offer you work anymore.
flag.ending_claudius: The Shadow of the Senate ended on Claudius's side: the route to his villa at Tibur is open.
flag.ending_legion_caesar: You carry the Thirteenth's mail: the route from Ariminum to Ravenna is open.
flag.ending_legion_guild: The satchel without a side is yours: the neutral route from Rome to Ravenna is open.
flag.ending_legion_senate: The Senate trusts you with its mail: the route from the Curia to Ariminum is open.
flag.ending_lucius_book: The Widow opened her night market to you: there's a new map in the shop.
flag.ending_lucius_family: The Ox is a network way station: you arrive less tired on the Appia.
flag.ending_lucius_legion: You carry the Tenth's mail: the military route to Capua is open.
flag.ending_underworld: The Shadow of the Senate ended on the Underworld's side.
flag.ending_varus: The Shadow of the Senate ended on the Guild's side: Varus opens express post and contract swaps to you.
flag.eyes_open: You carry the satchel with your eyes open. Varus knows it.
flag.fled_bandits: You chose your legs over steel. Nobody blames you.
flag.fled_temple_accusation: You left the temple too soon. Someone noted your face.
flag.fought_bandits: Word got around: the courier who won't be robbed.
flag.heard_the_sibyl: You heard the whole prophecy. A sibyl's words don't fade.
flag.helped_deserter: A deserter is out there wearing your old cloak. He owes you his life.
flag.helped_lost_child: A little girl made it home holding your hand. That village will remember you.
flag.helped_rival: A rival courier owes you one. In the Guild, these things get around.
flag.helped_traveler: A traveler owes his afternoon to a nameless messenger.
flag.left_traveler: You rode on by. The road takes note of that too.
flag.legion_caesar: You chose the legion: Aufidio's warning went back north.
flag.legion_guild: You chose Varus's rule: you delivered the letter and kept quiet.
flag.legion_senate: You chose the Senate: Aufidio's warning goes to the Curia.
flag.lucius_book: You kept the book. Two hundred names travel with you.
flag.lucius_family: You chose the people on the list. Lucius won't forget it.
flag.lucius_legion: You chose the legion: the book for Gaius's pardon.
flag.paid_bandits: The roads know you pay now. That opens doors and draws trouble.
flag.paid_the_augur: The gods of the crossing are pleased with you.
flag.path_claudius: You chose the Senate. Claudius opens his doors.
flag.path_underworld: You chose the Underworld. Rome has another face now.
flag.path_varus: You chose the Guild. Varus will keep it in mind.
flag.read_aufidio: You read Aufidio's letter. You know when the Thirteenth marches.
flag.read_the_birds: You left an augur without an omen. Someone saw it and was amused.
flag.refused_northman: The northerner left empty-handed and with a good memory.
flag.refused_spy: You said no to the first offer. There will be a second.
flag.reported_smuggler: The Legions put your name on the list of the trustworthy.
flag.rode_contraband: You carried cargo that wasn't yours. Someone in the Underworld knows.
flag.route_nocturna_unlocked: The Night Route is open: jobs that don't exist by day.
flag.saw_the_message: You read what wasn't meant for you. Now you know something others would pay for.
flag.sold_a_look: You sold a look. Cheap today, costly later.
flag.sold_look_claudius: Claudius knows you can be bought.
flag.spared_thief: The boy you let go doesn't forget a debt.
flag.swore_neutral: You swore to Varus the satchel takes no side. Someone heard.
flag.told_varus: Varus knows about the job. He trusts you, and now expects more.
flag.varus_cold: Varus still gives you jobs, but he doesn't look at you the same.
flag.walked_the_storm: You crossed a pass with the storm on top of you. They tell that one in the taverns.
l1_cellar_men.description: Two men without livery come into the Ox, order wine and don't touch it. One eyes the cellar trapdoor. Lucius keeps drying a jug that's already dry. He looks at you.
l1_cellar_men.title: Cellar visitors
l1_old_debt.description: Lucius pours for you without asking and leans his forearms on the bar. "I didn't call you over a debt. I called you because you're the only courier I know who doesn't fully belong to anyone yet." He waits for your answer.
l1_old_debt.title: Lucius's tab
l2_gaius_plea.description: Before you leave, Gaius grabs your arm in the cellar. He's twenty with an old man's hands. "I didn't desert out of fear. My centurion was selling the cohort's grain. If I go back, I'm the one they hang."
l2_gaius_plea.title: The nephew
l2_legion_search.description: A patrol from the Tenth is going through the taverns one by one, asking about a twenty-year-old deserter with a scar on his hand. Gaius has that scar. And you're carrying the letter that names him.
l2_legion_search.title: A search in the Subura
l3_ledger_choice.description: At the inn in Aricia you open Lucius's ledger. It's not accounts: it's a list. Tavern keepers all along the Appia who hide deserters, pay off officers and store contraband. Gaius is just one line. There are two hundred.
l3_ledger_choice.title: The open ledger
l3_milestone_watchers.description: At the third milestone of the Appia, a seated man eats figs and watches you pass. At the fifth, another just like him. Someone knows you're carrying Lucius's ledger, and they're counting your steps.
l3_milestone_watchers.title: Eyes on the milestone
l4_book_hunters.description: In the woods by Forum Appii, four men block the road. They don't want your purse. "The ledger, courier. The spare one." They know exactly what you carry and where.
l4_book_hunters.title: Those who want the ledger
l4_burning_inn.description: Past Aricia, a column of black smoke cuts the sky. It's one of the inns on the list: the roof is burning and the innkeeper is shouting from the yard. Someone is burning the names in the ledger, one by one.
l4_burning_inn.title: The inn on fire
l4_cohort_ride.description: Sextus has come with half a century to receive the ledger. But first he wants the arsonists. "You know the inns on the list," he tells you. "Tell me which one they'd burn next."
l4_cohort_ride.title: Sextus's column
l4_sister_inn.description: In Forum Appii, Livia's inn still stands, but two men with unlit torches sit across the street, waiting for nightfall. Livia sees you arrive and says nothing: she's already seen them.
l4_sister_inn.title: Livia's house
l5_book_auction.description: At the back table of the Golden She-Wolf, the Widow has four buyers waiting: an agent of Petro's, a legion man out of uniform, a harbor merchant and a Senate scribe. They all want the ledger. You have it.
l5_book_auction.title: Golden She-Wolf auction
l5_family_vote.description: In the shuttered Ox, a dozen Appia tavern keepers sit around the big table. All of them are in the ledger; all of them are afraid. Lucius gives you the floor: "You carried it. You say what we do."
l5_family_vote.title: The tavern keepers' table
l5_legion_oath.description: At the Porta Capena, Sextus waits for you with Gaius at his side, wearing the Tenth's tunic again. The thieving centurion is in chains. "The legion owes you one," says Sextus. "And the legion pays in work."
l5_legion_oath.title: Sextus's oath
l5_lucius_last.description: Lucius sets two jugs on the Ox's bar. He doesn't say whether he's grateful or angry: with Lucius you never know until the second. Gaius, Livia, the ledger: it all passed through your hands.
l5_lucius_last.title: The last jug
legion_1.epilogue: Ariminum smells of fear and wet wool. Pompey's recruiters count boys in the forum, and in the taverns a different tale goes around: that Caesar's legion is a day to the north, beyond a skinny river nobody watched until this winter. Tomorrow you cross it.
legion_1.intro: Varus lays a contract on the table. "The Thirteenth, at Ravenna. They pay triple for a courier who isn't from the legion." He doesn't smile. "When a legion pays triple, it's because it doesn't want a soldier carrying its letters."
legion_1.journal: Varus sent me north with the Guild satchel for the Thirteenth. In Ariminum everyone is looking at the same river.
legion_1.lore: The camp of the Thirteenth pays triple for a civilian courier.
legion_1.package: The Guild satchel for the Thirteenth
legion_1.title: Chapter I · The northern satchel
legion_1_sexto.epilogue: Ariminum smells of fear and wet wool. In the forum, Pompey's recruiters count boys; in the taverns, everyone tells a different tale: that Caesar's legion is a day to the north, across a small river nobody watched until this winter. Tomorrow you cross it.
legion_1_sexto.intro: Sexto stops you at the Porta Capena. "The Thirteenth, at Ravenna, wants a courier who wears no uniform. I gave your name to an old friend, Aufidio." He hands you a letter. The bull plaque weighs on your chest, and winter has already come down the Flaminia.
legion_1_sexto.journal: Sexto sent me north with a letter for a centurion of the Thirteenth. In Ariminum everyone is looking at the same river.
legion_1_sexto.lore: Sexto gave your name to the Thirteenth. Ravenna is waiting for a courier.
legion_1_sexto.package: A letter from Sexto for the centurion Aufidio
legion_1_sexto.title: Chapter I · The northern satchel
legion_2.epilogue: Aufidio sees you off at the praetorian gate. "For Quintus Petilio, oil merchant in Ariminum. Nothing more." Behind him, the Thirteenth greases its boots as if it had a long way to walk. Nobody says where.
legion_2.intro: Between Ariminum and Ravenna runs the Rubicon: a skinny, muddy river marking where Caesar's province ends and Italy begins. No general may cross it under arms without the Senate's leave. You cross it with a satchel.
legion_2.journal: Aufidio, centurion of the Thirteenth, gave me a letter for an oil merchant in Ariminum. A centurion doesn't write to an oil merchant without reason.
legion_2.lore: You cross the Rubicon toward the camp of the Thirteenth.
legion_2.package: The satchel, and whatever they give you at camp
legion_2.title: Chapter II · The centurion Aufidio
legion_3.epilogue: In Petilio's back room, among the oil amphorae, the letter is no longer a secret: the Thirteenth marches before the Ides, and Aufidio is warning Ariminum so it isn't caught asleep. You've chosen what to do with that. The river no longer seems so skinny.
legion_3.intro: You leave camp with Aufidio's letter in your sandal. The tribunes search every civilian heading south, and the south begins at the river. Aufidio didn't look at you when you left.
legion_3.journal: Aufidio's letter warns that the Thirteenth will cross the river. He owes everything to Pompey and everything to his men. I decided who gets the warning.
legion_3.lore: Aufidio's letter has to cross the Rubicon before his legion does.
legion_3.title: Chapter III · The letter that crosses the river
legion_4_caesar.epilogue: The legate reads the letter without a flicker and sends it to the general's tent. At nightfall the answer comes back: Aufidio loses his command, but is free to go south with his baggage. "The general doesn't hang men who choose the other side. He lets them go and beats them later." You get a horse.
legion_4_caesar.intro: You head back north with Aufidio's letter for the legate of the Thirteenth. A warning to the enemy, signed by a centurion, on the eve of the march. You know what that's worth in a legion. You also know Aufidio chose you.
legion_4_caesar.journal: I gave Aufidio's letter to the legate. Caesar didn't punish him: he let him go to Pompey. I was given a legion horse.
legion_4_caesar.lore: You take Aufidio's letter to the legate. Aufidio doesn't know yet.
legion_4_caesar.title: Chapter IV · The price of the warning
legion_4_guild.epilogue: You reach Ravenna with the Guild seal unbroken. The tribune who searches you finds letters from mothers, promissory notes and a recipe for garum. Nothing else. At the praetorian gate, Aufidio nods to you. He doesn't know what you kept quiet. Or he does.
legion_4_guild.intro: You delivered Aufidio's letter like any other letter, and kept quiet. But both sides already know a civilian courier comes and goes between Ravenna and Ariminum. When you head back north with the satchel, both want to know what's inside.
legion_4_guild.journal: Both sides tried to open the Guild satchel and neither could. I reached Ravenna with the seal unbroken. Varus will be satisfied, if such a thing exists.
legion_4_guild.lore: Both sides want to open the Guild satchel. Varus said no.
legion_4_guild.title: Chapter IV · The price of the warning
legion_4_senate.epilogue: You enter Rome through the Porta Flaminia with the warning intact and your legs not. In the Forum they're still arguing as if there were time. A slave of Claudius finds you before you find anyone: "The Senator wants you to say it in the Curia. In your own voice."
legion_4_senate.intro: You take the Flaminia toward Rome with Aufidio's warning. Ariminum is too small for a secret: before noon, at the north gate, two riders of the Thirteenth are already asking after a civilian courier.
legion_4_senate.journal: I reached Rome with Aufidio's warning and Caesar's riders behind me. Claudius wants me to tell it in the Curia, in person.
legion_4_senate.lore: You carry the Thirteenth's warning to Rome, with Caesar's riders behind you.
legion_4_senate.package: Aufidio's warning, copied on a tablet
legion_4_senate.title: Chapter IV · The price of the warning
legion_5_caesar.epilogue: On the bank, the general stands a while looking at the water. Then he says something about the die being cast, and the cohorts cross in silence. Ariminum opens its gates at dawn without a fight. From today, the Thirteenth's mail between Ravenna and Ariminum bears your name.
legion_5_caesar.intro: News arrives from Rome: the Senate has driven out the tribunes who spoke for Caesar, and they fled to Ravenna disguised as slaves. That night the Thirteenth forms up without trumpets. The legate gives you the orders for the Ariminum outposts.
legion_5_caesar.journal: I crossed the Rubicon ahead of the Thirteenth. The general said the die was cast. From today I carry the legion's mail between Ravenna and Ariminum.
legion_5_caesar.lore: The Thirteenth marches on the Rubicon and you ride ahead.
legion_5_caesar.title: Chapter V · The night of the river
legion_5_guild.epilogue: At dawn there's a three-line agreement: a satchel under the Guild seal passes through both camps and nobody opens it. Days later the Thirteenth crosses the river, and Aufidio with his men. Wars change owners; roads don't. The neutral satchel is now yours.
legion_5_guild.intro: Varus has summoned one of Caesar's tribunes and one of Pompey's agents to the same table at headquarters. Neither wants to be there; both need their letters to arrive. You bring the satchel from Ravenna and sit at the end.
legion_5_guild.journal: Varus sat Caesar and Pompey at the same table, through two men who hated each other. The Guild satchel has no side, and I'm the one who carries it.
legion_5_guild.lore: Varus seats both sides at his table. You bring the letters.
legion_5_guild.package: Letters from both sides, in the same satchel
legion_5_guild.title: Chapter V · The satchel without a side
legion_5_senate.epilogue: The Curia erupts. That same night, Pompey's men leave for Ariminum with a three-day head start they didn't have before. It isn't enough to stop Caesar, but nobody catches them asleep. The Senate needs couriers who can reach the north. Now it has one.
legion_5_senate.intro: Messengers wait on the steps of the Curia; you've never been inside. Today Claudius brings you in among togas that look at you like mud on their sandals. "Tell them what you saw," he says. "No embellishments. We'll add those."
legion_5_senate.journal: I spoke in the Curia. I told what I saw at Ravenna and the Senate split in two. Now I carry the Senate's mail to the north.
legion_5_senate.lore: Claudius wants you to tell the Curia what you saw at Ravenna.
legion_5_senate.title: Chapter V · The voice in the Curia
lg1_flaminia_post.description: On the way down to Narnia, a post of Pompey's recruits checks everyone heading north. The optio is a boy of twenty itching to find something. Your satchel is the most interesting thing he's seen all morning.
lg1_flaminia_post.title: The Narnia checkpoint
lg1_varus_rule.description: At the city gate, Varus catches up with you at an old man's hurried pace. "Up north there are two sides and one road. The Guild's satchel has no side. Understood, or shall I write it down?"
lg1_varus_rule.title: Varus's rule
lg2_aufidio_letter.description: Aufidio takes you behind the latrines, the only place in camp without ears. He has scars from Gaul and a Picenum accent, Pompey's country. "A letter for Ariminum. No seal. I trust you."
lg2_aufidio_letter.title: The centurion from Picenum
lg2_rubicon_ford.description: The Rubicon is not much: muddy water between reeds and a post of the Thirteenth on the bank. On the other side, Caesar's province. The guards count everyone who crosses, and write it down.
lg2_rubicon_ford.title: The skinny river
lg3_three_doors.description: In Ariminum, Petilio the oil merchant reads Aufidio's letter and goes pale. "The legion marches before the Ides." He looks at you. "Nobody knows this but you and me." That's the problem.
lg3_three_doors.title: Petilio's back room
lg3_tribune_search.description: At the camp's south exit, a young tribune in a new cloak searches civilians one by one. His orders: nothing written leaves for Ariminum. You have something written in your sandal.
lg3_tribune_search.title: The praetorian gate
lg4_aufidio_cell.description: They took his vine staff and his crest. Aufidio waits in a guard tent with his hands unbound: nobody fears he'll run. He sees you come in and isn't surprised. "I knew you were honest. I didn't know to whom."
lg4_aufidio_cell.title: Aufidio, without his staff
lg4_both_camps.description: At the Rubicon way station two men wait for you at separate tables: one of Caesar's tribunes and one of Pompey's agents. Both want a look in the satchel and both pay well. Neither knows about the other.
lg4_both_camps.title: Two offers at the way station
lg4_caesar_riders.description: On the Flaminia, half a day from Ariminum, you spot two riders of the Thirteenth trotting up behind you. They haven't seen you yet. No need to ask who they're after.
lg4_caesar_riders.title: Riders of the Thirteenth
lg4_winter_road.description: December gets into your bones: fog off the marshes, frost on the paving stones and a sky so low you can't see the next milestone. The horse slips. So do you.
lg4_winter_road.title: Frost on the road
lg5_aufidio_farewell.description: Before you leave Ravenna, Aufidio waits at the praetorian gate, helmet under his arm. His letter died in the drawer of a frightened oil merchant. "I won't write it again. I'm staying with my men."
lg5_aufidio_farewell.title: Aufidio at the gate
lg5_curia_floor.description: Hundreds of senators, and you in the middle with Aufidio's warning. Claudius signals you from his bench. Some shout that Caesar wouldn't dare; others, that he should already be in chains. Everyone waits for you to speak.
lg5_curia_floor.title: The courier's voice
lg5_guild_table.description: At headquarters, one of Caesar's tribunes and one of Pompey's agents sit at opposite ends of Varus's table. Nobody touches the wine. Varus hands you the floor: "You've crossed that river more times than they have. Talk."
lg5_guild_table.title: Varus's table
lg5_river_night.description: Pitch dark on the bank of the Rubicon. The cohorts wait without torches and the general stares at the water in silence. The legate calls you: the orders for Ariminum have to cross first.
lg5_river_night.title: The night of the river
lg5_varus_report.description: A tablet from Varus catches up with you on the road with a single word in his cramped hand: "Report." That night, by the light of an oil lamp, you must decide how much of the winter fits in the wax.
lg5_varus_report.title: The report to Varus
lucius_1_claudius.epilogue: Lucius tears up the note in front of you and takes you down to the cellar. Behind the barrels is a thin, trembling boy and, on a cask, a fat ledger. "My nephew Gaius, deserter from the Tenth. And half the Appia is in that book. Tell Claudius what you like. I'm telling you the truth."
lucius_1_claudius.intro: Your first job in Claudius's livery is an odd one: collecting from a tavern keeper. Lucius, of the Ox, owes the Senator a favor from twenty years ago. Claudius doesn't want the money. He wants to know what Lucius is hiding.
lucius_1_claudius.journal: I went to the Ox to collect a debt for Claudius and Lucius opened his cellar to me. A deserter nephew and a book with half the Appia in it. It's not an old debt anymore: it's a new one.
lucius_1_claudius.lore: Claudius sends you to collect an old debt at the Ox Tavern.
lucius_1_claudius.package: Claudius's IOU against a tavern keeper
lucius_1_claudius.title: Chapter I · An old debt
lucius_1_underworld.epilogue: Lucius is no fool: he knows who sent you. He takes you down to the cellar anyway. Behind the barrels is a thin, trembling boy and, on a cask, a fat ledger. "My nephew Gaius, a deserter. And that's the book the Widow wants. Now you decide what to tell her."
lucius_1_underworld.intro: The Widow slides a note across the back table. "Lucius, of the Ox, writes down everything that happens on the Appia. He's been writing for thirty years. Go have a wine with him and tell me what you see."
lucius_1_underworld.journal: The Widow sent me to look at the Ox's cellar. Lucius showed it to me himself: a deserter nephew and the book half of Rome wants. He chose me as a witness, not a spy.
lucius_1_underworld.lore: The Widow wants to know what Lucius keeps in the cellar of the Ox.
lucius_1_underworld.package: A note from the Widow, folded in four
lucius_1_underworld.title: Chapter I · An old debt
lucius_1_varus.epilogue: Lucius pours for you on the house and takes you down to the cellar. Behind the barrels is a thin, trembling boy and, on a cask, a fat ledger. "My nephew Gaius, deserter from the Tenth. And half the Appia is in that book. Varus says you know how to keep quiet. I hope so."
lucius_1_varus.intro: Varus takes you aside. "Lucius, of the Ox, was a network way station before you were born. He asked me for a courier he can trust. I told him I had one." He says no more. With Varus, that's already praise.
lucius_1_varus.journal: Varus sent me to the Ox. Lucius showed me his cellar: a deserter nephew and a book with half the Appia inside. Varus trusts me with this. Lucius doesn't, yet.
lucius_1_varus.lore: Lucius, an old friend of Varus, asks for you at the Ox Tavern.
lucius_1_varus.package: A greeting from Varus, by word of mouth
lucius_1_varus.title: Chapter I · An old debt
lucius_2.epilogue: Sexto reads the letter twice and burns it in the brazier. "Tell Lucius he has until the Kalends. After that, it's not my call." When you get back to the Ox, Lucius already has another job: the book has to leave Rome this very week.
lucius_2.intro: The Tenth is searching the taverns for Gaius. Lucius writes a letter to Sexto, the centurion, who owes him his life from an old night. "I'm not asking forgiveness for the boy. I'm asking for time."
lucius_2.journal: I took Lucius's letter to the camp. Sexto gave Gaius time, not forgiveness. And now the book has to leave Rome by the Appia.
lucius_2.lore: The legion is hunting Gaius. Lucius writes to an old friend in the camp.
lucius_2.package: A letter from Lucius to the centurion Sexto
lucius_2.title: Chapter II · Gaius, the deserter
lucius_3.epilogue: That night in Aricia you don't sleep. Two hundred names, and behind each one a family. You've chosen what to do with them. Tomorrow the Appia will start to find out.
lucius_3.intro: Lucius gives you the book wrapped in leather and an address in Aricia: his sister Livia's house. "Don't open it," he says. You both know you will.
lucius_3.journal: I opened Lucius's book in Aricia. It wasn't accounts: it was a list of two hundred inns hiding what the legion is looking for. I've already chosen what to do with it.
lucius_3.lore: Lucius's book has to reach Aricia without anyone reading it.
lucius_3.title: Chapter III · The Appia list
lucius_4_book.epilogue: You reach Forum Appii smelling of smoke, the book intact. Now you know what it's worth: enough to burn inns. The Widow sends word from Rome: "Bring it to the She-Wolf. I have buyers."
lucius_4_book.intro: With the book strapped under your tunic, you head for Forum Appii to see what it's worth. There's smoke on the road: someone is burning the inns on the list. And that someone knows you carry the whole list.
lucius_4_book.journal: They burned inns on the Appia looking for the book I'm carrying. I protected it. Now I know what it's worth, and so does the Widow.
lucius_4_book.lore: Inns from the list are burning, and whoever's burning them wants the book you carry.
lucius_4_book.package: The book, strapped to your body
lucius_4_book.title: Chapter IV · The Appia burns
lucius_4_family.epilogue: Livia's house greets the dawn intact. There's smoke from others on the road, but not this one. Livia gives you bread for the road and a message for her brother: "Tell him to stop writing things down." Lucius will laugh, and then he'll cry.
lucius_4_family.intro: The news reaches the Ox: inns on the Appia are burning, and all of them are in the book. Lucius doesn't shout; his face goes gray. "Livia." You're out the door before he finishes the name.
lucius_4_family.journal: I reached Livia's house in time. Other inns on the list burned. Lucius's family is still standing, and the book is still hidden in a cold oven.
lucius_4_family.lore: Inns from the list are burning. Livia's could be next.
lucius_4_family.package: A warning from Lucius for Livia
lucius_4_family.title: Chapter IV · The Appia burns
lucius_4_legion.epilogue: By day's end the column has a name: Gaius's centurion, the one selling the grain, is wiping out those who could accuse him. Sexto tucks the book into his saddlebag. "Now it's the legion's business. And yours is the Ox: Lucius is waiting."
lucius_4_legion.intro: Sexto waits for you on the road with half a century. But on the way to Forum Appii there's smoke: someone is burning the inns in the book before the legion can read it.
lucius_4_legion.journal: The inns burning were the ones that could accuse Gaius's centurion. Sexto has the book and the name. Lucius doesn't know yet who I gave it to.
lucius_4_legion.lore: Inns from the list are burning. Sexto wants the arsonist before the book.
lucius_4_legion.package: The book, to hand over on the road
lucius_4_legion.title: Chapter IV · The Appia burns
lucius_5_book.epilogue: The book no longer belongs to Lucius, nor entirely to you. It belongs to the Subura, which pays and remembers. The Widow opens her night market to you: maps, names and roads that appear in no register.
lucius_5_book.intro: The Widow has gathered four buyers at the back table. First, you stop at the Ox: Lucius deserves to know what you did with what he wrote.
lucius_5_book.journal: Lucius's book ended up on the Widow's table. Lucius poured me the last jug anyway. In the Subura I now have an open account at the night market.
lucius_5_book.lore: Four buyers await the book at the Golden She-Wolf.
lucius_5_book.title: Chapter V · The Ox
lucius_5_family.epilogue: The Ox wakes with a new sign over the door: the same seal the network's way stations use. Every time you pass along the Appia, there's a bed, a soup and someone looking after your legs. Lucius says it's the least he can do. It's quite a lot.
lucius_5_family.intro: Twelve tavern keepers from the Appia travel to Rome in secret to meet at the Ox. You go ahead, collecting their letters at each inn, and then take a seat at the table with them.
lucius_5_family.journal: The Ox is a network way station. The Appia's tavern keepers watch our roads and we watch them. Lucius wrote the book to protect his family, and in the end the family grew.
lucius_5_family.lore: The tavern keepers on the list gather at the Ox to decide what to do.
lucius_5_family.title: Chapter V · The Ox
lucius_5_legion.epilogue: Lucius reads Gaius's pardon and says nothing about his book. He sets out two jugs, then a third for Gaius, who walks in wearing the tunic of the Tenth. The Appia is still dangerous. But now you have a safe-conduct to cross it with the legion.
lucius_5_legion.intro: Sexto delivered: the thieving centurion is in chains and Gaius returns to his cohort. It falls to you to carry the pardon to the Ox and tell Lucius who you gave his book to.
lucius_5_legion.journal: Gaius is back in the Tenth and the thieving centurion is in chains. I gave Lucius's book to the legion. Two hundred names for one. Now I carry military mail along the Appia.
lucius_5_legion.lore: Sexto kept the deal. Now Lucius has to hear it.
lucius_5_legion.package: Gaius's pardon, under the seal of the Tenth
lucius_5_legion.title: Chapter V · The Ox
npc.atia.role: priestess of the temple of Mercury
opt_accept_ring.fail: Your bow comes out deeper than dignity allows and the slave smiles with the superiority of a senator's slave, which is the worst kind. Ring accepted, style surrendered. Varus needn't hear the details.
opt_accept_ring.journal: Petro gave me a ring with a raven. Varus says patrician favors are hooks. Hooks pull fish out of the water too.
opt_accept_ring.partial: You accept with the exact bow Varus taught you for patricians: respect without submission. The slave nods slightly, as if approving the technique. The ring weighs little. The favor it stands for, we'll see.
opt_accept_ring.success: The ring fits perfectly, which is unsettling: someone found out even the size of your fingers. "The Senator says one raven always knows another," the slave recites. Ally or marked man — in Rome, the difference is nuance.
opt_accept_ring.text: You accept the ring with a measured bow
opt_aqueduct_channel.fail: Halfway through, they open the sluice to test the repair. You burst out the first grate soaked, chased by a jet of water and the whole crew's laughter.
opt_aqueduct_channel.partial: The channel is dry but not clean: green mud, indignant toads and a ceiling lower than promised. You come out with a bumped head and the package intact.
opt_aqueduct_channel.success: You slip in through the inspection hatch and run crouched along the empty channel, light falling through the grates. You come out past the works before the foreman finishes shouting.
opt_aqueduct_channel.text: You cross through the aqueduct's dry channel
opt_aqueduct_curator.fail: The engineer is asleep under an awning and his assistant won't dare wake him. When he finally opens one eye, he says no and goes back to sleep.
opt_aqueduct_curator.partial: The engineer lets you through, but first makes you hold the groma while he takes a measurement. It takes longer than planned; at least now you know what a groma is.
opt_aqueduct_curator.success: The engineer is a thin Greek who loves talking gradients. You sit through three sentences on water levels and in return he opens a walkway only the inspectors use.
opt_aqueduct_curator.text: You look for the water commissioner's engineer
opt_aqueduct_wait.fail: Just as they wave you on, a pulley gives and everyone runs to hold the arch. You end up hauling a rope with twenty slaves and an engineer who won't stop cursing Vitruvius.
opt_aqueduct_wait.partial: They let you through when the day's last stone is down, and not before. You reach the other side white with lime, like a statue out for a stroll.
opt_aqueduct_wait.success: The foreman finishes counting blocks, looks you up and down and has the oxen moved. "Rome's water can wait for a courier. For a bit." You pass through the dust with his blessing.
opt_aqueduct_wait.text: You wait for the foreman to clear a way
opt_ask_price.fail: The question offends her one degree — one exact, measured, teaching degree. "At my table you don't ask the price: you trust or you leave." You stay. You drink. That was the lesson.
opt_ask_price.partial: "Cost, cost..." — the Widow swirls her cup — "let's say the back tables have memories." It's not an answer and it's every answer. You toast with your eyes open, which is what she wanted to teach you.
opt_ask_price.success: The Widow looks at you with professional delight. "Ah, you learn fast. This cup is free; the third will cost you a favor; the tenth, one of your secrets. Drink knowing." She's the first person in weeks to tell you the whole truth. You toast gladly.
opt_ask_price.text: "Before we toast: what will this cup cost me?"
opt_auction_keep.fail: The legion man tries to snatch the ledger right at the table. The Widow has two giants throw him into the street. The ledger is still in your satchel; your calm, less so.
opt_auction_keep.partial: You show them the ledger and they leave, but Petro's agent looks at you in a way you don't like. Owning a book like this means owning patient enemies.
opt_auction_keep.success: You open the ledger, show them their names are in it and close it again. "It's not for sale. It's in my satchel." They leave pale. The Widow claps slowly. Now they all owe you silence, and silence charges interest.
opt_auction_keep.text: You sell nothing: you show them you have it
opt_auction_pages.fail: The buyers agree in low voices and drop their prices together. You end up selling cheap. The Widow looks at you with professional pity: "Next time, don't let them talk to each other."
opt_auction_pages.partial: It works halfway: the legion man realizes you sold him worthless pages and storms off. The rest sell well. Half a victory, in gold.
opt_auction_pages.success: You separate the pages and auction them one at a time. Petro buys his rivals'; the merchant, the harbor's; the scribe, the senators'. The Widow keeps a commission and a smile. You made more than with the whole ledger.
opt_auction_pages.text: You sell it page by page to the highest bidder
opt_auction_widow.fail: The Widow takes the ledger and pays you with a future favor instead of gold. Not what you wanted, but you don't argue payment terms with the Widow.
opt_auction_widow.journal: I sold Lucius's ledger to the Widow. The other buyers left empty-handed, with my face in their memory.
opt_auction_widow.partial: The Widow pays, but less than you hoped: "Who sells fast doesn't sell dear." The buyers leave muttering. The ledger has changed hands.
opt_auction_widow.success: You set the ledger in front of the Widow, not in the middle of the table. The four buyers understand and get up. The Widow pays in gold and pours you the back-room wine. "Now the whole Appia owes me something. And you're the one who brought it."
opt_auction_widow.text: You sell it whole to the Widow
opt_authority.fail: The doorman calls the steward. You lose time explaining.
opt_authority.partial: The doorman hesitates, then yields. Your tone did the trick.
opt_authority.success: The doorman wants no trouble. He lets you in at once.
opt_authority.text: "This comes straight from the Senate's network. Care to explain the delay to the Senator?"
opt_barge_drive.fail: The mule doesn't recognize your authority and sits down. The boatman wakes, offended, and retakes the reins with vengeful slowness.
opt_barge_drive.journal: I crossed the Marshes driving the barge mule myself. The boatman snored and the passengers paid for my wine.
opt_barge_drive.partial: The mule pulls well, but wants to eat at every bend. You lurch forward, with passengers giving advice nobody asked for.
opt_barge_drive.success: You talk the boatman into resting and take the reins. The mule, happy with someone sober, trots. The passengers applaud you on the bank and buy you a drink.
opt_barge_drive.text: You take the mule's reins yourself
opt_barge_ride.fail: The boatman ties up the mule and goes to sleep on the bank. At dawn a passenger throws a bucket of water on him and you finally set off. You arrive bitten even on your eyelids.
opt_barge_ride.partial: The boatman falls asleep halfway and the mule stops to graze. You lose a long hour stuck in the canal, fighting mosquitoes with your cloak.
opt_barge_ride.success: The barge glides through the dark while frogs sing and mosquitoes dine. At dawn you're across the Marshes, bitten but rested.
opt_barge_ride.text: You board the barge and endure it
opt_barge_walk.fail: You stray onto a sunken stretch of causeway and end up mud to the knees. The barge passes you with the boatman singing.
opt_barge_walk.partial: The causeway is fine, but the marsh fog rises and you have to slow down. You arrive at dawn, damp to the bone.
opt_barge_walk.success: You walk the Appia by night, on dry stone, the canal beside you. The mosquitoes follow but can't catch you. You arrive before the barge.
opt_bees_run.fail: The swarm chases you half a mile. You dive into a stream to shake it off and climb out wet, stung and short some dignity.
opt_bees_run.partial: You dash through and come out with four stings and a buzzing in your ears that lasts an hour. But you got through.
opt_bees_run.success: You cover your head with your cloak and run as if a praetor were after you. The bees take a while to work out what happened. By then you're far away.
opt_bees_run.text: You charge through the swarm at full speed
opt_bees_smoke.fail: The smoke calms the bees and spooks the horses of an approaching cart. You spend a good while gathering hives and calming a carter.
opt_bees_smoke.journal: I helped gather hives with green-grass smoke. They paid me in honey and a single sting.
opt_bees_smoke.partial: The smoke works, but the wind shifts and blows it in your face. You weep, cough and help. In the end the beekeeper gives you honey and a rag for your eyes.
opt_bees_smoke.success: You light damp grass and the smoke tames the swarm. Together you right the hives and the queen goes home. The beekeeper fills a jar with thyme honey for you.
opt_bees_smoke.text: You make smoke and help the beekeeper
opt_bees_wait.fail: A scout bee finds your hiding place and tells the others. You end up waiting in an irrigation ditch, water up to your neck.
opt_bees_wait.partial: The bees half calm down. You pass very slowly, not breathing, and just one stings your ear. Enough for the ear to remind you.
opt_bees_wait.success: You sit in the shade fifty paces off. At dusk the bees cluster on a branch and the road is clear. The beekeeper gives you a honeycomb for your patience.
opt_bees_wait.text: You wait far off for them to calm
opt_bluff_delivered.fail: The one in the middle smiles wider: "Then we don't need you in one piece." You dodge the first grab by a miracle and the chase is brutal. You reach Petro's with your tunic torn and the message intact. Tell the miracle later: now, deliver.
opt_bluff_delivered.partial: They hesitate. "Search him." They pat you down for weapons and scrolls — the copy is in your boot, where no one in a hurry looks. They release you with a shove and a routine threat. You walk unhurried to the corner. At the corner, you run.
opt_bluff_delivered.success: You say it with the exact boredom of someone already paid. The three trade looks: if it's true, killing you is pointless. The middle one curses in refined Greek and they go to report failure. Lying well is a martial art.
opt_bluff_delivered.text: "You're late. Petro read it all an hour ago."
opt_buyer_confess.fail: He laughs: "Tell him. Varus won't believe you." The doubt stays lodged in you. You write to Varus anyway, and days pass with no reply. Varus's silence weighs more than the blackmail.
opt_buyer_confess.journal: The man who bought a peek tried to blackmail me. I told him the Guild would hear it from me. His business fell through.
opt_buyer_confess.partial: He leaves, but not before promising someone else will hear of it. You write to Varus that same night. For now, neither side has made a move.
opt_buyer_confess.success: You tell him you'll write to Varus tonight, all of it, his face included. The blackmail falls apart in his mouth. He leaves without finishing his bread. You do write to Varus, and the reply comes dry: "Well done. Late, but well done."
opt_buyer_confess.text: You tell him you'll tell Varus yourself
opt_buyer_pay.fail: You pay, and instead of leaving he orders another jug on your tab and stays to tell you his life story. Three hours of a likable blackmailer. You paid for that too.
opt_buyer_pay.partial: You pay; he wants more. You pay a bit more and he goes. He'll be back, just not today.
opt_buyer_pay.success: You hand him a purse that hurts. He takes it, swears by every god he doesn't know you and leaves. The proverb holds: cheap today, dear later. Now you know how much dear is.
opt_buyer_turn.fail: He smells the lie at once. "I thought you were subtler." He leaves without blackmailing you, but taking notes. Now you have a patient enemy.
opt_buyer_turn.partial: The lie half works: he has doubts, but goes off to check. You've bought a few days of peace. When he finds out, you'd better be in another province.
opt_buyer_turn.success: You whisper that the real package is going up the Flaminia in another satchel, and you're the decoy. He believes you, because he wants to. Tomorrow he'll be fifty miles off, chasing a courier who doesn't exist.
opt_buyer_turn.text: You sell him a false lead and send him far away
opt_call_guards.fail: The shout only makes the whole market stare at you. The boy is a memory, and the guards, an interrogation.
opt_call_guards.partial: The guards are too late for the boy but in time for the lecture: half an hour of questions to return a purse that turned up empty.
opt_call_guards.success: Two guards nab him at the corner. They return your purse in full. The boy watches you as they take him away. The law is the law, you tell yourself. The look doesn't leave.
opt_call_guards.text: "Stop, thief!" — let the guards catch him
opt_calm_dog.fail: The dog barks louder. You end up waiting anyway.
opt_calm_dog.partial: The dog half settles. The guard arrives just in time.
opt_calm_dog.success: The dog sniffs you and settles. The guard appears, surprised.
opt_calm_dog.text: You approach slowly and calm the dog
opt_carry_him.fail: Halfway there, his own network's cart shows up: they thank you curtly and take him. Two hours of effort for a lesson in humility.
opt_carry_him.partial: You carry him in stretches, resting every thousand paces. You arrive late but you arrive, and his gratitude weighs less than he does, luckily.
opt_carry_him.success: A league and a half with a messenger on your shoulder who won't stop apologizing. You both arrive, you both deliver. In the tavern that night, the story already has music.
opt_carry_him.text: No letter, no excuses: you carry him to the town
opt_cellar_distract.fail: The mule driver isn't in the mood to fight and apologizes to you instead. The argument dies before it's born. The men laugh, pay and leave, eyeing the trapdoor one last time.
opt_cellar_distract.partial: The argument half works: one man watches the fight and the other keeps watching the cellar. Lucius uses the moment to close the trapdoor and set a barrel on it. They leave with their suspicion intact.
opt_cellar_distract.success: You spill wine on a big mule driver and the argument grows until it fills the room. The two men watch the show and lose sight of the trapdoor. When it all calms down, they leave having seen nothing.
opt_cellar_distract.text: You start an argument at the other end
opt_cellar_follow.fail: At the second corner one of them turns and looks you in the eye. You play drunk, stumble into a wall and they leave you behind laughing. They bought it. This time.
opt_cellar_follow.journal: I followed the men sniffing around the Ox. Someone on the Appia wants Lucius's ledger as badly as he wants to hide it.
opt_cellar_follow.partial: You follow them to the Porta Capena and lose them among the carts there. You know where they come from: the Appia. For Lucius, that's enough to worry.
opt_cellar_follow.success: You follow them through three alleys to an inn by the Porta Capena, where they report to a man with a bronze ring. You don't know his name, but now you know his face. Lucius goes gray when you describe it.
opt_cellar_follow.text: You follow them out to see who sent them
opt_cellar_sit.fail: You sit, but one of them sits across from you and talks about nothing for an eternity. He doesn't go down to the cellar, but he leaves knowing you're guarding something.
opt_cellar_sit.partial: You sit and eat slowly, without looking at them. They wait, you wait. Whoever has more patience wins, and you have a whole dinner ahead of you.
opt_cellar_sit.success: You drag a bench over, sit on the trapdoor and order dinner. To look below they'd have to move you, and moving you would make noise. They pay and leave. Lucius serves you a double portion.
opt_cellar_sit.text: You sit on the trapdoor as if nothing's wrong
opt_census_crowd.fail: The scribe counts twelve where there were eleven. The family swears they don't know you, the goat too. You end up declaring everything, branded a gatecrasher.
opt_census_crowd.partial: You get through with the family, but the mother adopts you for two milestones and makes you carry a toddler who won't stop pulling your hair.
opt_census_crowd.success: A family of eleven bustles through with hens and a goat. You join as the quiet cousin. The scribe counts eleven, writes eleven, and you're already through.
opt_census_crowd.text: You blend in with a large family
opt_census_official.fail: The scribe is a purist: "official service has a father and tribe too." He records you in full, with exemplary slowness, so you'll learn.
opt_census_official.partial: The scribe lets you through but records you anyway, in a separate column marked "in a hurry." You don't know what being in that column means.
opt_census_official.success: You point to the package seal and say "courier on service" in the voice of someone who's said it a thousand times. The scribe doesn't even look up: he waves you through.
opt_census_official.text: You show you're traveling on official service
opt_census_queue.fail: When your turn comes, the tablet runs out of wax. They send for more. The slave returns, the light fails, and the scribe decides the rest of the census is tomorrow.
opt_census_queue.partial: The scribe wants your grandfather's name and you're not sure. You make one up together. You leave registered, with a new ancestor.
opt_census_queue.success: You declare name, father, tribe and a list of property that fits on one line. The scribe smiles for the first time all day: someone who doesn't lie. He sends you off with a stamp on the tablet.
opt_charcoal_fugitive.fail: He knows you and panics: he thinks there's a patrol behind you. It takes a good while to convince him you're alone. At last he shakes your hand, still trembling.
opt_charcoal_fugitive.journal: The deserter I didn't turn in burns charcoal in the hills. He has another name and the same eyes.
opt_charcoal_fugitive.partial: He knows you and signals you to follow without speaking. The path is good but slow; he can't leave the kiln for long.
opt_charcoal_fugitive.success: It's the deserter from the rocks. He has a new name now and soot up to his eyebrows. He knows you, talks to the others, and they take you by a shortcut no patrol knows.
opt_charcoal_greet.fail: They don't like your accent. They send you around the outside of the forest, on a nettle-choked path nobody uses for good reason.
opt_charcoal_greet.partial: They let you through, but first make you wait until a kiln finishes burning, in case you're a spy for the forest's owners.
opt_charcoal_greet.success: You greet them and say where you're from and where you're going. The burner spits, nods and lets you through. A younger one walks you to the forest's edge so you don't get lost in the smoke.
opt_charcoal_greet.text: You greet them and ask leave to pass
opt_charcoal_push.fail: The man won't move and neither will you. It ends in shoving, with you sitting on warm charcoal. They let you pass afterward, since you've given them their fun.
opt_charcoal_push.partial: You get through, but the smoke makes you weep and cough like an old bellows. The burners laugh. You leave the forest as black as they are.
opt_charcoal_push.success: You walk straight on, eyes neither lowered nor raised. The man on the path steps aside. Charcoal burners respect those who ask for nothing.
opt_charcoal_sneak.fail: One of the burners' dogs finds you in the stream and escorts you, barking, all the way to the camp. You arrive escorted and suspect.
opt_charcoal_sneak.partial: The stream loops farther than you thought, and for one stretch you have to wade in. You come out wet, but unseen.
opt_charcoal_sneak.success: You drop down to the stream and follow the water through the ferns. The smoke hides you better than any shadow. You leave the forest without anyone knowing you were there.
opt_charcoal_sneak.text: You skirt the camp along the stream
opt_charm.fail: Lucius won't budge. You end up showing the seal anyway.
opt_charm.partial: Lucius accepts, with reservations. Next time, he says, bring better credentials.
opt_charm.success: The urgency in your voice convinces Lucius. He takes the message.
opt_charm.text: You tell him the message is urgent and confidential
opt_chase.fail: The boy knows every crack in the district and you know none. You end up in a dead end, no purse, two neighbor women laughing.
opt_chase.partial: You lose him in the maze, but the purse turns up dropped on a corner: he took a few coins and left the rest. A thief in a hurry, not in hate.
opt_chase.success: You catch him in three blocks: the trade outruns hunger. You get the purse back. The boy waits for a blow that never comes. "Run the other way next time," you tell him.
opt_chase.text: You chase him through the alleys
opt_child_ask.fail: You ask table to table with no luck, and the whole inn ends up eyeing you as a suspect of something. You leave with no answers and the time lost.
opt_child_ask.partial: No one at the inn knows her, but the innkeeper offers to look after her until someone comes. You leave trusting the word of a kind stranger.
opt_child_ask.success: The innkeeper knows half the district: he recognizes the name the girl keeps saying and sends a boy for her uncle. Before your wine goes cold, they're taking her home.
opt_child_ask.text: You ask about her family at the nearest inn
opt_child_leave.fail: The road you pointed out has a fork you forgot to mention. You only learn of it at the next village, when someone asks about a lost girl.
opt_child_leave.journal: I pointed a lost girl down a road and kept going. The deadline won. I don't know if I did right.
opt_child_leave.partial: You point the way, and a hundred paces on you hear her still crying in the same spot, afraid to walk alone. You hesitate, but go on.
opt_child_leave.success: You point out the straight road to the village and watch her go, unsure but determined. You continue your route with a barely uneasy conscience.
opt_child_leave.text: You point her the way and hurry on
opt_child_walk.fail: It gets late and it's the wrong village: no one there knows her. You retrace your steps with the girl asleep in your arms and the sun already low.
opt_child_walk.journal: I took a lost girl to the village. I arrived late at my destination. It was still the right thing.
opt_child_walk.partial: The village is farther than you thought and the girl tires halfway. She rides the last blocks on your shoulders, lighter than the package.
opt_child_walk.success: You walk together to the village, her telling you about every flower on the way. In the square, a woman shouts her name and runs. "Thank you, messenger" isn't enough, but she says it anyway.
opt_child_walk.text: You take her by the hand to the nearest village
opt_claudius_first.fail: Claudius's steward makes you wait an hour out of pure spite, and you reach Petro's after midnight. Both read, both went pale, both will pay. The Widow will forgive the delay. Your feet won't.
opt_claudius_first.partial: Claudius holds you with questions you won't answer; you leave the villa with a cold neck. Petro takes his with a chess player's calm. "Tell your mistress I accept the terms." An odd day in a trade of odd days.
opt_claudius_first.success: Claudius reads, and his hands, trained not to shake, shake. He searches your face and finds the professional blankness the Widow taught you. At Petro's, by contrast: a short laugh, an "it was only a matter of time," and he even offers you water. Two senators, two styles of losing.
opt_claudius_first.text: Claudius first — the most dangerous, better early
opt_climb_ivy.fail: The ivy gives way under you and the crash wakes the dogs. You end up explaining the note surrounded by three mastiffs and a humorless guard. Claudius will have to come down and rescue you.
opt_climb_ivy.partial: You climb well until the ivy decides to retire halfway up. The landing in the rosebush lacks dignity, but no one saw. Almost no one: a peacock eyes you with contempt.
opt_climb_ivy.success: The ivy holds and so do you. You drop into the inner garden without a sound, just as Claudius steps out for air. "Punctual, and over the wall," he murmurs, genuinely impressed. "Better than I was told."
opt_climb_ivy.text: You climb the ivy on the west wall
opt_cohort_guess.fail: You chose wrong: the big one is empty, and that night smoke rises from another. Sextus says nothing. He needn't.
opt_cohort_guess.partial: It's the right inn, but they arrive late: the stable is already burning. They catch one of the three. One is enough to start.
opt_cohort_guess.success: The biggest, the one that pays most and hides most. They arrive at nightfall and find three men with oil in the stable. They take them without a single wound. Sextus eyes you sideways: "You think like a thief." Coming from him, it's praise.
opt_cohort_guess.text: You pick the biggest inn on the stretch
opt_cohort_read.fail: You spend an hour reading and Sextus loses patience with Lucius's handwriting. "He writes like a drunk." You close the ledger with nothing clear. The column rides out blind.
opt_cohort_read.journal: I read the ledger with Sextus. The inns that burn are the ones that stopped paying Gaius's centurion. The grain thief is erasing his witnesses.
opt_cohort_read.partial: You half find the pattern: the burned inns made payments to the same officer, but the name is smudged. Sextus has a suspicion. He needs more.
opt_cohort_read.success: Sitting on a rock, you read the two hundred lines together. The burning ones have something in common: they all paid the same centurion, and they all stopped paying. Gaius's. Sextus shuts the ledger with a sharp slap. Now he knows who to look for.
opt_cohort_read.text: You read the ledger with him to find the pattern
opt_cohort_scout.fail: You run so hard you arrive exhausted and wrong: the inn you scouted is quiet. When you get back, Sextus has already left in another direction. You catch up breathless and with no news.
opt_cohort_scout.partial: You find the arsonists, but they see you too. They flee before the column arrives. They won't be back to this inn.
opt_cohort_scout.success: You run ahead along the road and at the second inn you see horses tied out back. You return to warn them before the column finishes forming up. They catch them with lit torches in hand.
opt_cohort_scout.text: You go ahead alone to scout
opt_compitalia_offering.fail: Your bread falls off the altar and a dog runs off with it. People take it as an omen and argue a long while whether to let you pass or bathe you in wine to cleanse you.
