opt_compitalia_offering.partial: The offering pleases, but the magister also wants you to say your name to the Lares out loud. You say it, people clap, you turn red.
opt_compitalia_offering.success: You leave bread and a coin on the altar with the respect the feast demands. The neighborhood magister nods approval and opens a gap in the crowd for you.
opt_compitalia_offering.text: You leave an offering and pass
opt_compitalia_slip.fail: They grab your cloak halfway across. "No toast, you buy a round!" You buy a round for half the neighborhood and leave with a lighter purse.
opt_compitalia_slip.partial: You get by, but an old woman sees you and shouts that you'll have bad luck on the road. You don't believe in such things. For a good while, you watch your step.
opt_compitalia_slip.success: While everyone sings, you slip behind the altar, head down. Nobody notices someone passed without toasting. The Lares, if they noticed, said nothing.
opt_compitalia_slip.text: You slip behind the altar without toasting
opt_compitalia_toast.fail: The wine was watered, but the third cup not so much. You wake in the altar's shade with a wool doll in your hand and no idea how long it's been.
opt_compitalia_toast.partial: One toast leads to another and the dance to a ring that never ends. You break free of the ring with the sun lower than you'd like.
opt_compitalia_toast.success: You toast the Lares of the crossroads, those of the road and those of an insistent grandmother. They tie a ribbon to your bag "so the package arrives." You leave light and blessed.
opt_compitalia_toast.text: You toast with the neighbors and dance a little
opt_confident.fail: The guard detains you for not answering. Awkward.
opt_confident.partial: It almost works. The guard stops you, then lets you pass on seeing the official seal.
opt_confident.success: Your purposeful stride makes the guard assume you're authorized.
opt_confront_shadow.fail: The skinny one was the bait: the big one grabs you from behind. They rough you up a little, but a night watchman whistles in the distance and they vanish. You reach the temple bruised and with more questions.
opt_confront_shadow.partial: The skinny one slips your grip but loses a sandal and his pride. Both disappear. You're left with the sandal and a suspicion they'll be back another day with friends.
opt_confront_shadow.success: You wait where the alley narrows and pin him to the wall before he can breathe. "Tell whoever pays you that nobody follows Claudius's courier." He runs. So does the other one. Message delivered — and this one was free.
opt_confront_shadow.text: You corner the skinny one in an alley
opt_contacts.fail: "Anyone can flash an old seal," says the centurion. The search that follows is twice as long for your trying.
opt_contacts.partial: The seal impresses the rank-and-file, but the centurion wants a second look. In the end it works, though you've earned a gaze that doesn't forget faces.
opt_contacts.success: The centurion looks at the seal, then at you, and something in his posture changes. "Free passage for the Senate's post." No one touches your bag.
opt_contacts.text: You show a Senate seal you know
opt_contraband_again.fail: At the harbor checkpoint they look at your bag twice. You get through, heart in your mouth, and the merchant pays you less because "you were slow getting out." Smuggling has its bad days too.
opt_contraband_again.journal: I carried a load for the dock merchant again. Twice is no longer a mistake: it's a trade.
opt_contraband_again.partial: The load is heavier than promised and slows you down. You deliver it anyway and get half for the delay. The merchant says the next one will be lighter.
opt_contraband_again.success: The load is a small leather parcel that fits in your bag without a bulge. You deliver it at a roadside tavern, get paid, and nobody asks. The merchant already counts you as one of his.
opt_contraband_price.fail: He calls it extortion and looks for another courier, a cheaper one, right in front of you. You're left with no load and no price. Some deals close by asking too much.
opt_contraband_price.partial: He offers half again as much and you accept. You carry it without trouble. It's clear what's worth paying for isn't the load: it's that nobody knows.
opt_contraband_price.success: You explain the first time was cheap for being the first. He laughs, but pays double. You carry the load and get paid like a professional. On the dock, they start saying your name with respect.
opt_contraband_price.text: You ask double for your silence
opt_contraband_refuse.fail: He takes offense and loudly reminds you, in front of a stevedore, of the last load. Now one more person knows. You leave red-faced.
opt_contraband_refuse.partial: He insists twice and on the third shrugs. He's left suspecting you might report him. You leave quickly.
opt_contraband_refuse.success: He looks at you without anger, calculating. "You're not who you were." He says it like a compliment. You leave the dock with no extra load and no new debts.
opt_contraband_refuse.text: You say no, and tell him not to call you again
opt_counterfeit_accept.fail: At the next way station you bite them before paying and the tavern keeper sees. "Bad coin in my house?" Explaining takes a long while and double the bill.
opt_counterfeit_accept.partial: You pocket them, but the weight of knowing comes along. At the next way station you pay with good coin and the fakes stay in your purse, like stones.
opt_counterfeit_accept.success: You pocket the coins without a word. Later you hand them to a tavern keeper who doesn't look at them either. The world is a chain of fake denarii and you're already out of it.
opt_counterfeit_accept.text: You pocket them and move on
opt_counterfeit_aedile.fail: The aedile is the changer's cousin. He lectures you on false accusations and lets you go late and without your change.
opt_counterfeit_aedile.partial: The aedile confiscates the coins, yours too, as evidence. You get half back. Justice, but pricey.
opt_counterfeit_aedile.success: The aedile arrives, bites a coin and grimaces. The changer ends up without a stall and you with your change in good coin. Some locals applaud you quietly.
opt_counterfeit_quiet.fail: The changer pretends not to understand and asks you to step away from his stall. Two big men appear behind him. You step away with the fake coins.
opt_counterfeit_quiet.partial: The changer swaps the coins, but looks at you like someone who knows too much. You'll see his face again, somewhere.
opt_counterfeit_quiet.success: You lean in and tell him, very softly, which alley in Rome those coins come from. The changer goes pale, swaps everything for good silver and adds a denarius of apology.
opt_counterfeit_quiet.text: You ask for proper change, quietly
opt_debt_cold.fail: Lucius frowns: "Don't bring your fights with Varus to my bar." He listens anyway, but with the door open in case you have to leave. Trust will cost a bit more.
opt_debt_cold.journal: I told Lucius that Varus had turned his back on me. He gave me a key to the Ox. Some doors open when others close.
opt_debt_cold.partial: Lucius says nothing about Varus, but pours you another cup. Some silences are solidarity. You stay a while longer than you need to.
opt_debt_cold.success: Lucius nods slowly: he knew Varus before the network. "Varus is hard on those who leave because many left him." He sets a key on the bar. "This one's for the back room. In case you need a place."
opt_debt_cold.text: "Varus looks at me differently. I need a place."
opt_debt_listen.fail: Lucius talks and talks, and with so many detours never quite tells you what he wants. A customer interrupts and the talk breaks off. You're left with half a story and an unfinished wine.
opt_debt_listen.partial: You listen, but the story is long and circles back on itself. Lucius notices you eyeing the door and cuts it short: "I'll tell you the rest downstairs." You earned something; not everything.
opt_debt_listen.success: Lucius talks for an hour straight: about the network when he was young, the Appia way stations that were his, a ledger he never should have written. You listen. When he's done, he knows you won't sell him out. And to Lucius, that's already a contract.
opt_debt_listen.text: You let him talk to the end
opt_debt_price.fail: The tavern keeper doesn't care for haste. "We'll talk money when you know what you've got into." You're left with no price and the feeling you started on the wrong foot.
opt_debt_price.partial: Lucius quotes you low to see if you haggle. You haggle. You end on a number that pleases neither of you, which is how good deals close.
opt_debt_price.success: Lucius likes it: "That's how I talked at your age." He tells you the price, which is good, and the job, which is worse. A hidden nephew and a ledger. You accept before the jug is empty.
opt_debt_price.text: "Tell me what you want and the pay."
opt_debt_vetoed.fail: Lucius finds it funny, but doesn't quite believe you: he thinks Claudius sent you to spy. He has to see you work before he trusts you. You start from zero, but you start.
opt_debt_vetoed.journal: I told Lucius that Claudius shut his door on me. He laughed: says it's the best introduction on the Appia.
opt_debt_vetoed.partial: Lucius laughs, but also eyes you carefully: someone with Claudius against him brings trouble. He decides it's worth it. "You bring the trouble; I'll bring the wine."
opt_debt_vetoed.success: Lucius lets out a laugh that rattles the jugs. "A courier Claudius can't buy! That's worth more than a letter of recommendation." He pours you the good wine, the one he keeps under the bar.
opt_debt_vetoed.text: "Claudius doesn't give me work anymore. I'm free."
opt_decline_ride.fail: A league later, you pass the cart again... stopped by a patrol checking the tarp. You quicken your pace, eyes fixed on the horizon. Good call, better timing.
opt_decline_ride.partial: You walk on, watching the cart's dust recede. Slower, cleaner. The trade is also knowing how to say no.
opt_decline_ride.success: "My legs are my trade," you tell him, and the merchant laughs and tosses you an apple. Each to his own road and his own risks.
opt_decline_ride.text: You decline with a smile and walk on
opt_decline_ring.fail: Your refusal comes out blunter than planned and the slave takes offense on someone else's behalf, which is his job. With luck, Petro will take it as a soldier's rudeness, not an insult. Varus will have to smooth it over. Again.
opt_decline_ring.journal: I refused Petro's ring. The network doesn't charge for loyalty. Let the senators learn the difference.
opt_decline_ring.partial: The slave insists three times — refusing twice is courtesy, refusing three times is a stance. You hold the stance. He leaves confused. Patricians understand gold; a messenger's pride is beyond them.
opt_decline_ring.success: The slave blinks: nobody refuses Petro's gifts. "The Senator will find this... interesting." An hour later, a message from Varus: "Petro asks if all my men are like that. I told him the good ones are." Better than any ring.
opt_decline_ring.text: "I served the network, not the Senator. No debt."
opt_decoy_run.fail: The one in the middle doesn't even glance at the satchel: "He's carrying the scroll on him." You run anyway, faster than you've ever run, and the night saves you by a toga's hair. You reach Petro's by the back way, shaking.
opt_decoy_run.partial: The decoy half works: one goes for the satchel, two come for you. You lose them in the maze of the Subura, lungs on fire and sandals begging forgiveness.
opt_decoy_run.success: The satchel flies left with your flask and your bread; you fly right with what matters in your tunic. By the time they get the trick, you're a shadow three blocks away. The bread was good. Freedom, better.
opt_decoy_run.text: You throw your satchel one way, run the other
opt_deserter_avoid.fail: A patrolling legionary stops you two leagues on, asking if you saw anyone odd on the road. You lie badly, and it costs you a full search of your bag.
opt_deserter_avoid.partial: You walk on, but your heart pounds for a good while, waiting for patrol shouts that never come.
opt_deserter_avoid.success: You go on your way without turning your head. What you didn't see, you don't have to explain. The road stays quiet the rest of the afternoon.
opt_deserter_help.fail: He's barely gone when a patrol catches him in front of you. They question you too, just in case. The cloak, they say, "matches the description."
opt_deserter_help.journal: I helped a legion deserter escape. I hope it's worth it, for him and for me.
opt_deserter_help.partial: You give him the cloak, but he dithers so long at the detour you're nearly caught together. He goes at last, and you with your pulse still high.
opt_deserter_help.success: You toss him the old cloak and nod toward the woods. He vanishes without a thank-you, the only proper way to say it in his position. You go on, lighter by one cloak and one doubt.
opt_deserter_help.text: You give him your old cloak and point out a detour
opt_deserter_talk.fail: The boy panics mid-conversation and runs for the woods again. You're left empty-handed, feeling you lost an hour for nothing.
opt_deserter_talk.partial: You half convince him: he agrees to go, but changes his mind twice on the way. In the end you leave him with the centurion, nothing guaranteed.
opt_deserter_talk.success: You know a centurion who handles these things with more sense than punishment. You convince the boy to report there, not at just any post. It goes better than he expected.
opt_deserter_talk.text: You persuade him to turn himself in to an officer you know
opt_detour.success: The detour is longer, but you arrive without trouble.
opt_detour_b.fail: Halfway around you find the "next bridge" is just two planks with ambitions. You cross anyway, one plank at a time, praying in Latin.
opt_detour_b.partial: The next bridge exists, but it's packed with market carts. You cross at a walk among oxen and shouting.
opt_detour_b.success: Six hours of extra road, zero surprises. Sometimes the fastest messenger is the one who stays dry.
opt_detour_b.text: You go around to the next bridge
opt_dice_expose.fail: The cheat is quicker: when you pry his hand open, there's just a coin. The whole table glares at you. You leave after buying an apology round.
opt_dice_expose.partial: The loaded die turns up, but the cheat has friends. You leave through the window with a swollen eye and the satisfaction of being right.
opt_dice_expose.success: You squeeze his wrist and a third die drops from his sleeve. The whole table piles on him. You use the uproar to slip out, with the gratitude of five losers.
opt_dice_play.fail: His dice have opinions. You lose your stake and a bit more, and leave certain you were the evening's entertainment.
opt_dice_play.partial: You win one hand and lose another. You leave as you came, except now they know your name in a tavern where nobody gives theirs.
opt_dice_play.success: You bet small, win a little and quit while everyone demands a rematch. You've earned a seat at the table and a tip: one of the players knows a shortcut and tells you, laughing.
opt_dice_refuse.fail: A player who lost everything blames you for bringing bad luck by watching. The tavern keeper asks you to leave through the kitchen, among pots and an offended cat.
opt_dice_refuse.partial: You stay a while too long watching, because the game is hypnotic. You lose nothing but time and a bit of a messenger's dignity.
opt_dice_refuse.success: You eat with your back to the game and your purse between your knees. When you leave, the shouting goes on and none of those coins are yours. Nor are their problems.
opt_dice_refuse.text: You eat fast and accept nothing
opt_dice_viuda.fail: One of the players owes the Widow money and goes pale. He begs you not to say you saw him. You lose a while hearing why, in full detail.
opt_dice_viuda.partial: The name works, but the cheat wants to send the Widow his regards and dictates a long message. Now you carry two jobs, one unpaid.
opt_dice_viuda.success: The name lands on the table like a fourth die. The cheat pockets his and pours you wine. Before you go, he gives you a road tip worth more than everything in play.
opt_dice_viuda.text: You mention the Widow of the She-Wolf
opt_dismiss_omen.fail: A hundred paces past the crossroads, you trip on the most visible root on the whole road. From behind, the augur's voice: "The crows, messenger!" You don't deign to look.
opt_dismiss_omen.journal: I said no to an augur at the crossroads. In Rome, that gets talked about.
opt_dismiss_omen.partial: You go on without paying, but for the next league every bird's shadow makes you look up. The augur collects anyway, in his way.
opt_dismiss_omen.success: You walk on. No lightning falls, no crow attacks. Superstition is the Empire's only optional toll.
opt_dismiss_omen.text: "My deadlines don't understand crows." You walk on
opt_double_game.fail: He spots the fake at second glance. He gets up without a word, and that look tells you you've landed on the wrong list.
opt_double_game.partial: The trick half works: he suspects, pays half and leaves without a goodbye. The real post never left your tunic.
opt_double_game.success: You sell him smoke with a marble face: an olive price list with a prop seal. He pays, reads, nods like an expert and leaves. A work of art.
opt_double_game.text: You pretend to accept... and show him a fake letter
opt_double_sell.fail: Halfway through your improvised "edit," the agent smells the trick and cuts you off. He leaves without paying and with suspicions. Now Petro knows someone is selling... and that someone is creative. Better the Widow hears your version first.
opt_double_sell.partial: The double sale goes through, but the agent is less stupid than he looked: he pays half "pending verification." Still: two payments for one letter. You're starting to like Subura arithmetic.
opt_double_sell.success: You sell the agent a version with the right names and the wrong sums: true where it matters little, false where it matters most. You get paid twice for the same secret. When the Widow finds out — and she will — she'll applaud.
opt_double_sell.text: You hear the figure... and sell him an "edited" version
opt_drink_toast.fail: The toast goes clumsily: you clink too hard and the wine jumps. The Widow laughs — a real laugh, rare as summer rain. "Clumsy with cups, deft with secrets. I prefer that to the reverse." Approved anyway.
opt_drink_toast.journal: I toasted with the Widow at the back table. In the Subura I'm now "the night courier." Titles here aren't bought: they're drunk.
opt_drink_toast.partial: You toast trying to hide that the wine is spinning your head: the Widow pours strong to see how her partners hold up. You hold up. Barely, but you hold up. She notes everything, even that.
opt_drink_toast.success: The wine is better than anything you've ever drunk, which is also a message. "To those who know," the Widow repeats, "and to those who know how to keep quiet." The back table has a place for you now. Rome's nights just changed hands.
opt_drink_toast.text: You raise your cup: "To those who know."
opt_evade.fail: When you stop, the man comes over. He turns out to be a vendor looking for customers.
opt_evade.partial: The man sees you waiting but walks on anyway.
opt_evade.success: The man walks on by. Either it was nothing, or you lost him well.
opt_evade.text: You turn a corner and wait out of sight
opt_family_bread.fail: The mother is a little hurt that you won't stay. She gives you the bread anyway, but the goodbye is cool. Some gratitude asks for time, not just bread.
opt_family_bread.partial: They load you with so much bread you leave half at the next inn. There's enough to treat another courier. Having extra isn't so bad.
opt_family_bread.success: They give you bread, cheese and a wineskin you can't refuse. You eat as you walk. That night at the way station you have dinner while the other couriers pay for theirs.
opt_family_bread.text: You take bread and move on
opt_family_eat.fail: You eat too much, and the afternoon walk feels uphill though the road is flat. The girl waves you off from the door. Worth every slow step.
opt_family_eat.journal: I ate at the house of the girl I brought back to her village. They gave me bread for three days and a place at the table when I return.
opt_family_eat.partial: The food is good and the after-dinner talk endless. The grandfather won't let you go until he finishes his tale of the war with the Samnites. You leave late, happy and with bread.
opt_family_eat.success: The mother cooks as if you were family, and the grandfather tells you valley shortcuts only the villagers know. You leave with a full belly, bread for three days and two new roads in your head.
opt_family_eat.text: You go in and eat with them
opt_family_news.fail: The father is out in the fields and the mother knows nothing of roads. You stay a while anyway, out of courtesy. The girl shows you her rag doll. You gained no time, but you gained something else.
opt_family_news.partial: He tells you what he knows, which is plenty, and what he believes, which is more. You sort the useful from the doubtful on the way. Half of it helps.
opt_family_news.success: The father drives mules all over the valley and knows everything: which bridge fell, which patrol overcharges. He tells you gladly, as if paying a debt. You travel the rest of the day where no one else knows to go.
opt_family_news.text: You ask them what's happening on the road
opt_ferry.fail: The boatman wants triple once he sees your rush. You haggle, lose, and pay in time: he takes you last, after three loads of goats.
opt_ferry.partial: The boatman agrees, but first he finishes "some business" on the far bank. You wait, watching the water go by — the only thing in a hurry here.
opt_ferry.success: The boatman doesn't ask what you carry and you don't ask why his boat has a false bottom. Clean crossing, fair deal, and a new contact on the bank.
opt_ferry.text: You bargain with a local boatman
opt_ferry_bribe.fail: The boatman takes your money and three other people's at once, without settling the order. You end up arguing for a place in line you thought you'd bought.
opt_ferry_bribe.partial: He takes double, but makes you wait "a little while" that stretches on. You cross anyway, feeling you overpaid for not much.
opt_ferry_bribe.success: The boatman counts the coins with a crooked smile and puts you aboard before anyone else. You cross the estuary while those waiting are still complaining on the bank.
opt_ferry_bribe.text: You offer him double to jump the line
opt_ferry_swim.fail: Midway, a sandbar stops you at the worst moment: water to your chest, you have to wade half a league before finding a way out.
opt_ferry_swim.partial: The estuary current is stronger than any river's and pushes you well past the spot you wanted. You land upstream, exhausted but with everything intact.
opt_ferry_swim.success: You know the estuary's currents better than the boatman himself: you go in where the water pushes your way and climb out the far side before the barge casts off.
opt_ferry_swim.text: You swim the estuary, well away from the barge
opt_ferry_wait.fail: When your turn finally comes, the tide drops too low and the barge can't sail. You wait a full turn of the tide, staring at the empty estuary.
opt_ferry_wait.partial: Your turn takes twice as long as promised: the boatman favors whoever pays extra. You cross anyway, the sun already sinking.
opt_ferry_wait.success: You wait your turn on the bank, watching gulls and carts go by. The boatman, seeing you don't complain, fits you in before the line said he would.
opt_ferry_wait.text: You wait your turn, without rushing the boatman
opt_fight.fail: There were too many. They leave you on the ground, pride broken and body worse, though the package — hidden in time among the rocks — survives.
opt_fight.journal: I stood up to the road bandits. Let it be known: this messenger pays no tolls.
opt_fight.partial: You fight like a cat among dogs. You take blows, so do they, and in the end the package is still yours. Costly, but yours.
opt_fight.success: The first to close in takes an elbow that rearranges his thinking. The rest think better of it. "Not this one," says the leader, and the road opens. The story will spread.
opt_fight.text: You defend your cargo with all you've got
opt_fight_through.fail: They're professionals: they pin you in seconds. But they search your satchel for a scroll... that isn't there. You swallowed it — the small copy, the emergency one. They let you go "without the message." Idiots. You are the message.
opt_fight_through.partial: You fight dirty and fast, the way people fight at night. You take a cut on the forearm but open the gap you needed. You run the last blocks bleeding and smiling.
opt_fight_through.success: The first expects a frightened messenger and gets a professional knee. The second is stopped by the stone bench you hand him as a hat. The third decides Claudius doesn't pay that much. The way to Petro's lies open, and with style.
opt_fight_through.text: The network taught you to fight. Prove it.
opt_fire_bucket.fail: The fire is too much: the whole inn is lost. They saved the horses and the people. You go on smelling of smoke and defeat.
opt_fire_bucket.partial: The fire takes the roof and half the stable, but not the house. You leave with aching arms and a singed tunic. You arrive late, and don't regret it.
opt_fire_bucket.success: An hour of buckets from well to fire, shoulder to shoulder with mule drivers and slaves. The roof is lost, but the house stands. The innkeeper hugs you, his face black with soot. "I'll never forget your face."
opt_fire_push.fail: You keep going, and at the next bend a cart of neighbors heading to help blocks your way. You end up helping anyway, half an hour, pushing the cart. The road decides for you.
opt_fire_push.partial: You keep going, but the smoke stays on the horizon for hours and your pace grows heavy. You arrive in time, with a little less soul.
opt_fire_push.success: You run with the smoke at your back. Every mile you gain is an inn you might still save. By afternoon, the road ahead is clear of smoke. For now.
opt_fire_push.text: You keep going: the next one could be Livia's
opt_fire_soldiers.fail: The soldiers come, but late and arguing. The fire has taken everything. At least they get the family and animals out. The decurion thanks you anyway, which is no small thing.
opt_fire_soldiers.locked: The post's legionaries only listen to someone the legion knows.
opt_fire_soldiers.partial: The soldiers listen, but each wants to give a few orders. Together they save the house and lose the stable. Not bad for a cohort with no officer.
opt_fire_soldiers.success: The soldiers at the road post know you by name and follow you. In ten minutes you have a bucket chain ordered like a formation. The inn is saved almost whole. The decurion asks if you'd like to enlist.
opt_fire_soldiers.text: You organize the legionaries from the post
opt_fire_trail.fail: You hunt for tracks while everyone throws water, and a neighbor accuses you of gawking instead of helping. You have to explain who you are. By the time they let you be, the trail is gone.
opt_fire_trail.journal: I followed the Appia arsonist's trail: legionary boots and a bronze ring. The man from the Porta Capena doesn't work alone.
opt_fire_trail.partial: You find the prints and the oil jar. The trail vanishes on the road, among a hundred carts. You know how they did it; you don't yet know who.
opt_fire_trail.success: Behind the stable are hobnailed boot prints and a broken oil jar. You follow them to the road, where a rider was waiting. In the mud lies a bronze ring. The same one you saw at the Porta Capena.
opt_fire_trail.text: You look for the trail of whoever set it
opt_flood_cross.fail: An eddy takes your footing halfway. You swim more than you walk and reach the far bank coughing brown water and cursing the sky.
opt_flood_cross.partial: The current carries you farther than you figured and you come out twenty yards downstream, among reeds. Wet to the neck, but with everything you carried.
opt_flood_cross.success: You read the current like an old ford-walker: firm step, body sideways, package held high. You come out soaked to the chest and nothing worse.
opt_flood_cross.text: You wade across, water to the waist
opt_flood_plank.fail: The shepherd changes his mind at the last moment: "Not today, lad." You lose the bargaining time and cross anyway, right where you meant to from the start.
opt_flood_plank.partial: The planks sag halfway across and you end up with one wet foot and a racing heart. The shepherd charges anyway, no discount for the scare.
opt_flood_plank.success: The shepherd keeps three planks for just such days. He charges dearly and smiles even more dearly, but you cross dry and quick on his makeshift bridge.
opt_flood_plank.text: You pay a shepherd for his plank bridge
opt_flood_wait.fail: You fall asleep against the trunk and the evening chill wakes you. The ford went down a while ago; you, not so much.
opt_flood_wait.partial: The wait stretches longer than you thought: the rain returns, light but stubborn. You cross anyway, after dark, mud to the knees.
opt_flood_wait.success: You sit under a willow and watch the current fall hour after hour. At dusk the ford reappears, meek as if it never rose. You cross with dry feet.
opt_flood_wait.text: You wait on the bank for the current to drop
opt_fog_bells.fail: The bells move faster than you and you lose them in the fog. You end up in an empty pen, with no goats and no road.
opt_fog_bells.partial: The bells belong to goats, and goats go wherever they please. You reach a good path, but scratched up and with a goat that's adopted you.
opt_fog_bells.success: The bells lead you to a herdsman and his cows, who know the mountain better than any map. You walk down behind them, stepping where they step.
opt_fog_bells.text: You follow the sound of the cowbells
opt_fog_rope.fail: The stick finds air where you expected stone and you jump back so hard you sit down in a puddle. You go on, but very, very slowly.
opt_fog_rope.partial: The stick snaps halfway and you go on probing with your foot. You make it, with your heart in your mouth two or three times.
opt_fog_rope.success: You advance slowly, tapping the edge stones with a stick like a blind man in the Forum. The method is slow but exact, and the fog doesn't beat you.
opt_fog_rope.text: You probe the edge with a stick
opt_fog_veteran.fail: You get overconfident and quicken your step. A root reminds you every road is different. You go on limping, your pride a notch lower.
opt_fog_veteran.partial: Body memory helps, but fog isn't a storm and it confuses you at a fork. You find the road again after a short detour.
opt_fog_veteran.success: Your body remembers on its own: short steps, weight back, ears alert. The fog is just a silent storm. You cross it without losing your bearing.
opt_fog_veteran.text: You walk as you did crossing the storm
opt_fog_wait.fail: The fog doesn't leave; it settles in. When it finally clears it's nearly night, and you have to come down the mountain in the last light.
opt_fog_wait.partial: The fog lifts and drops twice, mocking you. You advance in short stretches, cloak wet and fingers cold.
opt_fog_wait.success: You wrap yourself in your cloak and wait, counting breaths. By mid-afternoon the fog rises like a curtain and you find you were two steps from the edge. You go on, more respectful.
opt_fog_wait.text: You sit down and wait for it to lift
opt_forge_help.fail: The smoke beats you before the flames do, and you end up coughing off to the side while others finish the job. Still, no one faults you for trying.
opt_forge_help.journal: I helped put out a fire at a roadside forge. I arrived late, but the village has a roof.
opt_forge_help.partial: The fire yields, but not before taking half the roof. You leave smelling of smoke, hands blistered, but the whole village slaps you on the back.
opt_forge_help.success: The bucket line slowly gains on the fire, and with your extra arms it's out before reaching the stable next door. The smith, sooty and grateful, swears to remember your face.
opt_forge_pass.fail: The smoke shifts just as you pass, and you end up running a stretch with streaming eyes and a raw throat, having neither helped nor avoided anything.
opt_forge_pass.partial: You walk on, but the shouting follows you two full blocks before fading behind. You reach the next stretch with your mind elsewhere.
opt_forge_pass.success: You skirt the crowd and walk on. The fire, you later learn, went out on its own before much damage. Your deadline, intact.
opt_forge_pass.text: You skirt the commotion and go on your way
opt_forge_smart.fail: You give orders confidently, but no one knows you and no one quite obeys. Chaos wins the first half hour, until the fire decides to go out on its own.
opt_forge_smart.partial: Your method half works: the main fire yields, but a spark catches the pen next door. You end up helping there too, more tired than planned.
opt_forge_smart.success: You hand out tasks like you've done it all your life: some with water, others blocking the wind with damp earth. The fire dies fast and the whole village asks your name.
opt_forge_smart.text: You organize the rescue: water on one side, earth on the other
opt_front_gate.fail: The first guard can't read and the second distrusts what he reads. By the time the steward appears, you're the night watch's best story. Claudius will hear about your graceless entrance.
opt_front_gate.partial: The guards spend five minutes arguing whether the note is genuine, until the steward appears and settles it with a gesture. You're in, but no longer discreet: half the household has seen your face.
opt_front_gate.success: The guard reads the note, pales slightly, and escorts you in silence through the main garden. Being expected by a senator opens more doors than any lockpick.
opt_front_gate.text: You walk up front and show the note
opt_fugitive_lie.fail: They half believe you: two head for the river and the third stays to watch you till they return. You wait sitting, sweating, while the runaway lies still twenty paces off.
opt_fugitive_lie.journal: I sent the catchers to the river. The man in the ditch looked at me once, and that was enough.
opt_fugitive_lie.partial: They believe you, but one stares at you a long while before following the others. Your face is now in the memory of someone who hunts people.
opt_fugitive_lie.success: You describe a man running for the river in such detail that even you believe it. They gallop off. As you pass the ditch, someone whispers "thank you" from the mud.
opt_fugitive_lie.text: You send them toward the river
opt_fugitive_point.fail: The ditch is empty: the man had already moved. The catchers come back and accuse you of sending them the wrong way. You spend a long while proving you're not his accomplice.
opt_fugitive_point.journal: I pointed to the ditch. The catchers tossed me a coin I still haven't spent.
opt_fugitive_point.partial: They find him right away. You don't look back, but you hear it anyway. The road is clear and the day, suddenly, heavier.
opt_fugitive_point.success: The catchers gallop off where you pointed. One tosses you a coin without looking. You move on fast, and the silence of the fields keeps you more company than you'd like.
opt_fugitive_point.text: You point to the ditch without a word
opt_fugitive_shrug.fail: The leader decides no one passes here without seeing something. They keep you standing in the sun until they find tracks heading elsewhere. You lose half an afternoon suspected of nothing.
opt_fugitive_shrug.partial: They don't quite believe you and search your bag to be sure. They find stale bread, a sealed letter and your bad mood. They let you go with contempt.
opt_fugitive_shrug.success: The catchers look at you, decide you're not worth the effort and ride on. You helped no one and handed over no one. The road asks no more than that of you, for today.
opt_fugitive_shrug.text: You say you saw no one
opt_gaius_believe.fail: Gaius dictates so fast and so angrily that half of it is illegible. You have to make a clean copy twice. The letter goes out late and smudged. But it goes out.
opt_gaius_believe.journal: Gaius says he deserted because his centurion stole. I believed him. His side goes in the letter to Sextus too.
opt_gaius_believe.partial: You write what he says, but it's short on dates and long on anger. The letter comes out uneven. Sextus will have to read between the lines.
opt_gaius_believe.success: Gaius dictates and you write: dates, sacks, names. Lucius's letter asks for time; yours now asks for justice. Gaius squeezes your hand with a soldier's grip. For the first time since you arrived, he smiles.
opt_gaius_believe.text: You believe him and promise to write it in
opt_gaius_doubt.fail: Gaius gets angry and Lucius has to come down to calm him. You leave with the noise of the argument behind you. It's not your fight, but now you've heard it.
opt_gaius_doubt.partial: Gaius doesn't insist, but he looks at you like those left behind. You climb the stairs with that look on your neck.
opt_gaius_doubt.success: Gaius lets go of your arm and nods. "You're right. Just take it." A letter is easier to carry than a cause. You leave light, though something stays heavy.
opt_gaius_proof.fail: Gaius has no proof: he has rage. He wastes half an hour of yours trying to remember something he never knew. You leave with the letter as it was and less time.
opt_gaius_proof.partial: Gaius remembers a name, but isn't sure of the street. You write it down anyway. Half a lead beats nothing.
opt_gaius_proof.success: Gaius thinks and gives you what you needed: the name of the miller who bought the stolen grain. Something Sextus can verify in an afternoon. The letter stops being a plea and becomes a grounded accusation.
opt_gaius_proof.text: You ask him for proof: something Sextus can check
opt_ghost_ask_local.fail: The muleteer is offended that you doubt the legend and refuses to say more. You cross the stretch with the same uncertainty as always, only later.
opt_ghost_ask_local.partial: The muleteer tells three different versions of the same story, each more inflated. You cross anyway, with more doubts than certainties.
opt_ghost_ask_local.success: The muleteer, more wine in him than fear, tells you the real story: an old accident, nothing supernatural. You cross the next day, free of superstition.
opt_ghost_ask_local.text: You ask a muleteer for the real story of the stretch
opt_ghost_cross_night.fail: An owl shrieks right behind you and for a moment you run more than you walk. You cross anyway, shaken and in no mood to tell anyone the details.
opt_ghost_cross_night.partial: You cross, but every creaking branch makes you look back. You reach the far side with nothing real to report, except a pulse still racing.
opt_ghost_cross_night.success: You cross with a steady step and a cool head, giving no night noise a body. On the other side, the road is still just road.
opt_ghost_offering.fail: You leave the offering, but a fox carries it off before you've gone ten paces. You take it as a bad sign and cross at a run, tripping on every root. No ghosts; plenty of roots.
opt_ghost_offering.journal: I left bread and salt on the stone of the nameless stretch. The augur at the crossroads was right: roads charge a toll too.
opt_ghost_offering.partial: You leave the offering and cross alone. The stretch is still, too still, but nothing steps into your path. You reach the far side with your neck prickling and the package dry.
opt_ghost_offering.success: Bread, salt and a coin on the carved stone, as the augur at the crossroads used to do. The muleteers watch, and one spits to the side, approving. Two walk you across. The night passes without a single extra sound.
opt_ghost_offering.text: You leave an offering on the stone, as the augur taught you
opt_ghost_wait_dawn.fail: You oversleep and lose a good part of the morning. The stretch is still there, as much a stretch as ever, in no hurry at all.
opt_ghost_wait_dawn.partial: The night drags on, full of noises that are probably animals and an imagination that doesn't help. You cross at first light, worn out from barely sleeping.
opt_ghost_wait_dawn.success: You camp on the safe side of the carved stone, fire high all night. At dawn the stretch is just more road, long and shadowless.
opt_ghost_wait_dawn.text: You camp before the stone and wait for dawn
opt_gladiator_around.fail: The lanista spots you and takes you for a runaway slave from another school. Explaining you're a free courier, with his hand on your neck, takes a while.
opt_gladiator_around.partial: The ditch is deeper than it looked and you climb out muddy to the knees. From the wagon, a gladiator claps slowly.
opt_gladiator_around.success: You drop into the ditch while the lanista argues with the driver. No one looks: gladiators don't watch what they can't fight. You rejoin the road a hundred paces on.
opt_gladiator_around.text: You skirt the wagon by the ditch
opt_gladiator_fame.fail: The giant knows you and, for that very reason, insists on testing whether the story is true. You escape the bear hug with a complaining rib and your reputation intact.
opt_gladiator_fame.partial: They know you, but the lanista wants the whole fight told. You give the short version; they want the long one. You pass to applause, throat dry.
opt_gladiator_fame.success: The giant comes over and shakes your hand like a colleague. The other gladiators lift the wagon themselves so you can pass, and the lanista offers you a contract you decline gracefully.
opt_gladiator_fame.text: "Aren't you the one who stopped the bandits?"
opt_gladiator_push.fail: The wagon gives the wrong way and pins half your foot in the mud. Nothing broken, but you limp a good while and the lanista doesn't even apologize.
opt_gladiator_push.partial: The axle goes in on the third try, and your back will remember it until the next way station. The giant gives you half a smile: you've charmed someone who kills for a living.
opt_gladiator_push.success: Between you, two slaves and the giant, the wagon rises just enough to seat the axle. The lanista slaps your back like you're good merchandise. "If you ever want to eat every day, Capua awaits."
opt_gladiator_push.text: You help lift the broken axle
opt_gladiator_spar.fail: One blow and you see sky. When you wake, the wagon is gone and someone has tucked the package under your head as a pillow. An almost kind gesture.
opt_gladiator_spar.journal: I lasted a bout with a Capuan gladiator in the middle of the road. My ears are still ringing.
opt_gladiator_spar.partial: You stay on your feet, which is a lot. The giant lands a backhand that leaves your cheek hot, and waves you through with a look of "we'll finish another day."
opt_gladiator_spar.success: You dodge the first blow, the second and the third. On the fourth you drive a shoulder into his ribs, and the giant laughs from the ground. The lanista, delighted, clears the road with his own men.
opt_gladiator_spar.text: You agree to a bout with the giant
opt_grill_northman.fail: Your questions spook him: professionals don't chat. He evaporates mid-sentence and leaves you talking to yourself, no money and no information. At least the seal is intact.
opt_grill_northman.partial: The talk is a chess game of hints. He gets nothing from you; you get next to nothing from him. "The north," he says, leaving, "always pays better than the south." Noted.
opt_grill_northman.success: You play his game: question for question, silence for silence. In the end he lets slip more than he meant to: "Petro pays. Petro pays to know what your master is plotting." You leave having sold nothing and knowing a name worth more than two hundred denarii.
opt_grill_northman.text: You ask first: "Who pays to look at wax?"
opt_grudge_pay.fail: He grabs the purse and, for pure fun, makes you wait on a rock while he counts it coin by coin. A quarter hour of arithmetic humiliation. Then he lets you go.
opt_grudge_pay.partial: The purse looks thin to him, so he makes you empty your pockets too. You lose your travel bread and keep the package. You walk on, whistling low out of spite.
opt_grudge_pay.success: He catches the purse midair, weighs it and steps aside with a stage bow. "Those who pay come back too." You pass untouched. The roads already tell a different story about you.
opt_grudge_pay.text: You toss him the purse and pass
opt_grudge_stand.fail: You stand firm, but there are five. They knock you into the mud, search your bag and laugh a while. You hid the package well and they don't find it. You get up muddy, without having run. That's something.
opt_grudge_stand.journal: The bandit I once ran from was waiting for me. This time I didn't run.
opt_grudge_stand.partial: You stand firm through the first shove, and the second. At the third the leader raises a hand: "Enough, this one's changed." They let you pass with a bruise and a different reputation.
opt_grudge_stand.success: You don't run. That alone disarms them: they came to laugh, not to fight. The first to come close takes a staff across the wrist, and the rest remember they have things to do. The leader waves from afar, with fresh respect.
opt_grudge_stand.text: This time you stand your ground
opt_grudge_woods.fail: You get lost among identical pines and come out on the road right behind them. They see you, laugh, and this time you do run. Your legs, at least, are still good.
opt_grudge_woods.partial: The pines are full of dry branches and one cracks like a whip. They shout, search a while, get bored. You come out with your tunic full of resin and the package safe.
opt_grudge_woods.success: They watch the bend; you're already among the pines, treading needles without a sound. You come out on the road half a mile on and hear them still waiting. You didn't run this time: you walked very well.
opt_grudge_woods.text: You slip into the pines where they don't expect you
opt_guild_warning.fail: He laughs. "The Guild is far away and I'm right here." He doesn't leave until the innkeeper, who does know Varus, asks him to pay and go. The innkeeper saved you, not your name. Not yet.
opt_guild_warning.locked: To speak for the Guild, the Guild must respect you.
opt_guild_warning.partial: He hesitates, calculates, and finally rises — but first lets you know the Guild isn't in every inn. He's right. Tonight you sleep with your bag for a pillow.
opt_guild_warning.success: You say it without raising your voice. The northerner gathers up the pouch slowly, as if he'd dropped it, and leaves without finishing his wine. In the network's way stations, a Guild threat is worth more than a sword.
opt_guild_warning.text: "The Guild already knows who you are. Leave."
opt_heat_farmer.fail: The farmer distrusts a stranger asking for water at noon and shuts the gate on you without much explanation. You go on with your skin as empty as before.
opt_heat_farmer.partial: The farmer gives you water but asks for help in return: carrying two buckets to the pen. You pay in sweat for what you meant to get free.
opt_heat_farmer.success: The farmer fills your skin without hesitation and even tosses you an old straw hat "for the road." You go on cool, with water to spare and a new story.
opt_heat_farmer.text: You ask a farmer by the road for water
opt_heat_push.fail: The heat beats you halfway and you end up sitting in a rock's shade, waiting for the world to stop spinning before going on.
opt_heat_push.partial: You make it through the stretch, but the heat takes its toll in brief dizzy spells that force you to stop twice. You arrive whole, swaying a bit.
opt_heat_push.success: You ration every sip of what's left and find the right pace to keep from burning out. You reach the next village with a dry throat and the deadline intact.
opt_heat_push.text: You keep walking in the full sun
opt_heat_rest.fail: You oversleep under the tree and wake with the sun already sinking on the other side. The nap took more time than you asked for.
opt_heat_rest.partial: The shade you find is scant and shared with a herd of noisy goats. You wait anyway, amid the bleating, until the sun eases a little.
opt_heat_rest.success: You find the generous shade of an old carob tree and wait out the day's hardest hours. When you set off again, the road is another: cooler, kinder.
opt_heat_rest.text: You find shade and wait for the sun to drop
opt_help_full.fail: The old man is more stubborn than his mule: he insists on going back for his goods. It takes longer than planned to convince him life is worth more than wineskins.
opt_help_full.journal: I lost two hours helping an old man on the road. Some deliveries carry no seal.
opt_help_full.partial: You leave him safe with a family of shepherds. You lost two hours and gained something not priced in denarii.
opt_help_full.success: You carry him to the nearest hamlet. He turns out to be a merchant known in three provinces. "A messenger who stops," he says. "I'll remember your face, and your Guild."
opt_help_full.text: You help him properly: water, bandages, and on to the village
opt_help_quick.fail: In your haste the bandage is loose and you have to redo it. Half measures always cost double.
opt_help_quick.partial: You do what you can in little time. As you walk away, his "thank you" follows you a whole league.
opt_help_quick.success: Quick hands: you give him water, splint his arm, and leave him in view of the next caravan. The best of both worlds, and the deadline breathes.
opt_help_quick.text: You leave him water and shade — the deadline rules
opt_honest.fail: Claudius isn't satisfied. You mention Varus, and that complicates things.
opt_honest.partial: Claudius frowns but accepts the answer.
opt_honest.success: Claudius values honesty. "A messenger who doesn't lie — rare and valuable."
opt_honest.text: "Only my direct superior, who sent me."
opt_horse_cure.fail: The horse stands, looks at you and lies back down, on your cloak. The dealer laughs from the door and raises his price.
opt_horse_cure.partial: The horse half recovers and carries you slowly to the next station. You leave him resting there and they give you another, which may or may not be better.
opt_horse_cure.success: You get him up, walk him in circles and rub his belly as a muleteer once taught you. Soon the horse passes what was troubling him and whinnies. You ride out, the keeper impressed.
opt_horse_dealer.fail: Two milestones on, a rider shouts that the horse is his. You have to hand it back and go on foot. The dealer, of course, is long gone from the station.
opt_horse_dealer.partial: The horse runs well for a while, then remembers it's old. You arrive, but at a procession's pace, having paid for a charger.
opt_horse_dealer.success: You haggle like at the Forum Boarium and the dealer gives in with a fake smile. The horse is genuinely good. You don't ask where it came from and he doesn't say.
opt_horse_wait.fail: The relay arrives lame in one foreleg. You need the smith, and the smith is at a wedding. The day slips away among oxen and whinnies.
opt_horse_wait.partial: The relay arrives, but it's an old mare who trots at her own pace. You arrive, yes. She decides when.
opt_horse_wait.success: The relay arrives from the neighboring station, healthy and eager. Meanwhile you helped walk the sick one, who now stands on his own. The keeper writes your name among the good ones.
opt_horse_wait.text: You wait for the next official relay
opt_hostage_ignore.fail: The decurion saw the hiss and searches your load in case you carry something for the hostage. He finds nothing, but takes his time not finding it.
opt_hostage_ignore.partial: The decurion wants to know what the Gaul said. You tell the truth: nothing. He keeps you a while asking the same thing in other words.
opt_hostage_ignore.success: You salute the decurion by the book and he returns it, with a drink of cool water. The Gaul watches you pass with the face of someone who expected nothing else.
opt_hostage_ignore.text: You ignore him and salute the decurion
opt_hostage_letter.fail: The decurion catches you both. The Gaul swears he asked for water, and you that you gave it. They let you go late, with a promise your name will appear in a report.
opt_hostage_letter.journal: I'm hiding a Gallic hostage's letter to his mother. If they find it, nobody wrote it.
opt_hostage_letter.partial: You get the letter, but a legionary sees you stow something. You have to invent a romance with a washerwoman from Arelate. He believes you, more or less.
opt_hostage_letter.success: The Gaul slips you a small tablet while the sentry relieves himself behind a tree. You hide it in your sandal sole. He looks at you and, for the first time, seems a boy of twenty.
opt_hostage_letter.text: You secretly take his letter for his mother
opt_hostage_talk.fail: Your ten words of Gaulish include an accidental insult. The hostage is offended, the decurion laughs, and you leave with burning ears.
opt_hostage_talk.partial: The decurion agrees to read the letter, but the Gaul doesn't want it read. In the end nothing is sent, and you leave with time lost and a clean conscience.
opt_hostage_talk.success: With your Latin for the decurion and your ten words of Gaulish for the boy, you get the hostage to send his letter openly, read and sealed by the escort. Nobody lies and everyone's at ease.
opt_hostage_talk.text: You talk to both in their own tongue
opt_hunters_decoy.fail: The leader opens the fake on the spot and throws it in the mud. "Not this one." Now you have to really run, and you run with the real ledger pounding your ribs.
opt_hunters_decoy.partial: They grab the fake, but one can read and starts flipping pages. You're already two hundred paces off. They shout; they don't catch you.
opt_hunters_decoy.success: You toss them the expense book from the Aricia inn, bought for exactly this. They open it, see numbers and names, and run off to show whoever pays them. By the time they realize, you'll be in Rome.
opt_hunters_decoy.text: You toss them a fake ledger
opt_hunters_run.fail: They catch you in the clearing. In the struggle the ledger falls open; one man ends up with a page. You escape with the rest. Two hundred names, minus eight.
opt_hunters_run.partial: They follow longer than you expected. One nearly grabs your cloak. You leave it in his hands and run on. The ledger stays.
opt_hunters_run.success: Four heavy men against a light courier in woods you know. You lose them at the stream. You reach the road on the far side with the ledger dry and your breath in pieces.
opt_hunters_run.text: You run into the woods, ledger strapped to you
opt_hunters_widow.fail: The leader doesn't fear the Widow: he works for someone who doesn't either. But the name gives them just enough pause for you to slip away through the trees.
opt_hunters_widow.locked: The Widow's name only protects those the Subura respects.
opt_hunters_widow.partial: They hesitate. The leader sends one to check with someone. Meanwhile, you walk off slowly. By the time he's back with the answer, you'll be gone.
opt_hunters_widow.success: The name drops like a stone down a well. The four exchange looks. Nobody on the Appia wants to take something from the Widow. They step off the road and one even wishes you a good journey.
opt_hunters_widow.text: You name the Widow: "The ledger already has a buyer."
opt_ignore.fail: The man was indeed following you — a spy of Claudius vetting the messenger. An unexpected plus.
opt_ignore.partial: Nothing happens. You reach your destination.
opt_ignore.success: It was a coincidence. You arrive without trouble.
opt_ignore.text: You ignore it and keep a normal pace
opt_jam_organize.fail: You push at the wrong spot and the wheel jams worse. The drovers thank you for trying with a look that says the opposite.
opt_jam_organize.partial: You free one wheel, but the other needs more hands than yours alone. You end up helping anyway, more tired than planned.
opt_jam_organize.success: With strength and knack you free the wheel no one wanted to touch. The drovers applaud with callused hands and the whole line moves thanks to you.
opt_jam_organize.text: You help free the wheels yourself
opt_jam_wait.fail: Just as the line starts moving, a wheel breaks completely. You wait again while someone fetches a carpenter from the nearest village.
opt_jam_wait.partial: The drovers' argument drags on with witnesses, insults and an impromptu bet. You cross at last, when no one remembers how it all began.
opt_jam_wait.success: You wait patiently while two drovers argue over whose fault it was. Finally someone gives way, the wheels come free and the line moves faster than expected.
opt_jam_wait.text: You wait your turn in line, resigned
opt_jam_walk.fail: As you pass between the carts, an ox spooks and nearly crushes you against the railing. You cross anyway, heart in your throat.
opt_jam_walk.partial: You cross on foot, but a drover takes you for part of the problem and shouts useless instructions the whole way. You come out the other side whole and a bit deaf.
opt_jam_walk.success: You slip through on foot between the locked wheels and resigned oxen. You cross in minutes, leaving behind shouting that isn't your problem.
opt_jam_walk.text: You cross the bridge on foot, between the carts
opt_keep_secret.fail: As you pass the barracks, the door opens: Varus himself, seeing someone out. "Where to, so smartly dressed, messenger?" You improvise a tavern excuse. He looks at you a second too long before nodding.
opt_keep_secret.journal: I didn't tell Varus about Claudius. Everyone's entitled to one secret. This is mine.
opt_keep_secret.partial: You walk on, though at the corner you hesitate a moment — long enough for a colleague to see and greet you. Will he tell Varus he saw you out at night? The secret is born with witnesses.
opt_keep_secret.success: You pass the barracks without slowing. Varus's lamp falls behind. For the first time since you started, you carry a message no one else knows. It feels like vertigo. It feels like growing up.
opt_keep_secret.text: You walk on — this is yours
opt_known_by_legion.fail: He mistakes you for someone else. By the time you clear it up, the centurion has decided you're guilty of something. Full search.
opt_known_by_legion.journal: A centurion recognized me from the bandit business. Fame travels faster than I do.
opt_known_by_legion.partial: The story reached him crooked — in his version there were eight bandits and a bear — and he makes you tell it twice. You pass anyway, after a stint as a bard.
opt_known_by_legion.success: You nod. The centurion addresses his men without taking his eyes off you: "This one smashed the Capua lot and never let go of the bag." They give you passage and something like respect. No one checks a thing.
opt_known_by_legion.text: The centurion narrows his eyes: "Aren't you the one from the Capua road?"
opt_known_cipher.fail: You name the cipher and get one sign wrong. He smiles: you know something, but not much. He leaves without the letter and with your face well studied. Next time he'll come better prepared.
opt_known_cipher.journal: The northerner used the same cipher as the scroll from the square. Now I know who he works for, and he knows I know.
opt_known_cipher.partial: You name the cipher and he doesn't leave: he stays to bargain over what you know and don't. Half an hour of fencing with words. In the end he rises, but makes it clear he has you noted now.
opt_known_cipher.success: The tablet peeking from his sleeve bears the same cipher as the scroll you opened in the square. You tell him so, quietly. He goes pale, leaves the pouch on the table and walks out. The pouch is a message too: keep quiet.
opt_known_cipher.text: You know that cipher: the scroll you read
opt_known_price.fail: Saying it was a mistake: the agent gathers you can be bought and offers a pittance to see if you bite. You don't. You leave with your pride intact and the feeling you gave information away for free.
opt_known_price.journal: I told Petro's agent that Claudius had already bought a glance from me. My price became a benchmark. That's reputation too.
opt_known_price.partial: The agent notes the detail and offers nothing more: he'll think it over. The good part is Petro now knows Claudius paid. The bad part is Claudius will find out you told.
opt_known_price.success: The agent's eyes gleam: if Claudius already paid, the secret is truly expensive. He raises the offer unasked. You tell him the Widow has first refusal, and he leaves happy to be on the list. That's how prices are set in the Subura.
opt_known_price.text: "Claudius already paid to look. My price is public."
opt_landslide_climb.fail: Halfway up, a stone gives under your weight and you tumble a good way back. You start over, bruised and less keen on shortcuts.
opt_landslide_climb.partial: You climb well, but a loose stone twists your ankle on the last stretch. You cross anyway, limping, your pride in better shape than your foot.
opt_landslide_climb.success: You pick each rock as if the slide were a staircase built on purpose. You cross in minutes what will cost others hours of detour.
opt_landslide_climb.text: You climb straight over the fallen rocks
opt_landslide_detour.fail: The old road vanishes into the scrub twice and you have to backtrack to find it. The detour stretches beyond anyone's patience.
opt_landslide_detour.partial: The old road has its own rockslide, a smaller one, which you get around by climbing through brush. You lose more time than you figured, but no scares.
opt_landslide_detour.success: The old road is longer but whole: no one has used it since the new pass opened, and today that works in your favor. You arrive tired, not stranded.
opt_landslide_detour.text: You look for the old road around the hills
opt_landslide_read.fail: You trust a rock that looked firm and wasn't. The stumble doesn't throw you, but you must redo half the climb another way.
opt_landslide_read.partial: Your reading is good but not perfect: you find firm footing at the cost of an extra detour among the largest rocks.
opt_landslide_read.success: You tell the settled rocks from the ones still shifting and trace a path invisible to anyone else. You cross fast without a single slip.
opt_landslide_read.text: You read the rocks and find the firmest way
opt_last_ask.fail: "Because I was young and stupid," says Lucius, and adds nothing. You drink in silence. Sometimes the short answer is the true one.
opt_last_ask.partial: Lucius dodges the question with a story about the network. At the end, between the lines, he mentions a hanged friend. You don't press. The second jug arrives on its own.
opt_last_ask.success: Lucius takes his time. "Because when I was young I saw a tavern keeper hanged for hiding a boy. Nobody remembered his name. I wanted someone to remember all of them." He pours the second. Now you understand the ledger.
opt_last_ask.text: You ask him why he wrote the ledger
opt_last_toast.fail: You toast too hard and Lucius's jug cracks. A laugh escapes him, the first in weeks. "Even toasting you're a courier: you break everything to arrive." He pours you another.
opt_last_toast.partial: You toast, but Lucius drinks half in one go and stares at his jug. Something weighs on him. You'll have to come back another night for the missing part.
opt_last_toast.success: "To the Ox," you say, and Lucius repeats it without thinking. The jugs clink, the foam jumps. The rest goes without saying. Some friendships fit in a toast.
opt_last_toast.text: You raise your jug to the Ox
opt_last_truth.fail: Halfway through, Lucius raises a hand. "That's enough. I don't want to know more." He pours the second in silence. Some truths are told once and not repeated.
opt_last_truth.journal: I told Lucius everything I did with his ledger. He listened to the end and poured me the second jug.
opt_last_truth.partial: Lucius listens with his jaw clenched. At the end he pours the second, slowly. "I don't know if I thank you. But I believe you." It's enough.
opt_last_truth.success: You tell him every decision, even the ones he won't like. Lucius listens, nods and pours the second. "You did it your way. I did it mine, thirty years ago." You drink to ways.
opt_last_word.fail: The line sounds better in your head than in the Forum. "Messengers with philosophy arrive late," he answers dryly, and dismisses you like a fig seller. You leave with the letter delivered and your tongue bitten.
opt_last_word.partial: The line lands: his jaw tightens slightly and he dismisses you with a gesture. In Roman politics, silencing a senator for one whole second is a messenger's victory.
opt_last_word.success: Claudius goes still for an instant... then lets out a short, genuine laugh, the first you've heard from him. "Insolent, and with a memory. If Varus ever bores you, my door has a poor memory for grudges." Losing with style is patrician too.
opt_last_word.text: "No letter is just paper, Senator. You taught me that."
opt_ledger_family.fail: Livia's out and her husband wants nothing to do with it. You wait two hours for her to return. She finally hides it, but the husband has seen your face and the ledger. One more who knows.
opt_ledger_family.journal: I left the ledger with Lucius's sister in Aricia. Two hundred Appia families still depend on nobody reading it. Me included, now.
opt_ledger_family.partial: Livia takes the ledger, but distrusts you until you mention Gaius. She hides it badly, in a hurry. You'll have to trust nobody searches an oven.
opt_ledger_family.success: Lucius's sister, Livia, has the same stubborn brow. She hides the ledger in the cold oven without asking anything. "My brother wrote this to protect us. Let it stay that way." You return to the road without the weight, and with another: now you're part of the list.
opt_ledger_family.text: You leave it with Lucius's sister and read no more
opt_ledger_keep.fail: You keep it, and the first thing you do is read it cover to cover. It takes all night. By morning the innkeeper knows you have something, and by noon so does half of Aricia.
opt_ledger_keep.journal: I kept Lucius's ledger. Two hundred Appia names in my satchel. Not Lucius's, not the legion's: the ledger belongs to whoever carries it.
opt_ledger_keep.partial: You keep it, but you don't know how to hide it: you carry it in your satchel like anything else. The first night, nothing happens. The second, someone goes through your things while you wash.
opt_ledger_keep.success: You close the ledger and strap it to your body, under your tunic. Two hundred names, two hundred favors, two hundred threats. Lucius wrote it to protect himself; you'll use it for something more. That night you sleep with one eye open.
opt_ledger_keep.text: You keep it: this ledger is worth more than the tavern
opt_ledger_legion.fail: Your message to Sextus is slow and the answer comes with new conditions: the ledger, plus the names of those hunting it. You accept. The deal grew while you slept.
opt_ledger_legion.journal: I decided to take the ledger to Sextus in exchange for Gaius's pardon. Two hundred names for one. The legion doesn't forget, and neither will I.
opt_ledger_legion.partial: Sextus agrees, but wants the ledger before signing anything about Gaius. You'll have to trust a centurion. There are worse bets. Not many.
opt_ledger_legion.success: You write to Sextus that same night: the ledger exists, and you know where it is. In exchange, Gaius returns to the cohort unpunished. The answer comes at dawn with the seal of the Tenth: "Deal. Bring it to the road." Lucius doesn't know yet.
opt_ledger_legion.text: You take it to Sextus: the ledger for Gaius's pardon
opt_legion_writ.fail: The paper is good; the centurion, suspicious by trade. He sends a rider to confirm with the camp and sits you in the shade to wait. The rider returns with confirmation and an apology that doesn't sound like one.
opt_legion_writ.locked: The Legions must respect you to grant that paper.
opt_legion_writ.partial: The safe-conduct is good, but the new optio reads all of it, letter by letter, lips moving. Ten minutes of military grammar. Then he waves you on with a crooked salute.
opt_legion_writ.success: The centurion knows the Tenth's seal before you finish unrolling it. He half stands to attention, which for a centurion is a bow, and lifts the barrier himself. Those in line look at you like a tribune.
opt_let_go.fail: You let him go... and a block later find he took your good kerchief too. The noble gesture has its taxes.
opt_let_go.journal: A kid stole my purse and I let him run. He had the hunger I once had. May he spend it well.
opt_let_go.partial: You let him go, angry, and with something older than anger. Money can be replaced. Other things can't.
opt_let_go.success: You lower your arm and watch him vanish into the crowd. A greengrocer who saw it all tosses you an apple: "Well done. That kid feeds three mouths." Rome has eyes.
opt_let_go.text: You let him go — you know that thinness
opt_lg_camps_deal.fail: Pompey's agent is insulted at sharing a courier with "those people" and leaves. The tribune stays, amused. Half a deal beats none.
opt_lg_camps_deal.journal: At the Rubicon way station I offered Caesar and Pompey to carry their mail in the same satchel, never opened. Both said they'd think about it. It's a start.
opt_lg_camps_deal.partial: They like the idea, but neither wants to be first to say so. They agree to write to Varus separately. It's slow. It's politics.
opt_lg_camps_deal.success: You sit between the two tables. "I won't sell you what I carry. I'll sell you that nobody reads what you send." They look at each other for the first time. The tribune laughs; the agent doesn't. But both agree to take it up with Varus.
opt_lg_camps_deal.text: Offer to carry both their letters
opt_lg_camps_none.fail: You say it out loud, but it's so noisy only the innkeeper hears you, and he applauds. The two men come over to ask what happened. You have to say it twice more.
opt_lg_camps_none.partial: You say it out loud and both leave offended, each by his own door. You keep the satchel shut and gain two polite enemies.
opt_lg_camps_none.success: You stand in the middle of the room and announce, to both tables, that a Guild satchel doesn't open for anyone's money. The two men discover each other, glare with hatred and forget all about you.
opt_lg_camps_none.text: Tell them both no, out loud
opt_lg_camps_slip.fail: The kitchen door opens onto a pen with no way out. You come back through the front entrance, covered in straw, and sit at your table as if nothing happened. The two men look at you with pity.
opt_lg_camps_slip.partial: You slip out through the kitchen, but the cook screams, thinking you're skipping the bill. You pay at the back door as the two men peer out. You're already in the saddle.
opt_lg_camps_slip.success: You order soup, leave your old cloak on the chair and slip out through the kitchen with the satchel under your arm. When the two men reach your table, they find a patched cloak and the soup going cold.
opt_lg_camps_slip.text: Leave through the kitchen before they speak to you
opt_lg_cell_explain.fail: Halfway through, a guard comes in to change the lamp and you fall silent. Aufidio laughs without humor. "See: even you know it can't be said out loud."
opt_lg_cell_explain.partial: You explain, but it sounds like an excuse even in your own mouth. Aufidio lets you finish out of politeness. "Enough. Go carry your letters."
opt_lg_cell_explain.success: "This legion opened the river for me and trusted me with its satchel," you tell him. "So did you. I chose the bigger debt." Aufidio nods slowly. "I'd have chosen the same. That's why I'm leaving."
opt_lg_cell_plead.fail: The legate cuts you off at the third word: "Not a courier's business." At nightfall they free Aufidio anyway, on the general's orders. Your plea wasn't needed. It wasn't wasted either.
opt_lg_cell_plead.journal: I asked the legate to let Aufidio go to Pompey. He said the general had already decided. I think he said it to humor me.
opt_lg_cell_plead.partial: The legate listens with a soldier's patience and promises nothing. Later you learn Aufidio walks free. You'll never know if your plea counted.
opt_lg_cell_plead.success: You tell the legate about Gaul, about the scars, about a man torn between two debts. He listens and barely smiles. "The general has already decided: he goes south with his baggage. But thank you for asking." Aufidio hears it from the tent.
opt_lg_cell_plead.text: Ask the legate to let him go south
opt_lg_cell_sit.fail: You sit down and Aufidio turns toward the canvas. He doesn't want company, least of all yours. You stay a while anyway, out of stubbornness. It does no good, except to you.
opt_lg_cell_sit.partial: You both sit in silence until the lamp burns low. At last Aufidio says: "You did your job." Whether it's a reproach is anyone's guess. You leave without knowing.
opt_lg_cell_sit.success: You sit on the tent floor and share your bread. After a while Aufidio talks: about Picenum, about a young Pompey who gave him his first staff, about Gaul. He doesn't forgive you. But he doesn't send you away either.
opt_lg_cell_sit.text: Sit with him without saying anything
opt_lg_curia_claudius.fail: Claudius talks so long the session adjourns before voting on anything. It resumes tomorrow. You spent the day on a marble step, and the warning still hasn't left the room.
opt_lg_curia_claudius.partial: Claudius speaks well, but adds things you never saw: three legions, a blood oath. You bite your tongue. The Curia votes in fear, which is how it votes best.
opt_lg_curia_claudius.success: You hand Claudius the tablet and sit on a step. He speaks for an hour, with your story and his adjectives. The Curia applauds him. Only one senator looks at you, and that senator will hire you later.
opt_lg_curia_name.fail: You withhold the name, but a senator recognizes Aufidio's hand on the tablet: they served together in Hispania. At least he says it with respect. The name is no longer yours to protect.
opt_lg_curia_name.journal: In the Curia I gave the warning and kept Aufidio's name to myself. The Senate has the news; the centurion, his life.
opt_lg_curia_name.partial: You withhold the name, and an old senator accuses you of protecting a Caesarian. They argue about you for a good while, as if you weren't there. Eventually they move on to what matters.
opt_lg_curia_name.success: "Who gave you the warning?" asks a consul. "A soldier who loves his legion and Rome," you answer. "The name is his." Some protest; Claudius smiles. A courier who doesn't hand over names is worth more.
opt_lg_curia_name.text: Tell everything, but keep Aufidio's name to yourself
opt_lg_curia_plain.fail: Your voice cracks on the first sentence in front of so many togas. You start again, quieter. The back rows ask what you said. Claudius repeats each of your sentences aloud, like an expensive echo.
opt_lg_curia_plain.journal: In the Curia I told what I saw at Ravenna and nothing more. The senators wanted a story; I gave them a report.
opt_lg_curia_plain.partial: You tell it all, but a senator interrupts every sentence to ask if you're a Caesarian. You finish anyway, voice worn out. What you said is said, even amid the shouting.
opt_lg_curia_plain.success: You speak the way you speak to Varus: timber under a tarp, greased boots, a centurion sending a warning. No adjectives. When you finish, the Curia is silent. Claudius nods. "That's how the truth sounds without a lawyer."
opt_lg_curia_plain.text: Tell what you saw, not a word more
opt_lg_doors_guild.fail: Petilio grabs your cloak in front of the whole market. "You know what it says!" People stare. You pull free and lose yourself among the stalls. Being neutral, you learn, also makes noise.
opt_lg_doors_guild.journal: I delivered Aufidio's letter as it was given to me and told no one. The satchel takes no side. Neither do I, for now.
opt_lg_doors_guild.partial: You leave, but Petilio follows you to the door begging you to take the letter to Rome. You say no three times. The third time, he believes you. You don't, yet.
opt_lg_doors_guild.success: You turn your back on Petilio and his fear. A courier delivers; he doesn't decide. Outside, Ariminum carries on with its recruiters and its market. You sit at a fountain and eat bread. Varus's rule never tasted so bitter.
opt_lg_doors_guild.text: "I brought it. The rest is your business."
opt_lg_doors_legion.fail: You get the letter back, but Petilio shouts and two of Pompey's men burst in. You escape through the yard, over a pile of empty amphorae that ring like a choir. You have the letter and half of Ariminum on your heels.
opt_lg_doors_legion.journal: I chose to ride back to Ravenna and tell the legate about Aufidio. The legion that opened the river for me deserves to know who warns the enemy, even if he isn't selling it for silver.
opt_lg_doors_legion.partial: Petilio resists and you end up tugging the letter back and forth among the amphorae. You keep it, plus an arm soaked in oil. He'll send word anyway, by mouth. But you hold the proof.
opt_lg_doors_legion.success: You pull the letter from Petilio's hands before he can burn it. "This goes back north." The oil merchant doesn't dare argue with someone who has crossed the Rubicon twice. You leave with the letter and a knot in your stomach.
opt_lg_doors_legion.text: Ride back to Ravenna and tell the legate
opt_lg_doors_memory.fail: Petilio realizes you already knew what the letter said and looks at you like a thief. He doesn't stop you, but now someone in Ariminum knows you read other people's letters.
opt_lg_doors_memory.journal: Since I'd already read the letter on the road, I left it with Petilio and took the warning in my memory. Nobody will find anything in my bag.
opt_lg_doors_memory.partial: You remember almost all of it; one date gets muddled. Petilio confirms it without realizing. You leave with the full warning and the guilt of having taken it this way.
opt_lg_doors_memory.success: You leave the letter with Petilio without a word: you already carry what it says in your head, word for word. You leave for Rome without a scrap of proof on you. To Caesar's riders, you're an empty courier.
opt_lg_doors_memory.text: You already read it: carry the warning in your head
opt_lg_doors_senate.fail: Petilio's ink, more oil than ink, smears halfway through the copy. You start over twice. You leave for Rome with a well-written tablet and a badly begun day.
opt_lg_doors_senate.journal: I chose to take Aufidio's warning to Rome. If the legion crosses, the Senate shouldn't hear it from the screaming.
opt_lg_doors_senate.partial: You copy the letter, but Petilio doesn't want you taking it: "If they catch you with that, they catch me." You argue. In the end you take it and he stays behind praying to every god in the harbor.
opt_lg_doors_senate.success: You ask Petilio for a tablet and copy the letter word for word. "Ariminum warns Pompey; I warn Rome." The oil merchant gives you his best horse unasked. Some fears are generous.
opt_lg_doors_senate.text: Copy the warning and take it to the Curia
opt_lg_farewell_hand.fail: You hold out your hand just as a tribune walks by and Aufidio has to stand to attention. Your hand hangs in the air. He slaps it as he passes, quickly. It still counts.
opt_lg_farewell_hand.partial: You shake hands and he holds on a second too long, as if still in doubt. Then he lets go. Some decisions get made many times.
