opt_lg_farewell_hand.success: You offer your hand and Aufidio grips it with the strength of a man who has decided. "If that river is ever crossed, may there be couriers like you on both sides." He puts on his helmet. He's a centurion again.
opt_lg_farewell_hand.text: Shake his hand as an equal
opt_lg_farewell_mother.fail: Aufidio starts the letter and nothing comes. "Tell her I'm fine," he asks at last. You carry a spoken message, the hardest kind to deliver.
opt_lg_farewell_mother.journal: I left Ravenna with a letter from Aufidio to his mother in Picenum. That one I carry without a second thought.
opt_lg_farewell_mother.partial: Aufidio writes, erases and writes again. The letter comes out short and crooked. He hands it over like something fragile. You put it in the best spot in the satchel.
opt_lg_farewell_mother.success: Aufidio falls silent, then writes, leaning on your back, a short letter to his mother in Picenum. "This one you can read." You don't. Some letters deserve more respect than the secret ones.
opt_lg_farewell_mother.text: Offer to carry a letter to his family
opt_lg_farewell_nod.fail: You walk past and trip over a palisade stake in front of the whole guard. Aufidio laughs for the first time in days. You did say goodbye, after all.
opt_lg_farewell_nod.partial: You walk past, but after twenty paces you turn around. He turned too. You both laugh, without much heart, and go on.
opt_lg_farewell_nod.success: You nod and walk past. Aufidio does the same. Between you remain a letter nobody read aloud and a river nobody has crossed yet. That's how people who know how to keep quiet say goodbye.
opt_lg_farewell_nod.text: Leave without a word: everything's been said
opt_lg_ford_post.fail: The guard misspells your name, crosses it out and writes it again, worse. You pass with someone else's name on the legion's tablet. Maybe that's not so bad.
opt_lg_ford_post.partial: The post has its rhythm: fodder carts first, civilians after. You wait sitting on the bank, watching the water. It's a river so small you're embarrassed to respect it.
opt_lg_ford_post.success: The guard writes your name in a soldier's hand and asks if you brought wine. You didn't. He laughs anyway and helps you carry the satchel over the footbridge. In the Thirteenth, respect the post and you're halfway there.
opt_lg_ford_post.text: Cross at the post and give your name
opt_lg_ford_reeds.fail: Among the reeds you run into two legionaries who also slipped away from the post, to fish. All three of you look guilty. They escort you to the post "to keep it legal" and eat your bread.
opt_lg_ford_reeds.partial: You cross unseen, but the Rubicon mud swallows a sandal. You reach the road limping, with no proof of crossing except the foot.
opt_lg_ford_reeds.success: Half a mile downstream, the reeds cover you to the shoulders. You cross knee-deep and come out on a fishermen's path. Nobody counted you. For a while, you exist on no side at all.
opt_lg_ford_reeds.text: Wade across through the reeds, far from the post
opt_lg_ford_timber.fail: You stare at the tarp so long the guard asks if you want to buy it. You say no, red-faced, and move on. You kept the suspicion; the guard kept your face.
opt_lg_ford_timber.journal: At the Rubicon I saw cut beams and pack mules hidden under a tarp. A legion that's only waiting doesn't stockpile bridge timber.
opt_lg_ford_timber.partial: You see the tarp and the shapes under it, but a guard steps in front just as you look. "Firewood," he says. Firewood cut square. You ride on, your doubts well fed.
opt_lg_ford_timber.success: Behind the post, under a tarp, there are beams cut to measure and mules already in harness. A legion that's waiting doesn't stockpile bridge timber. You pass without asking. You already know more than the Senate.
opt_lg_ford_timber.text: Look at what nobody looks at on the bank
opt_lg_frost_gallop.fail: The horse steps on a frozen puddle and leaves you sitting in the frost with a bruise you'll remember at every way station. It comes back for you on its own, ashamed. You go on slower and wiser.
opt_lg_frost_gallop.partial: It works until the dirt turns to mud and you have to go back to the stone, at a walk. You gained something, not everything.
opt_lg_frost_gallop.success: The verge is hard but not slick. You gallop along the boundary stones and beat the fog by half a day. The horse arrives steaming and proud.
opt_lg_frost_gallop.text: Gallop on the dirt verge, not the stone
opt_lg_frost_sky.fail: The wind doesn't turn: it stays still all day, just to prove you wrong. You leave in the fog anyway, your forecaster's pride colder than your feet.
opt_lg_frost_sky.partial: The wind turns, but later than you figured. You wait twice as long, the horse impatient. When the sun comes out, so do you.
opt_lg_frost_sky.success: You know this sky: when the wind turns toward the sea, the fog is gone within the hour. You wait under an eave for exactly that. Then, open road and winter sun.
opt_lg_frost_sky.text: Read the sky to know when it clears
opt_lg_frost_walk.fail: You walk so long in the fog that you wander off the road without noticing and end up in a sheep pen. The shepherd puts you back on the road in exchange for news from the north. You give him the worst.
opt_lg_frost_walk.partial: Walking keeps you from falling, but not from the cold. By evening you can't feel your toes. At a way station they give you hot broth and look at you like a madman.
opt_lg_frost_walk.success: You walk beside the horse, step by step, talking to it softly. The fog lifts by mid-afternoon and the whole road appears, glittering with frost. You arrive slowly, with all four of the horse's legs and both of yours.
opt_lg_frost_walk.text: Dismount and lead the horse by the bridle
opt_lg_gate_carts.fail: At the gate, a soldier jabs a pitchfork into the hay a hand's width from your ear. You climb out with your hands up and explain you were sleeping. They throw you out of camp, which is exactly what you wanted.
opt_lg_gate_carts.partial: The cart gets out, but the carter finds you halfway and charges you for the ride. You pay. At least the tribune is behind you.
opt_lg_gate_carts.success: You squeeze between two hay carts heading out for more hay. The tribune checks the first carter and gets bored by the second. You hop off a mile later, straw in your hair and the letter where it belongs.
opt_lg_gate_carts.text: Slip out hidden among the fodder carts
opt_lg_gate_open.fail: The tribune reads every letter aloud, including a love letter from a Cretan archer. Half the guard laughs. It takes forever, but by the end he's so embarrassed he searches you no further.
opt_lg_gate_open.partial: The tribune goes through the whole satchel, then looks at your hands, your cloak, your belt. He stops at the sandals. A centurion calls him just in time. You leave with your heart in your throat.
opt_lg_gate_open.success: You take out every letter and show it to him, one by one, with a scribe's patience. By the tenth the tribune is bored and waves you off: "Go." He never looks at your feet.
opt_lg_gate_open.text: Open the whole satchel, slowly, in front of him
opt_lg_gate_rule.fail: The tribune laughs at the rule and searches you anyway, except the sandals, because the Rubicon mud disgusts him. Sometimes dirt protects better than an oath.
opt_lg_gate_rule.journal: I recited to the tribune the rule I swore to Varus, and he let me through without opening anything. A given word weighs more than a seal.
opt_lg_gate_rule.partial: The tribune doesn't know the rule, but he knows the tone. He lets you through after a long look. He knows you carry something; he also knows you won't say.
opt_lg_gate_rule.success: You repeat the rule you swore to Varus, in the same voice as at the gate of Rome. The tribune hesitates and calls an old centurion, who says: "That's right, the Guild doesn't open." You pass and nobody touches a thing.
opt_lg_gate_rule.text: Recite the rule: a Guild satchel stays closed
opt_lg_letter_ask.fail: "If I tell you, you won't carry it," Aufidio answers, and he's right. He stays silent until you leave. You lost some time and gained a suspicion.
opt_lg_letter_ask.partial: Aufidio weighs the answer, then keeps it. "It says what a soldier can't say out loud." He gives you the letter anyway. Now you carry a secret shaped like a man.
opt_lg_letter_ask.success: Aufidio doesn't lie. "It says I owe my first vine staff to Pompey and my life to this legion. And that I don't want to see the two fighting." He says no more. He doesn't need to.
opt_lg_letter_ask.text: Ask him straight out what it says
opt_lg_letter_read.fail: You unfold it and a gust nearly tears it from your hands. You chase it through the mud and get it back stained. Yes, you read it. Now it also carries your thumbprint.
opt_lg_letter_read.journal: I read Aufidio's letter. It's for an oil merchant in Ariminum who works for Pompey, and it says when the legion marches.
opt_lg_letter_read.partial: You read it in a hurry, one eye on the road. You get the gist: the legion moves soon, and Aufidio is warning the south. The rest blurs with the fear that someone sees you.
opt_lg_letter_read.success: Half a mile past the camp, behind an olive tree, you unfold the letter. A few lines in a soldier's hand: the Thirteenth marches before the Ides, and Ariminum had better not be asleep. You fold it back exactly as it was. Now it weighs twice as much.
opt_lg_letter_read.text: Read it on the road, without him knowing
opt_lg_letter_take.fail: As you crouch to hide it, an optio rounds the corner of the latrines. Aufidio chews him out for something made up and you pretend to tie your sandal. It works, but nobody breathes easy.
opt_lg_letter_take.partial: You put it away unread, but Aufidio keeps staring at the sandal as if he wanted it back. He doesn't ask. You both stay silent longer than needed.
opt_lg_letter_take.success: You fold the letter in four and slip it into your sandal without a glance. Aufidio breathes deep. "Varus trains good people." He squeezes your shoulder with a hand as heavy as a shield.
opt_lg_letter_take.text: Tuck it in your sandal without reading it
opt_lg_night_bridge.fail: The bridge goes up, but you end up crossing behind the pack mules, who refuse. You cross pushing a mule by the rump. That's how you enter history.
opt_lg_night_bridge.partial: The bridge takes longer than promised: one beam is short. You wait with the silent cohorts, listening to thousands of men breathe. By the time you cross, dawn is close.
opt_lg_night_bridge.success: The engineers lay the beams that were under the tarp and within an hour there's a bridge. You cross among the first, feet dry and orders too. On the other side the night is the same. Nothing else is.
opt_lg_night_bridge.text: Wait for the legion's timber bridge
opt_lg_night_ride.fail: The horse balks at the bank and throws you into the water alone. You cross on foot and wait for it on the far side; the animal strolls over behind a cohort. You arrive without glory and with the orders dry.
opt_lg_night_ride.partial: You cross at a gallop and get soaked to the ears. The cold knocks the wind out of you, but not the orders. You reach the outposts shivering and they have to pry the orders from your hand.
opt_lg_night_ride.success: The horse plunges into the river without hesitation and comes out the other side at full gallop. You don't look back. At midnight you pound on the gate of the Ariminum outposts. When the general crosses, the city will already know what to do.
opt_lg_night_ride.text: Cross at a gallop and ride straight to Ariminum
opt_lg_night_wade.fail: You slip mid-river and the orders nearly float off with the current. A legionary from the vanguard grabs your belt and hauls you out. You reach Italy led by the hand of the legion you're guiding.
opt_lg_night_wade.journal: I crossed the Rubicon before the Thirteenth. The water was freezing. On the other side, it was already a different war.
opt_lg_night_wade.partial: The bottom is mud and you sink to your knees. You come out shivering, the orders dry. Behind you, the general says something soldiers will repeat for years. You didn't quite catch it.
opt_lg_night_wade.success: You wade into the icy water with the orders above your head. Climbing out on the far side, in Italy, you turn around: the general finally says something about the die being cast. Behind you, the Thirteenth begins to cross.
opt_lg_night_wade.text: Cross first, waist-deep in the water
opt_lg_post_ford.fail: A stone shifts under your foot and you end up sitting in the river. A shepherd fishes you out, laughing, and to top it off walks you to the checkpoint. The optio searches you, dripping.
opt_lg_post_ford.partial: The ford is deeper than the shepherds claim. You reach the far bank chest-deep, the satchel dry by some miracle. Your sandals, less so.
opt_lg_post_ford.success: Upstream, where shepherds cross their sheep, the Nar runs cold but gentle. You wade across with the satchel on your head and come out on the Flaminia a mile past the checkpoint. Nobody wrote anything down.
opt_lg_post_ford.text: Cross the Nar at the shepherds' ford
opt_lg_post_plaque.fail: The optio doesn't know the bull of the Tenth and the plaque means nothing to him. He searches you like everyone else. At least he hands it back carefully, as if it came from a temple.
opt_lg_post_plaque.journal: At Narnia I showed the bull plaque and a post of Pompey's men stood to attention for a courier of the Tenth. The bronze still opens doors.
opt_lg_post_plaque.partial: The optio knows the plaque, but hesitates: the Tenth is Caesar's and he is Pompey's. In the end habit beats politics. He lets you through with an odd look.
opt_lg_post_plaque.success: The optio sees the bronze bull and snaps to attention before he can think. "Courier of the Tenth, pass." He doesn't even glance at the satchel. Behind you, a carter mutters that this is what friends are for.
opt_lg_post_plaque.text: Show the bull plaque of the Tenth
opt_lg_post_wait.fail: The optio has never heard of the Guild and sends for his centurion, who is at lunch. You wait an eternity. The centurion arrives, looks at the seal, curses the optio and lets you go.
opt_lg_post_wait.partial: The line is long and the optio thorough. He checks every seal twice and writes your name on a tablet. You pass, but now your name travels south in some report.
opt_lg_post_wait.success: You wait in line among turnip carts and show the satchel without hurry. The optio checks the Guild seals, finds them in order and waves you through like a commander. You made his day without giving him anything.
opt_lg_post_wait.text: Wait in line and open whatever they ask
opt_lg_report_all.fail: You write it all, then, tired, erase half so it fits. You send a version full of gaps. Varus will read the gaps too; he always does.
opt_lg_report_all.journal: I wrote Varus the whole winter, leaving nothing out. Including what I did with Aufidio's letter.
opt_lg_report_all.partial: You write it all, but the wax runs short and you have to shrink your letters at the end. Varus will need good light. The important part fit.
opt_lg_report_all.success: You fill both sides of the tablet and ask for another. Everything: the river, the letter, your choice. You send the wax south without rereading it. Varus answers in four days with one line: "Well told." Coming from him, it's a crown.
opt_lg_report_all.text: Write him everything, even what he won't like
opt_lg_report_ask.fail: Varus answers the question with another: "And what would you have done if you hadn't done what you did?" You spend the night thinking. Typical Varus.
opt_lg_report_ask.partial: Varus answers everything but the question. In one corner of the wax there's a single word: "Later." Someday he'll tell you.
opt_lg_report_ask.success: You end the report with a question: what would he have done. The answer arrives a few days later: "The same, or the opposite. What matters is you got there." You keep that tablet at the bottom of your saddlebag.
opt_lg_report_ask.text: Ask him what he would have done
opt_lg_report_short.fail: Three lines, and in one you get the date wrong. Varus will correct the date in his reply before anything else. That's him.
opt_lg_report_short.partial: Three lines seem too few, so you add a fourth. Then you erase it. It leaves a smudge in the wax that says more than the other three.
opt_lg_report_short.success: "Arrived. Chose. I'm fine." You send the tablet south with half a smile. Varus, who invented the three-line tablet, will understand all three and what they don't say.
opt_lg_report_short.text: Send him three lines, like he does
opt_lg_riders_hide.fail: The kiln has a tenant: a shepherd who doesn't want visitors. You argue in whispers while the riders pass twice. They don't see you, but the shepherd charges you rent in bread.
opt_lg_riders_hide.partial: The kiln hides you, but the horse whinnies as they pass. The riders stop, listen and move on: in winter every horse whinnies. You wait twice as long, just in case.
opt_lg_riders_hide.success: Beside the road is a lime kiln that's been cold for years. You squeeze in, horse and all, behind the wall. The riders pass, come back, pass again. By afternoon they give up. You come out white with lime and free.
opt_lg_riders_hide.text: Hide in an abandoned lime kiln
opt_lg_riders_lie.fail: One of the riders recognizes you from camp: "You crossed the river last week." They search you head to toe. The warning is sewn into your cloak lining and they don't find it, but now they know your face.
opt_lg_riders_lie.partial: They half believe you: one heads for the coast and the other rides beside you a good while, chatting about the cold. Eventually he gets bored and follows his comrade.
opt_lg_riders_lie.success: When they catch up, you describe a thin, hurried courier who turned toward the sea at the last crossroads. They thank you and gallop off toward the coast. You carry on along the Flaminia, the only courier on the road.
opt_lg_riders_lie.text: Keep a walking pace and lie to them calmly
opt_lg_riders_race.fail: They catch you on the climb and block the road. They search saddlebag and cloak and find nothing, because the warning is in your boot. They let you go, but one of them trails you at a distance until nightfall.
opt_lg_riders_race.partial: You pull ahead, but your horse tires before theirs. A bend with a cart across it saves you: they rein in, you squeeze past on the side.
opt_lg_riders_race.success: You dig in your heels and Petilio's horse, better than it looked, stretches out over the road. They carry armor; you, a tablet. You reach the way station a mile ahead and swap horses almost without dismounting.
opt_lg_riders_race.text: Outrun them at a gallop to the way station
opt_lg_rule_ask.fail: "What I know of the north, the road will tell you," Varus answers, and leaves. You're left at the gate with the question in your mouth and the mule drivers staring.
opt_lg_rule_ask.partial: Varus tells you what the way stations say: that in Ravenna there's a bored legion and a general who isn't. He knows no more, or won't say. It's something.
opt_lg_rule_ask.success: Varus lowers his voice. "Caesar has a single legion this side of the Alps, and the Senate wants him disarmed before the Kalends. One legion alone crosses nothing. Unless he sends it." It's the closest thing to a map he'll give you.
opt_lg_rule_ask.text: You ask what he knows of the north
opt_lg_rule_eyes.fail: "Those who look too much end up telling," says Varus, and repeats the rule twice more, slowly. You leave late, feeling you failed an exam you didn't know you were sitting.
opt_lg_rule_eyes.journal: I told Varus I'd carry the satchel with my eyes open. He didn't like it, but he didn't say no either.
opt_lg_rule_eyes.partial: Varus doesn't answer. He adjusts your satchel strap, like when you were an apprentice, and turns back without a word. You'll carry that silence all the way to Ariminum.
opt_lg_rule_eyes.success: Varus gives you a long look. "Open eyes aren't a sin. An open mouth is." He lets you go. You know he liked the answer more than he'll admit.
opt_lg_rule_eyes.text: "I'll carry it, but with my eyes open."
opt_lg_rule_swear.fail: You swear so solemnly that Varus frowns: "It's not a temple, it's a gate." You repeat it quieter. You've lost some time and some dignity, but the rule has been said.
opt_lg_rule_swear.journal: I swore to Varus the satchel has no side. I said it aloud, at the gate, in front of the mule drivers.
opt_lg_rule_swear.partial: You swear, but get one word wrong and Varus makes you start over. The mule drivers grow impatient behind you. The second time it comes out whole, and Varus listens as if it were the first.
opt_lg_rule_swear.success: You lay your hand on the leather and repeat the rule word for word. Varus nods just once. A passing mule driver doffs his hat, as if he'd witnessed a real oath. So did you.
opt_lg_rule_swear.text: You swear the rule with your hand on the satchel
opt_lg_table_rule.fail: Pompey's agent gets up halfway through your proposal and Varus has to fetch him from the street. He comes back with him by the arm. They sign late and in a foul mood, but they sign.
opt_lg_table_rule.journal: At Varus's table I proposed that the Guild satchel pass sealed through both camps. Both signed, each convinced he was fooling the other.
opt_lg_table_rule.partial: They argue every word. The tribune wants exceptions; the agent, guarantees. At dawn they sign a version with two lines struck out. Varus says the best laws have crossings-out.
opt_lg_table_rule.success: You say it in three lines, as Varus taught you: a satchel under the Guild seal passes through both sides and nobody opens it. The two men look for the trick and don't find it, because there isn't one. They sign. Varus signs last.
opt_lg_table_rule.text: Propose the rule: sealed satchel, free passage
opt_lg_table_silence.fail: Your silence makes them both nervous, each sure you know something about him. They spend the night distrusting each other. Varus kicks you under the table. They sign at dawn, out of exhaustion.
opt_lg_table_silence.partial: Varus talks, but the two men look at you, waiting for something. In the end you nod once. It's enough. They sign.
opt_lg_table_silence.success: You keep quiet, and your silence weighs more than a speech: the courier who crossed between them has nothing to sell. Varus says little. The two men sign so as not to be the first to leave.
opt_lg_table_silence.text: Say nothing and let Varus talk
opt_lg_table_story.fail: You tell the river part so well that the tribune and the agent start arguing over who has the right to cross it. Varus parts them with a look. The meeting resumes an hour later.
opt_lg_table_story.partial: The story is long and Pompey's agent yawns. But the tribune listens, and at the end says: "If he got through, anyone can." It's an odd argument. It works.
opt_lg_table_story.success: You tell them the winter: the checkpoints, the skinny river, the two tables at the way station. Without meaning to, you show them the satchel already works. The tribune is first to laugh. The agent, first to sign.
opt_lg_table_story.text: Tell them how you crossed without opening anything
opt_listen_story.fail: Midway through, the veteran falls asleep on his feet, leaning on your shoulder. You prop him against the railing and cross on tiptoe.
opt_listen_story.journal: I lost an hour listening to a one-eyed veteran on a bridge. The story was good. No one else listens to it.
opt_listen_story.partial: You hear the full version, with detours through three campaigns and two wives. You lose nearly an hour. The old man gains a good day.
opt_listen_story.success: The story is long, exaggerated and magnificent. At the end, the old man squeezes your shoulder: "You're the first in a year who hasn't dodged me." He walks you across the bridge himself, an honor guard.
opt_listen_story.text: You sit on the railing and listen
opt_long_route.fail: They're patient as debt collectors. In the end you lose them by sheer luck, when a procession of Isis floods the street. The gods help, but they charge in time.
opt_long_route.partial: The endless stroll works, but it costs you a long hour and your feet. When you finally reach the temple, the only shadows are the columns'.
opt_long_route.success: Three hours of pointless loops: you enter two taverns by one door and leave by another, pray at the wrong temple, buy figs you don't want. Your shadows give up in the second hour. Patience is a weapon too.
opt_long_route.text: You take the long way: let them follow, let them tire
opt_look_away.fail: You watch the river, but the river betrays you: in the still water by the pier, your eyes and Varus's meet anyway. An instant. Enough. Both walk on knowing the other saw.
opt_look_away.partial: You watch the brown water go by. The steps fade... and at the end, Varus's voice, without turning: "The river won't give you anything back, messenger." He had to have the last word. He always did.
opt_look_away.success: You study the Tiber as if you owed it money. Varus's steps pass behind you without slowing. Nobody said anything; nobody had to lie or forgive. Some silences are the last favor between two men who respected each other.
opt_look_away.text: You watch the river till they pass
opt_lose_them.fail: They're good: one covers each exit. You only lose them at the public baths, with an emergency change of tunic that costs you your dignity and a few denarii.
opt_lose_them.partial: You lose them, but the price is smelling of sardines all the way to the temple. The priest will wrinkle his nose. Better sardines than spies.
opt_lose_them.success: At this hour the fish market is a battlefield of baskets and shouting. You go in as someone and come out as no one, through the offal door. Your shadows are still waiting for you by the tuna.
opt_lose_them.text: You lose them in the fish market
opt_loyal_claudius.fail: The seal stays crooked no matter how you work it. You decide to tell Claudius yourself: "it fell, it opened, I didn't read it." He studies you for an eternity... and believes you. Or decides to, which is even better: now he knows you know, and you're still alive. That's patrician trust.
opt_loyal_claudius.journal: I read what I shouldn't have and chose to forget it. Claudius bets on winners, and I changed tables. Varus taught me the trade. Claudius will teach me power.
opt_loyal_claudius.partial: You mend the seal as best you can and bury what you read. On the bridge, your reflection in the Tiber looks at you oddly. Let it. You deliver. Period.
opt_loyal_claudius.success: You breathe deep, mend the seal with a surgeon's hand and keep walking. Varus's network gave you a trade; Claudius offers you a future. Sentimental men don't grow old in Rome. You deliver perfectly.
opt_loyal_claudius.text: You read nothing. You're Claudius's courier.
opt_loyal_varus.fail: You copy fast and badly, and the mended seal is visibly tampered with. Tiro will notice. Let him: by the time he tells Claudius, Varus will know everything.
opt_loyal_varus.journal: I read what I shouldn't have: Claudius is after Petro, and Petro's fall takes the network. I chose: Varus must know.
opt_loyal_varus.partial: Your copy comes out clumsy — your hands won't stop shaking — but legible. The mended seal would pass a careless inspection. You pray Tiro is careless.
opt_loyal_varus.success: With a steady hand you copy the essentials onto a strip of plane-tree bark, mend the seal with candle wax as the trade taught you, and deliver at Tiro's without a trace. The copy burns in your tunic. Varus will see it before dawn.
opt_loyal_varus.text: Varus has to see this. Tonight.
opt_loyal_widow.fail: The agent raises the offer three times before giving up, and the last figure follows you to the tavern door. Loyalty in the Subura costs dearly. Betrayal, more dearly still. You chose well. You think.
opt_loyal_widow.journal: Petro's agent offered triple to betray the Widow. In the Subura, your word is worth more than gold. And it's scarier.
opt_loyal_widow.partial: The agent presses with dizzying figures. You repeat the Widow's name like a charm, and it works: he leaves muttering about "the monopoly on information." It almost sounds like praise.
opt_loyal_widow.success: The agent goes pale at the name. "The Widow? You should have said so." The litter leaves almost at a trot. In the night trade, some names are armor.
opt_loyal_widow.text: "I already have a buyer. The Widow doesn't share."
opt_marco_who_told.fail: Marco doesn't want questions: he wants the dossier or a reason. The question sounds like an excuse. You argue on the bridge until a patrol passes and you split without looking at each other. You got through, but the friendship stayed on the bridge.
opt_marco_who_told.journal: I asked Marco who had told Varus. He couldn't answer. Now the network has a doubt, and the doubt isn't mine.
opt_marco_who_told.partial: The question stops him, but doesn't fully convince him: "Someone told him, and you're the one standing here." He lets you pass anyway, looking over your shoulder as if for someone else. Suspicion has changed direction.
opt_marco_who_told.success: Marco opens his mouth and closes it. You never said a word, and he knows it. So someone else talks to Varus, someone who knows your steps. "Go," he says, already thinking of something else. "I have something to find out."
opt_marco_who_told.text: "Varus didn't learn a thing from me. Ask him who told."
opt_milestone_farm.fail: The farm is farther than it looked and the dog won't let you near the door. You return to the fork with no answer and the sun quite a bit lower.
opt_milestone_farm.partial: The farm holds only a deaf old man who answers a different question. In the end you get it from his gestures. You return to the fork half convinced.
opt_milestone_farm.success: The farmwife gives directions without stopping her grinding. "The left one. The other goes to my brother-in-law's, and I don't recommend it." You go on, sure.
opt_milestone_farm.text: You ask at a nearby farm
opt_milestone_lift.fail: The stone turns, but the inscribed face is cracked right where it mattered. You get half a number and the name of a consul who's no use to you.
opt_milestone_lift.journal: I raised a fallen milestone at a lost fork. Someone else will reach their destination because of it.
opt_milestone_lift.partial: You turn the stone and scrape your hands raw. The inscription is worn, but the city's name is legible. Enough.
opt_milestone_lift.success: You lever it with a log and the stone rolls. The consul's inscription gives direction and distance. You stand it up again, for whoever comes next.
opt_milestone_lift.text: You turn the stone and read it
opt_milestone_sun.fail: A cloud covers the sun just when you need it. You choose wrong and find out late, facing someone's brother-in-law's pen. Going back takes a while.
opt_milestone_sun.partial: The sun gives you the general direction, but the road you pick winds more than it should. You arrive fine, though feeling you've traced an S.
opt_milestone_sun.success: You read the shadow, work out the hour and know where your city lies. You take the road without hesitation. Two milestones on, a standing stone proves you right.
opt_milestone_sun.text: You pick the way by the sun
opt_mute_bread.fail: The boy eats all the bread, yours included, and runs off. You're left hungry, with the odd feeling you did right anyway.
opt_mute_bread.journal: A mute boy followed me half a day. We ate together and he showed me a road no stone marks.
opt_mute_bread.partial: You share the bread and the boy walks beside you, slower than suits you. You leave him at a farm gate where someone calls him by name.
opt_mute_bread.success: You eat sitting on a rock, without talking. Then the boy tugs your sleeve and leads you down a goat path that saves you a whole loop. At the crossroads, he vanishes.
opt_mute_bread.text: You share your bread and let him follow
opt_mute_lose.fail: You hide, and the boy sits down to wait in the middle of the road. A cart nearly runs him over. You come out to get him and he looks at you as if to say "found you."
opt_mute_lose.partial: You lose him, but half an hour later he's back, twenty paces behind, as if nothing happened. You give up: he's more stubborn than you.
opt_mute_lose.success: You hide behind a roadside tomb and wait. The boy passes, looks everywhere and turns back. You go on alone and fast.
opt_mute_lose.text: You lose him at a bend in the road
opt_mute_ribbon.fail: He wants to take you home so the family can thank you. You can't quite refuse. The mother feeds you and the grandmother gives advice. You leave late and full.
opt_mute_ribbon.journal: The brother of the girl from the crossroads found me on the road. He can't speak, but he can thank.
opt_mute_ribbon.partial: You recognize the ribbon and understand everything. The boy walks with you a long stretch, proud, and there's no making him go faster. You don't mind much.
opt_mute_ribbon.success: It's the ribbon of the girl you led by the hand. The boy is her brother and was looking for you with a gift: a bundle of figs and a shortcut. You follow without hesitation.
opt_mute_ribbon.text: He shows you a ribbon you recognize
opt_mute_send.fail: The boy won't go: he starts crying without a sound, which is worse. You end up walking him to the nearest farm, which is the other way.
opt_mute_send.partial: He goes, but it takes a while to convince him with gestures. When you finally move on, you keep glancing back.
opt_mute_send.success: You point the way back, firmly and a little sadly. The boy hesitates, nods and goes. A while later, from a hilltop, he waves.
opt_name_varus.fail: The Centurion doesn't know Varus. A long verification.
opt_name_varus.partial: The Centurion sends someone to check. You wait ten minutes.
opt_name_varus.success: The Centurion knows Varus. He accepts the delivery without further questions.
opt_negotiate.fail: They take your payment... and hold you another hour "just in case." Humiliating, but you leave in one piece, and their books now list you as a client.
opt_negotiate.journal: I paid the bandits' toll. Varus wouldn't approve. The bandits did.
opt_negotiate.partial: The negotiation is tense and the price unfair. But you pay and pass, and in the world of the roads that's already friendship.
opt_negotiate.success: You speak their language: respect, no fear. A few coins change hands and the leader studies you. "You get how the road works. Go." You just bought more than passage.
opt_night_pass.fail: This patrol has orders to stop EVERYTHING, badge or no badge. They hold you against a wall until they check with the central post. The night grows shorter, and so does your patience.
opt_night_pass.partial: The badge works, but the optio insists on escorting you three blocks "for your safety." Three blocks of talk about how badly the vigiles pay. You smile and nod. The clock runs.
opt_night_pass.success: The patrol's optio examines your badge by torchlight. "Urgent post at this hour? Go on. And tell your boss he owes us one." The vigiles respect those who work nights like them.
opt_night_pass.text: You show your messenger badge and your urgency
opt_northman_debt.fail: The northerner recognizes you and for a moment seems about to help. Then he remembers who pays him. He gives you a three-step head start, nothing more, and chases you half-heartedly. Three steps are enough, just.
opt_northman_debt.journal: Among Claudius's men was the northerner I said no to. He let me through. Some people respect a no more than a bought yes.
opt_northman_debt.partial: The northerner recognizes you and hesitates. He doesn't defend you, but he doesn't attack either: he stands still and opens a gap in the ring. You take it. Behind you, the other two shout at him in a language you don't understand.
opt_northman_debt.success: The one on the left is the northerner from the temple, who offered you money to see the seal. He knows you. "This one doesn't sell," he tells the others, lowering his sword. "Not worth it." You pass between them untouched.
opt_northman_debt.text: You spot the northerner among them
opt_oath_accept.fail: You stumble on the formula and Sextus has to feed you the words in front of the whole gate. The soldiers laugh. You swore, which is what counts. The plaque weighs the same.
opt_oath_accept.journal: I swore to carry the Tenth's post along the Appia. Gaius went back to his cohort. Two hundred names for one, and the one was the one that mattered.
opt_oath_accept.partial: The oath is long and in barracks Latin you don't fully follow. You repeat it anyway. Sextus smiles at your accent. They give you the plaque.
opt_oath_accept.success: You lay your hand on the standard and swear. Sextus hands you a bronze plaque with the bull of the Tenth. "With this you pass any post on the road." Gaius salutes you with a closed fist. It's the first time you've seen him standing tall.
opt_oath_accept.text: You swear to carry the Tenth's post
opt_oath_gaius.fail: Gaius gets so emotional he forgets the formula, and so do you. Sextus makes you repeat it three times. The soldiers applaud the third, more from fatigue than feeling.
opt_oath_gaius.partial: Gaius swears with a breaking voice and Sextus gives him time. The ceremony runs long, but nobody rushes anybody. Some things aren't rushed.
opt_oath_gaius.success: You and Gaius swear together, side by side. Sextus writes both names on the same tablet. Lucius, watching from the gate, wipes his eyes with his apron and says it's the smoke.
opt_oath_gaius.text: You ask Gaius to swear with you
opt_oath_terms.fail: Sextus doesn't like terms. "The legion doesn't negotiate with couriers." He takes you on anyway in the end, but he'll remind you of it on every job.
opt_oath_terms.partial: Sextus accepts half your terms. The other half he leaves for "when I know you better." Fair enough. You sign.
opt_oath_terms.success: You tell them you'll carry military post, but you won't inform on anyone on the list. Sextus considers it and nods: "A courier, not a spy. That works for me." You sign a contract nobody else on the Appia has.
opt_oath_terms.text: You accept, but on your terms
opt_oracle_bargain.fail: Your story doesn't interest her enough. The Sibyl returns to her murmuring as if you hadn't spoken. You leave with nothing, not even an echo.
opt_oracle_bargain.partial: The exchange half works: she gives you a prophecy, but wrapped in so many symbols it'll take the rest of the trip to decipher.
opt_oracle_bargain.success: You tell her something true from the road and she, pleased, returns a prophecy without riddles: a concrete warning about what lies ahead. A rare deal, well closed.
opt_oracle_bargain.text: You offer her a story in exchange for a clear prophecy
opt_oracle_birds.fail: She knows you and finds it insolent that you'd set yourself on her level. She says the verse backwards, on purpose, and slips into the cave. You spend twenty minutes turning it over. Some of it makes sense.
opt_oracle_birds.journal: The Sibyl of Cumae knew I'd read the augur's birds. She spoke to me plainly, like a colleague.
opt_oracle_birds.partial: She knows you and is amused, but gives nothing away: the verse and one clue, no more. "The rest you read yourself, since you know how." You leave with a riddle and the sense of having spoken as equals.
opt_oracle_birds.success: The Sibyl laughs with every tooth she has left. "The one who stole the augur's omen." She gives you the whole verse and then, in prose, what it means. The first time an oracle has saved you time.
opt_oracle_birds.text: "I read the birds once. Let's speak plainly."
opt_oracle_ignore.fail: The coin rolls away and vanishes among the cave's stones. The Sibyl laughs, a sound that follows you several more steps than you'd like.
opt_oracle_ignore.partial: You leave the coin and the old woman waves it off: she wants something more, something you don't have to give. You leave with the coin still in your hand.
opt_oracle_ignore.success: The coin clinks in her bowl and the Sibyl says nothing more. You go on, lighter of purse and of superstition.
opt_oracle_ignore.text: You leave her a small coin and walk on
opt_oracle_listen.fail: The prophecy is lost between the cave's echo and the wind. You leave understanding nothing, except that you lost a whole hour listening to echoes.
opt_oracle_listen.partial: You hear most of the prophecy before another traveler interrupts with his own question. You leave with half a message you may never need.
opt_oracle_listen.success: The full prophecy is long, strange and in several tongues. In the end, something in her words fits something you'll see later on the road. You leave thoughtful, not afraid.
opt_oracle_listen.text: You stay to hear the rest of the prophecy
opt_orders.fail: The centurion wants confirmation from above. You wait half an hour.
opt_orders.partial: The centurion checks with his second. They let you through after a wait.
opt_orders.success: The centurion reads the seal. "Free passage. May the gods go with you, messenger."
opt_orders.text: You show the sealed military orders
opt_pass_by.fail: You walk on, but his voice follows you farther than any storm. This delivery will arrive on time and weigh a great deal.
opt_pass_by.journal: I left a man lying on the road because the deadline ruled. The deadline. That's what I tell myself.
opt_pass_by.partial: You pass without looking. A hundred paces later, you look back anyway. He's still raising his hand.
opt_pass_by.success: You walk on, firm of step and lighter of conscience. The job is the job, you tell yourself. You almost believe it.
opt_pass_by.text: You look away and keep going — the message can't wait
opt_pay_marco.fail: Marco refuses the money with a disgust that hurts more than a punch. "Bribing colleagues now? Claudius teaches fast." He lets you pass only because fighting would turn his stomach. The dossier weighs double the rest of the way.
opt_pay_marco.partial: Marco takes the purse without looking at you and throws it into the Tiber. "There's your pay. Now we've both lost something tonight." He lets you pass. The splash follows you to the Basilica.
opt_pay_marco.success: "I don't want your money," says Marco, and looks at the river anyway. "I want to be able to tell Varus I didn't see you. Go quickly; I'm a bad liar." You cross. Some friendships survive even loyalties.
opt_pay_marco.text: You offer him all your pay to look away
opt_pay_respect.fail: You reach for a coin and find only one big one left. The augur looks at it. You look at him. The gods win the arm-wrestle. A pricey shadow.
opt_pay_respect.partial: You leave the coin, the augur murmurs something in Etruscan and splashes you with water from a dubious bowl. Protected or wet: one of the two, surely.
opt_pay_respect.success: The coin clinks on the altar and the augur nods slowly. "The gods watch those who watch." You go on with an odd calm, as if the air weighed less.
opt_pay_respect.text: You leave a coin on the crossroads altar
opt_pilgrim_act.fail: You kneel on the wrong side of the altar and a junior priest lectures you for five minutes on liturgy. The sweeper-who-doesn't-sweep studies you the whole time. You deliver anyway, but marked.
opt_pilgrim_act.partial: Your worshipper act is passable, though you nearly give yourself away by not knowing which side the offering goes on. An acolyte patiently corrects you. You reach the priest just in time.
opt_pilgrim_act.success: You buy two candles and a handful of incense, and go in murmuring prayers with the face of a repentant debtor. Nobody looks twice at a worshipper with money troubles. The priest knows you by Claudius's password.
opt_pilgrim_act.text: You go in as a worshipper, offering and all
opt_pilgrims_carry.fail: Halfway there the old man wakes, takes offense at being carried and gets down. He walks faster than you the rest of the stretch.
opt_pilgrims_carry.journal: I carried a pilgrim to the spring. Atia said Mercury keeps note of such things.
opt_pilgrims_carry.partial: You reach the spring with trembling arms and the old man complaining about how you carry. Atia smiles and gives you a sip from her wineskin.
opt_pilgrims_carry.success: The old man weighs less than your guilt would have. At the spring he recovers and blesses you three times. Atia touches your forehead: "Mercury protects those who carry more than letters."
opt_pilgrims_carry.text: You carry the old man to the next spring
opt_pilgrims_herbs.fail: You pick the wrong weed. The old man sneezes so hard he wakes right up and glares at you. It worked, though no one thanks you.
opt_pilgrims_herbs.partial: The herbs wake him, but also give him hiccups. The old man goes on between hiccups and blessings. Atia can't stop laughing.
opt_pilgrims_herbs.success: You gather wild mint and rue, crush them and hold them under his nose. The old man opens his eyes and asks for wine. Atia looks at you with something like wonder.
opt_pilgrims_herbs.text: You prepare herbs to revive him
opt_pilgrims_pass.fail: Further on the road narrows and the caravan catches up. You end up walking with them anyway, the old man now on a litter and you its fourth bearer.
opt_pilgrims_pass.partial: You move on, but the pilgrims' songs reach you for a good while. Every verse sounds a little like reproach.
opt_pilgrims_pass.success: Atia nods without reproach: "Each walks their own road." You keep a good pace and the pilgrim caravan falls behind, singing softly.
opt_pilgrims_pass.text: You excuse yourself and move on
opt_pilgrims_sibyl.fail: You tell the prophecy wrong, swapping two words. Atia corrects you with endless patience and makes you recite it whole before letting you go.
opt_pilgrims_sibyl.partial: Atia listens, frowns and asks you to repeat it. She gives you a cautious reading and leaves you thinking the rest of the way.
opt_pilgrims_sibyl.success: Atia hears the prophecy in silence, then explains it in two clear sentences, like opening a letter. She sends you off with a blessing and a short road to your destination.
opt_pilgrims_sibyl.text: You tell her what the Sibyl told you
opt_plague_around.fail: You get lost among olive terraces that all look alike. When you finally find the road, you're facing the black rope again, but from the inside.
opt_plague_around.partial: The hills are steeper than they promised and the shepherds' dogs don't want you near. You rejoin the road late, with a grumbling ankle.
opt_plague_around.success: You climb through the olive groves and skirt the village from above. From there you see shuttered houses and the smoke of burning herbs. You drop back to the road on the far side, healthy and silent.
opt_plague_around.text: You skirt the village by the hills
opt_plague_cross.fail: The old man at the rope raises the alarm and half the village comes out to stop anyone leaving. They lock you in a stable until the healthiest decides you have no fever.
opt_plague_cross.partial: You cross fast, but a woman asks for water from a doorway and you can't bring yourself to refuse. You come out fine, though her face follows you for several milestones.
opt_plague_cross.success: You wrap your face in a vinegar-soaked cloth and cut straight through, touching nothing and no one. On the far side, you scrub your hands in a stream until they sting.
opt_plague_letter.fail: The stone with the tablet lands in an irrigation ditch and you have to fish it out with a stick. You reach the road wet to the elbow, the plea half legible.
opt_plague_letter.journal: I carried the plea of a fever village. It weighed more than my package.
opt_plague_letter.partial: They give you the tablet, but writing it takes a while since no one quite remembers their letters. You wait on the healthy side of the rope, watching a village breathe slowly.
opt_plague_letter.success: The old man throws you a tablet tied to a stone: they're asking for doctors and grain. You stow it with your load. "The courier carries what's needed," you'd say, if Varus were watching.
opt_plague_letter.text: You offer to carry their plea to the magistrate
opt_poet_accept.fail: The poet reads you the whole poem, all eleven books. You're on the third when the sun sets. You part with a headache and a supporting role.
opt_poet_accept.partial: The verses aren't bad, but the poet stops every hundred paces to fix a syllable. By the end of the stretch you know more about meter than about your own road.
opt_poet_accept.success: The poet walks slowly, reciting hexameters about your sandals. Turns out he has a patron in the Senate he'll speak well of you to. You arrive late, but immortal.
opt_poet_accept.text: You let him come along and listen
opt_poet_outrun.fail: You run so hard you miss the turnoff. When you come back, the poet is waiting at the fork, delighted: "This is exactly what I needed for the fourth canto."
opt_poet_outrun.partial: You leave him behind, but the poet runs better than he recites. He catches you twice before giving up, panting verses about your ingratitude.
opt_poet_outrun.success: You walk faster, then trot, then run. The poet shouts that this, too, is poetry. You lose sight of him before the next rhyme.
opt_poet_outrun.text: You speed up until you lose him
opt_poet_story.fail: You tell a story and he recognizes it: "That's Ennius." He asks for another, your own this time. You find one, but it costs you a good stretch.
opt_poet_story.journal: I gave a poet a story from the road. If I ever read myself in verse, I'll deny everything.
opt_poet_story.partial: He likes the story but wants details: the color of the sky, what you felt. You make some up. You leave suspecting you'll come off better than you were.
opt_poet_story.success: You tell him something real from the road, in your own words. The poet scribbles frantically and lets you go without a fight. You gave him a poem; he gave you back silence.
opt_poet_story.text: You give him a story and go
opt_push.fail: A vendor trips you. The package falls; everyone stares.
opt_push.partial: You reach the other side with dirty clothes and a little late.
opt_push.success: You weave deftly between the vendors without losing time.
opt_push_on.fail: A league on, the ankle says enough and you sit wherever your body decides. You end up resting anyway, in the worst possible spot.
opt_push_on.journal: I kept going on a swollen ankle. The package arrived on time; I, only halfway.
opt_push_on.partial: You keep going, but the ankle charges interest on every descent. You reach the next stretch limping and in a foul mood.
opt_push_on.success: You grit your teeth and find the stride that hurts least. The body protests; the will commands. You didn't lose a minute.
opt_push_on.text: You ignore the pain and press on at full speed
opt_push_past.fail: The one-eyed old man turns out to have intact reflexes on his good side. He catches your arm and now the story starts from the beginning. With more detail.
opt_push_past.partial: You dodge him, but the veteran grabs your cloak and you have to leave it to wriggle free. You get it back on the other side, with mutual apologies.
opt_push_past.success: A feint east, a step west, and you're across. "Scout's reflexes!" shouts the old man, half offended, half impressed.
opt_push_past.text: You dodge him with a twist of the hips
opt_push_storm.fail: A tree crashes down yards away and the roar throws you into the mud. You keep going, but bruised, drenched and cursing in three dialects.
opt_push_storm.journal: I crossed the pass with the storm on top of me. I don't recommend it. I'd do it again.
opt_push_storm.partial: You press on, but the mountain takes its toll: you slip in the mud, and a blow to the ribs keeps you company the rest of the way.
opt_push_storm.success: You lean into the wind, reading the ground as the road taught you. Every step is a wager and you win them all. The storm falls behind; you don't.
opt_push_storm.text: You force the pass in the rain
opt_rank_only.fail: The Centurion insists. You end up naming Varus anyway.
opt_rank_only.partial: The Centurion frowns but accepts. The orders are valid.
opt_rank_only.success: The Centurion appreciates proper protocol. "As it should be." He lets you through.
opt_rank_only.text: "My orders are not to reveal the chain of command. The orders speak for themselves."
opt_read_birds.fail: You point at the sky confidently just as a whole flock changes course without warning. The augur smiles with every tooth he has left. You pay the coin. Just in case.
opt_read_birds.journal: I read the birds for the crossroads augur. He was left without an omen and I without a shadow.
opt_read_birds.partial: You read the birds your own way and walk on. The augur shouts something about the arrogance of youth. A technical draw.
opt_read_birds.success: You know the sky better than any crossroads augur: those crows are headed to the mill's watering trough, like every afternoon. "They flew against the sun because the mill is west," you say. The augur, for the first time in years, has no omen.
opt_read_birds.text: You look at the sky and read the birds yourself
opt_refuse_letter.fail: Two days later you hear: his delivery was a whole village's pay. It arrived late. No one blames you out loud.
opt_refuse_letter.partial: You walk away with his silence at your back. In this trade everything gets told: what you do and what you don't.
opt_refuse_letter.success: You leave him your canteen and half your bread, but not the letter. He nods: he understands the trade better than anyone. No grudge. No favor either.
opt_refuse_marco.fail: Marco grabs for the tube — half-heartedly, so he can tell Varus he tried. Two friends who no longer are wrestle. You win; you have more to lose. "Take care," he says at the end. And the worst part is he means it.
opt_refuse_marco.journal: Marco asked me for the dossier in Varus's name and friendship's. I said no to both. The bridge was never so long.
opt_refuse_marco.partial: Marco doesn't step aside right away: he reminds you of the night he saved you from the patrol in Ostia. Memory plays dirty. "I paid that debt," you lie, and pass. You both know you didn't.
opt_refuse_marco.success: Marco studies you a long time, looking for the kid he knew. He doesn't find him. "May the gods pay you well, because we won't charge you cheap." He steps aside. You cross the bridge dry-eyed by sheer pride.
opt_refuse_northman.fail: Your refusal comes out loud and two passersby turn around. The man vanishes instantly, leaving you as the madman shouting at thin air. Now half the street remembers your face and your satchel.
opt_refuse_northman.journal: A spy offered 200 denarii to look at Claudius's seal. I told him to move. My word has no price. Yet.
opt_refuse_northman.partial: He pushes, raising it to three hundred. Your silence bores him before your refusal does. "Everyone has a price, messenger. Yours will be in another coin." He leaves in no hurry.
opt_refuse_northman.success: The man smiles as if you'd passed an exam. "Claudius chooses well. Pity." He dissolves into the crowd. You get the feeling the offer was half test, half trap.
opt_refuse_seal.fail: Your refusal comes out louder than you meant, and half the inn learns you carry something valuable. You sleep with one eye open.
opt_refuse_seal.journal: Someone tried to buy my post at an inn. The seal isn't touched. Ever.
opt_refuse_seal.partial: You turn down the offer and he smiles like a man adding a name to a list. You leave the inn with a tense neck, but the seal intact.
opt_refuse_seal.success: You rise without drama and he doesn't insist: professionals know each other. On your way out, the innkeeper pours you better wine. The walls listen, and sometimes approve.
opt_refuse_seal.text: "The seal isn't touched." You get up from the table
opt_remember_apologize.fail: He listens halfway, then walks into the kitchen without a word. Dinner comes cold and late, and the bed has fleas. Some debts don't settle with wine.
opt_remember_apologize.journal: The traveler I left on the road now owns an inn. I apologized. He served me wine without spitting in it.
opt_remember_apologize.partial: He accepts the wine, not the apology. He serves your dinner, charges double and doesn't say a word. You leave at dawn, the debt half paid.
opt_remember_apologize.success: You tell him the truth: you had a package, and you were afraid. He listens, pours a cup of the wine you paid for and clinks yours. "A cart came by the next day. The gods looked after me and left you the guilt." You sleep well, for the first time in weeks.
opt_remember_apologize.text: You apologize and pay for his best wine
opt_remember_bargain.fail: You talk suppliers and he talks about his leg. Too late, you see he didn't want business. You leave with dinner paid and the account still open.
opt_remember_bargain.partial: You offer contacts; he asks for money. You strike an odd deal: you find him a supplier, he gives you a discount. Not friends, but no longer enemies.
opt_remember_bargain.success: You ask what a new inn lacks. Salt, he says, and a supplier who doesn't steal. You give him the name of an honest merchant from the network. He looks at you differently: you're not asking forgiveness, you're paying the debt in what he needs.
opt_remember_bargain.text: You offer to bring him something he needs
opt_remember_leave.fail: At the door his son is waiting; he doesn't know the story, but knows his father hates you. He trips you and laughs in your face. You get up and go on. This time you earned it.
opt_remember_leave.partial: You reach the door and he says, without raising his voice: "Passing by again." He doesn't stop you. It stops you anyway, for a long while, inside.
opt_remember_leave.success: You stand, leave two coins on the table and head out without looking back. No one follows. You press on through the night, faster than ever, carrying something heavy that isn't the package.
opt_remember_leave.text: You leave the food and go before he speaks
opt_report_merchant.fail: The checkpoint is run by a yawning guard who files your report in his memory, where things get lost. You lost time and gained enemies.
opt_report_merchant.journal: I reported a smuggler at the checkpoint. The Legions are grateful. The roads have memory, and not all of it kind.
opt_report_merchant.partial: The report comes too late: the cart changed routes. Still, the decurion records your goodwill. And the road's merchants, your face.
opt_report_merchant.success: The decurion takes down your description with military precision. "Rome thanks its eyes on the road." He seals you a safe-conduct for the area. On the other side of the favor, someone curses your name.
opt_report_merchant.text: You note the cart and report it at the next checkpoint
opt_respectful_delivery.fail: Nerves trip up your greeting and Claudius raises an eyebrow worth a speech. "Tell Varus that even his victories are clumsy." The letter changes hands anyway. Cutting words come free to the loser.
opt_respectful_delivery.partial: Your protocol is correct, though your hand trembles a hair at the end. Claudius notices — he notices everything — but says nothing. Today he doesn't bite. Today he just collects his defeat.
opt_respectful_delivery.success: Perfect protocol: the right distance, the right bow, the letter in both hands. Claudius takes it and something like respect crosses his face. "Varus trains well," he concedes. From an enemy, that's a decoration.
opt_respectful_delivery.text: You deliver with full protocol, not a word too many
opt_rest.fail: You oversleep under the shifting sun. You wake with a start, ankle better and schedule worse.
opt_rest.partial: The rest half helps: the swelling goes down, but every slope reminds you. You go on, slower and wiser.
opt_rest.success: You bind your ankle with a strip of tunic and sleep in an olive tree's shade. When you wake, the pain is a memory and the road is where you left it.
opt_rest.text: You rest a few hours before going on
opt_return_coin.fail: The coin slips from your hand on the steps and rolls three steps down. A slave picks it up and gives it to Claudius, who barely smiles. "Clumsy even at paying back." Settled anyway. With an audience.
opt_return_coin.journal: I gave Claudius back the northerner's coin. I owe him nothing now, not even that glance.
opt_return_coin.partial: Claudius takes the coin without looking and hands it to his slave, like a tip. The gesture stings, but the debt is settled. You walk down the steps lighter.
opt_return_coin.success: Along with the letter, you leave in his hand the coin his man gave you at the temple. Claudius looks at it a long while. "Settled," he says, and for the first time speaks to you as an equal. You closed the account before he could.
opt_return_coin.text: You give back the coin the northerner paid you
opt_revenge_fight.fail: This time numbers won. They shake down your body and your bag, though what mattered was well hidden. The lesson hurts.
opt_revenge_fight.partial: The fight is ugly and even. You get through, but you leave your own blood at the toll you refused to pay.
opt_revenge_fight.success: They didn't expect the runner to throw the first punch. Surprise is worth two men. When the dust settles, the pass is yours, and so is the story.
opt_revenge_fight.text: This time you don't run: you fight
opt_revenge_ghost.fail: A skinny camp dog sniffs you out and barks. You run again, and again you barely make it. This is becoming a habit.
opt_revenge_ghost.partial: You dodge them by crawling along a dry ditch. It works, but you come out smelling of old mud, hours lost.
opt_revenge_ghost.success: Flat on the ground, the patience of stone. You watch them pass yards away, hear their bad jokes, and when the road clears you're part of the afternoon. They never knew.
opt_revenge_ghost.text: You saw them first: you melt into the terrain
opt_revenge_pay.fail: You pay, and on top of that they make you wait while they "verify" you're not carrying more. You leave lighter of purse and of patience.
opt_revenge_pay.partial: You pay double what it would have cost the first time. The leader lets you know it with a smile. An expensive lesson, but a complete one.
opt_revenge_pay.success: The leader counts the coins twice and nods. "You learn fast." They let you pass with something like respect. The road has its rules.
opt_revenge_pay.text: You pay the toll... with a surcharge
opt_ride_contraband.fail: Midway, an axle gives under the weight of the mysterious tarp. You help repair it — what choice is there — and arrive with dirty hands in more ways than one.
opt_ride_contraband.journal: I traveled fast in a cart customs never saw. I didn't see anything either. That's how it works.
opt_ride_contraband.partial: The trip is fast but tense: two checkpoints passed with stony smiles. You climb down with numb legs and a racing pulse.
opt_ride_contraband.success: The cart flies down the road and the merchant proves good company: he knows every inn and every bribable guard on the way. You arrive fresh, fast and with new acquaintances.
opt_ride_contraband.text: You climb aboard and admire the scenery
opt_rival_partner.fail: His pace breaks you halfway. He offers to wait; you tell him to go on. You arrive later, alone, and he's already ordered you some food. A kindness that stings worse than any defeat.
opt_rival_partner.partial: He's faster than you, and you have to push to avoid looking foolish. You arrive spent but on time. Tomorrow your legs will ache with pride.
opt_rival_partner.success: Two couriers at a trot cover more ground than one: you take turns setting the pace and keeping watch. You reach the way station with the sun still high. You part as colleagues, not rivals.
opt_rival_partner.text: You suggest finishing the stretch together
opt_rival_shortcut.fail: The shortcut was good last year. This year there's a new fence and an old dog. You get back to the road half an hour down and one pair of trousers short. He meant well.
opt_rival_shortcut.journal: The rival courier I helped paid me back with a shortcut. In this trade, debts are settled in roads.
opt_rival_shortcut.partial: The shortcut exists, but it has a stream he forgot to mention. You cross with the package on your head. You still gain time, soaked to the waist.
opt_rival_shortcut.success: He shows you a shepherds' path that cuts the hill in half and appears on no Guild map. You reach the other side an hour ahead. "We're even," he says, and leaves whistling.
opt_rival_shortcut.text: You take the shortcut he offers
opt_rival_warning.fail: He talks so much you both lose a quarter hour, and he's wrong about the one thing that matters: the patrol was before the bridge, not after. You're held up anyway. He owed you one, and paid half.
opt_rival_warning.partial: He knows some things and guesses others. Half the warnings come true. The other half make you careful for nothing, which isn't so bad either.
opt_rival_warning.success: He tells you everything: where the new patrol is, which inn pads the bill, which bridge charges extra toll. That's worth more than a shortcut. You travel the rest of the day without a single surprise.
opt_rival_warning.text: You ask him what lies ahead on the road
opt_rooftops.fail: A short jump ends in an awning that breaks your fall and wakes half the block. You run through shouts and dogs until you lose yourself. Your ankle remembers every tile.
opt_rooftops.partial: The rooftop road works until a tile gives way. You grab a cornice, heart in your mouth, and carry on more slowly. Rome at night doesn't forgive distraction.
opt_rooftops.success: The rooftops of the Subura are a road few know and fewer dare. You run above sleeping Rome, leaping alleys, the moon your accomplice. Below, the vigiles' torches search for someone who's no longer there.
opt_rooftops.text: Over the rooftops of the slums
opt_run.fail: You run, trip, roll down a slope and land in a stream. You got away by a miracle, and now they know your face.
opt_run.partial: You escape through the hills, losing your breath and a scrap of cloak to a bramble. Free, but these people don't forgive a runner.
opt_run.success: You run as if Mercury himself were pushing you. When the shouts fall behind, you know two things: you're alive, and they have long memories.
opt_salt_decline.fail: The thieves they mentioned are real, and seeing you carry nothing they charge you anyway, "a walking toll." They take two coins and teach you a lesson about company.
opt_salt_decline.partial: You go on alone and the stretch turns out longer and dustier than you thought. When the cart passes you, the salt carriers wave with pity.
opt_salt_decline.success: You leave the salt to them and the road to you. Half an hour later they're out of sight, ditties and all. Your stride outpaces any ox.
opt_salt_decline.text: You thank them and walk on
opt_salt_ride.fail: A wheel sinks in a pothole and you spend a good while pushing. The salt carriers promise next time they'll take you for free. They already were.
opt_salt_ride.partial: The stretch is quiet and the cart slower than a fasting priest. You arrive rested, lips cracked with salt and patience worn thin.
opt_salt_ride.success: The cart is slow but your legs rest, and the salt carriers sing ditties that make even the oxen laugh. Nothing gets stolen. You climb down with a handful of salt as a gift.
opt_salt_ride.text: You climb aboard and guard the salt
opt_salt_trade.fail: Your news is stale: the cheap post has a new collector. The salt carriers take offense, and their shortcut, mysteriously, ends in a marsh.
opt_salt_trade.partial: The shortcut exists, but their donkeys use it too. You make good time, dodging what the donkeys leave behind.
opt_salt_trade.success: You tell them which toll post charges least this week. Grateful, they point out a salt carriers' path that cuts off a whole bend of the road.
opt_salt_trade.text: You trade them news for a shortcut
opt_salute_varus.fail: "Commander," you say. Varus walks past as if the wind had spoken. The new ones hurry after him. You stand staring at the river, Claudius's livery heavy as mail. You chose. It costs. It costs every day.
opt_salute_varus.partial: Your greeting hangs in the bridge air. Varus nods once, a movement of millimeters, and passes. The new ones avoid your eyes. The bridge was never so long or so narrow.
opt_salute_varus.success: "Commander," you say, and the word comes out whole. Varus stops for a second. "Messenger," he answers — not your name, your trade — and walks on. It's cold, but it's a greeting. From Varus, after all, it's nearly a hug.
opt_same_hour.fail: The kid gets scared of Petro's doorman and comes back with the envelope. You end up making both deliveries anyway, running between villas like in your worst days. It works, but next time you pick a better helper.
opt_same_hour.partial: The timing is nearly perfect — the kid dawdles buying chestnuts with your advance. The two senators take the blow half an hour apart: enough for the effect, not enough to conspire. A narrow pass.
opt_same_hour.success: The kid delivers at Petro's at the exact moment you deliver at Claudius's: neither can warn the other, neither can negotiate first. When the Widow hears of the choreography, she smiles: "Hired. For life." In the Subura, that's a noble title.
opt_same_hour.text: You hire a Subura kid and you deliver at the same hour
opt_seal.fail: Lucius says the seal could be forged. You'll have to convince him another way.
opt_seal.partial: Lucius studies the seal a long while, but finally accepts.
opt_seal.success: Lucius recognizes the seal at once. He takes it, no fuss.
opt_seal.text: You show Varus's seal on the message
opt_seals.fail: The doorman says he needs spoken confirmation. You'll have to wait.
opt_seals.partial: The doorman goes to check. You wait five minutes at the entrance.
opt_seals.success: The Senate seal changes everything. The doorman steps aside immediately.
opt_seals.text: You show all three seals — the Senate's included
opt_search_deserter_way.fail: The barrel door is bricked up. You retrace your steps and run into the tail of the patrol. They look at you, but don't stop you. The shortcut is gone; you aren't.
opt_search_deserter_way.journal: I used the same route I showed the deserter on the road. Some shortcuts are only known to those who've helped someone escape.
opt_search_deserter_way.partial: The fuller's route is still there, though the fuller now has a dog. You calm it with half a loaf. You arrive a little late and smelling of dye.
opt_search_deserter_way.success: The deserter you gave your cloak to told you, before leaving, how to dodge a search: through the fuller's yard and the barrel door. It works in Rome too. You reach the camp without crossing a single helmet.
opt_search_deserter_way.text: You use the route the other deserter taught you
opt_search_roofs.fail: A loose tile leaves you hanging from a gutter right above the patrol. They see you. You have to explain you're a courier and rooftops are faster. They half believe you and walk you two blocks.
opt_search_roofs.partial: The rooftops work until an old woman sees you pass her window and screams. You come down fast and finish on foot. Luckily, the patrol is far away.
opt_search_roofs.success: You climb an insula's stairs and run across half the Subura, the hanging laundry your accomplice. You come down two blocks from the camp. The patrol never looked up.
opt_search_roofs.text: You cross the Subura by the rooftops
opt_search_talk.fail: The optio distrusts the helpful. He searches your whole satchel. The letter isn't there: it's in your sandal. He lets you go with a scowl.
opt_search_talk.partial: The optio doesn't need a courier, but he likes you. He lets you through unsearched. The chat costs a little time, no more.
opt_search_talk.success: The optio loves someone offering help instead of hiding. He asks you to take a notice to the camp, the very place you were headed. You pass with an escort and permission.
opt_search_talk.text: You ask the optio if he needs a courier
opt_search_wait.fail: You wait so long the patrol circles the block and comes back. They ask what you're doing there. "Waiting." They glance through your satchel. The letter is in your sandal. You pass.
opt_search_wait.partial: The patrol takes forever. As it passes, a soldier looks at your face for one long second. He says nothing. You're through.
opt_search_wait.success: The patrol walks past, busy with a fishmonger yelling at them. You fill your flask three times. When they finish the street, you carry on calmly.
opt_search_wait.text: You wait at a fountain until they're done
opt_sell_secret.fail: Nerves make you forget half the details the moment you deliver. But not the names: Claudius, Petro, the network. The names are enough. The Widow of the Subura finishes any story if you bring her the beginning.
opt_sell_secret.journal: I read what I shouldn't have and saw what nobody sees: a gold mine. Not Varus's, not Claudius's. It's the carrier's.
opt_sell_secret.partial: You memorize the essentials — names, sums, dates — and deliver with the seal passably mended. That night you don't sleep: in your head, two senators fight and you charge admission.
opt_sell_secret.success: You're a messenger: memorizing text is your trade. You engrave every word, mend the seal flawlessly and hand it to Tiro with a blank face. The letter, intact. The secret, yours. In the Subura you know an unmarked tavern where this is worth more than Claudius's villa.
opt_sell_secret.text: This is worth a fortune in the Subura
opt_servant_entrance.fail: The service usher turns out more ceremonious than the main protocol: he announces you at full voice in the scribes' hall. "The courier of Senator Claudius!" All that hiding for this. Rome doesn't allow anonymous deliveries. Ever.
opt_servant_entrance.partial: The service entrance exists but it's guarded: fifteen minutes of checks. You finally deliver, discreet as you wanted. Claudius will frown at the low profile. Let him.
opt_servant_entrance.success: A veteran usher leads you down the scribes' corridor, where nobody looks at anybody because everyone carries secrets. You deliver without witnesses or theater. Claudius wanted a show; you preferred results. There'll be time to argue about it.
opt_servant_entrance.text: You ask for the service entrance — no audience
opt_service_door.fail: The cook turns out to be the villa's official gossip. He sneaks you in, but tomorrow the whole household will know "a mysterious messenger" visited the master at night. Discretion: zero.
opt_service_door.partial: The cook makes you earn entry by hearing out his complaints about the steward. You get in through the kitchens, yes, but knowing the life and works of every servant in the villa.
opt_service_door.success: Ten minutes on the price of garum and the cook already considers you decent folk. He sneaks you through the kitchens: you enter the villa smelling of bay leaves, your face unknown to any guard.
opt_service_door.text: You chat with the cook at the service door
opt_sewer_path.fail: You take the wrong branch and end up under the cattle market, which drips what cattle drip. You climb out the first grate that gives. Your tunic will need a funeral.
opt_sewer_path.partial: The tunnel works, though two rats the size of cats dispute your passage and a surprise waterfall baptizes you. You make it. Wet, but you make it.
opt_sewer_path.success: You descend into Rome's bowels with a torch stolen from an altar. The Cloaca Maxima smells of digested empire, but it's straight, fast and utterly deserted. You come out two blocks from your destination, smelling of history.
opt_sewer_path.text: The Cloaca Maxima has no curfew
opt_shepherd_judge.fail: You rule for the man the ear mark favors. The other shepherd appeals to his dog, who doesn't accept your jurisdiction. You leave with heels safe and cloak bitten.
opt_shepherd_judge.journal: I judged a case over a ram in the middle of a drove road. The ram didn't appeal.
opt_shepherd_judge.partial: Your ruling convinces one and offends the other, who walks off muttering. You pass, with one shepherd who'll remember you fondly and one who won't.
opt_shepherd_judge.success: You check the ear mark, hear both sides and rule like Solomon, but in Latin: this season the ram covers both men's ewes. They shake hands and clear the way.
opt_shepherd_judge.text: You judge the case like a praetor
opt_shepherd_wade.fail: A ram, not the disputed one, takes you for a rival. He charges you twice, methodically. You reach the other side backwards and learning.
opt_shepherd_wade.partial: You get through, but the sheep bunch up and carry you sideways a stretch. You come out with wool stuck all over you, smelling of the pen for the rest of the day.
opt_shepherd_wade.success: You wade through the sheep as through waves, pushing with your knees and never looking back. On the far side, the shepherds are still shouting. They never noticed you passed.
opt_shepherd_wade.text: You push your way through the sheep
opt_shepherd_wait.fail: When they finally split the flocks, the ram bolts and everything mixes again. One shepherd offers you cheese as consolation. You take it: it's good cheese.
opt_shepherd_wait.partial: They split the flocks with shouts and sticks, sheep escaping and coming back. You get through when there's no light left for anything else.
opt_shepherd_wait.success: The dogs do the work the shepherds don't: in two hours every sheep is back on its side. The ram stays in the middle, dignified, choosing no one. You pass amid bleating.
opt_shepherd_wait.text: You wait while they sort the flocks
opt_shortcut.fail: Memory fails you: the slope path ended in an old rockslide. You retrace your steps with the storm laughing overhead.
opt_shortcut.partial: The detour works, though the fog makes you doubt two forks. You reach the other side with damp clothes and dry spirits.
opt_shortcut.success: The east slope cuts the wind like a wall. The detour is longer in steps but shorter in trouble. Well played.
opt_shortcut.text: You know a detour along the slope
opt_show_seal.fail: While he looks at the seal, his fingers brush the letter a moment too long. You yank it away. He pays anyway, but the doubt stays: did he manage to read something against the light?
opt_show_seal.journal: I let a northern spy see the seal on Claudius's letter. Two hundred denarii for two seconds of wax. Dirt cheap. Ruinously expensive.
opt_show_seal.partial: The man studies the seal through a lens that appears from his sleeve and disappears again. He pays, but on his way out he says: "Tell your master the north reads too." A free chill.
opt_show_seal.success: You show him the seal for exactly two seconds. It's enough for him: "Black wax. So it's true." He pays without haggling and vanishes. You've just confirmed something to someone, and you don't even know what.
opt_show_seal.text: You show him the seal — only the seal
opt_sibyl_ask.fail: The priest knows no more than you, but won't admit it. He gives you a very long, very wrong interpretation. You drop it at the first bend.
opt_sibyl_ask.partial: He explains it, priest-style: with three detours through the genealogy of the gods. You keep the useful part. The morning is gone.
opt_sibyl_ask.success: The priest is moved that someone else has heard the Sibyl and explains the whole verse with maps drawn in the dirt. You leave with the road clear and an ally at the shrine.
opt_sibyl_ask.text: You ask the priest what it means
opt_sibyl_ignore.fail: You laugh, carry on, and at the first bridge you meet what the verse foretold: an overturned cart. You have to go around. Far away, the Sibyl laughs too.
