opt_sibyl_ignore.partial: You keep to your route and remember the verse at every crossroads. Nothing bad happens, but you travel looking over your shoulder.
opt_sibyl_ignore.success: Verses are verses and the road is the road. You carry on as planned and it goes well. Maybe the Sibyl meant another messenger.
opt_sibyl_ignore.text: You laugh at the verse and go your way
opt_sibyl_trust.fail: You misread the verse and follow the wrong stream. An hour later you're back at the shrine. The priest looks at you and says: "The other stream." Everyone knew but you.
opt_sibyl_trust.journal: The Sibyl's verse came true at a roadside shrine. I heeded it and wasn't wrong.
opt_sibyl_trust.partial: The verse says the road of water, and the water is a marsh. You slog through it. You arrive, though, without meeting a soul. The Sibyl never promised comfort.
opt_sibyl_trust.success: "When the stone speaks, take the road of water." At the shrine stands a carved stele, and beside it, a stream. You follow it. It takes you straight to your destination, past no patrols. The Sibyl didn't lie.
opt_sibyl_trust.text: You follow the verse to the letter
opt_silence.fail: Claudius suspects your hesitation, but accepts the answer.
opt_silence.partial: Claudius gives you a long look. Finally he nods.
opt_silence.success: Claudius nods, satisfied. "Well trained. Varus chooses well."
opt_silence.text: "No one, Senator. It's between you and the sender."
opt_sister_move.fail: The cart gets stuck in the back ditch and you lose an hour freeing it. You save everything, but at dawn. The men across the street had fallen asleep. Lucky for you they're poor guards.
opt_sister_move.partial: You get nearly everything out, but the cart squeaks and the men across the street see it go. Now they know Livia hid something. The house stands; so does the suspicion.
opt_sister_move.success: You load the cold oven's contents, the accounts and the silver into a hay cart and take it out the back. If they burn the house, they burn walls. The torch men never learn there's nothing left to find.
opt_sister_move.text: You help Livia move the valuables out tonight
opt_sister_neighbors.fail: The neighbors are scared and three show up. The arsonists burn the back shed before being chased off. The house is saved; the winter firewood isn't.
opt_sister_neighbors.partial: You gather eight neighbors, not twenty. It's enough: the arsonists try the back once, see people and leave. Nobody slept, but the house stands.
opt_sister_neighbors.success: You knock door to door. By nightfall there are twenty neighbors with clubs in Livia's yard, singing to stay awake. The torch men leave without lighting them. The house greets dawn intact.
opt_sister_neighbors.text: You gather the neighbors to stand guard
opt_sister_scare.fail: They don't listen: they shove you. You end up on the ground with a split lip, but the shouting wakes the street. They run off. You won by losing.
opt_sister_scare.partial: They listen and laugh, but move from the door to the corner. They spend the night watching you and you watching them. Nobody lights anything.
opt_sister_scare.success: You cross the street and stand before them, hands in plain view. You tell them the inn has an owner, friends and a courier who knows their faces. They exchange looks, get up and leave. The torches stay on the ground.
opt_smuggler_jump.fail: You jump and hit a hidden rock. You reach the bank with a swollen elbow and one side of the package wet. The three laugh from the bridge. They don't follow: the river already collected.
opt_smuggler_jump.partial: The jump goes well, the river less so: a current drags you and one corner of the package gets wet. You crawl ashore coughing water, the wrapping set out to dry in the sun.
opt_smuggler_jump.success: You jump before they grab you. The river is cold and fast, and you sidestroke with the package in your free hand. You climb out half a mile downstream, soaked and free. Up top, the three are still arguing.
opt_smuggler_jump.text: You jump in the river and swim, package held high
opt_smuggler_legion.fail: There's no patrol in sight and they know it. They shove you against the railing and search your bag. They take your coin purse and leave the package. What saved you is they didn't know what it was.
opt_smuggler_legion.partial: You mention the legion and they hesitate just long enough for you to pass. They shout a promise at your back. For now, the bridge is behind you.
opt_smuggler_legion.success: You nod toward the hill where, sure enough, a helmet glints. The three exchange looks and decide the month can wait. "Another day, messenger." Here's hoping there isn't one.
opt_smuggler_legion.text: You warn them the legion patrols this bridge
opt_smuggler_pay.fail: You pay, but the smallest one also wants an apology. You kneel on the bridge with carts rolling past. It hurts more than the money. Account closed, pride wide open.
opt_smuggler_pay.journal: I paid for the month in jail of the merchant I reported. The account at the docks is closed.
opt_smuggler_pay.partial: They ask for more than you have and take what you have. You're without a denarius until the next way station. The account, at least, is closed.
opt_smuggler_pay.success: You work out a month's wages and pay without haggling. The tallest counts, nods and shakes your hand. "Account closed. Now you're one who pays." At the docks, that's worth something.
opt_smuggler_pay.text: You pay the month and settle up
opt_soldier_salute.fail: "The Twelfth? The Twelfth were useless!" You picked the rival legion. The story now covers why his legion was better. With demonstrations.
opt_soldier_salute.partial: You get the legion wrong but the respect right. The old man corrects you patiently and lets you through anyway.
opt_soldier_salute.success: You recognize the scar of the XII Fulminata and salute him properly. The veteran straightens three inches, returns the salute and steps aside, martial. "Free passage for the post."
opt_soldier_salute.text: You stand to attention and salute his rank
opt_speed.fail: A legionary shouts "Halt!" — you end up explaining everything anyway.
opt_speed.partial: They see you, but you're already far off. No one gives chase.
opt_speed.success: You slip through the shadows before they notice you.
opt_speed.text: You quicken your pace before they spot you
opt_spy_drop_it.fail: Just as you let it go, someone points at you from a window. You don't know if they saw you pick up the scroll or drop it, but you walk faster the rest of the afternoon.
opt_spy_drop_it.partial: You drop it, but a boy in the square picks it up before you're fully away. A few blocks on, you wonder what trouble the boy just walked into.
opt_spy_drop_it.success: You let it go exactly where it fell and walk off without suspicious haste. No one saw you pick it up, no one sees you leave it. As if it never happened.
opt_spy_drop_it.text: You drop it where it was and leave fast
opt_spy_known_face.fail: You point too soon and he sees you. He slips between the stalls and you spend half an hour explaining to a suspicious watchman why you hold someone else's scroll. They believe you, in the end. They don't find him.
opt_spy_known_face.journal: The scroll in the square was dropped by the same man who tried to buy my seal at the inn. I pointed him out to the watch.
opt_spy_known_face.partial: You spot him and keep him in sight while you look for a guard. When you come back with one, the man is gone. You hand over the scroll with a precise description. It's something.
opt_spy_known_face.success: It's him: the clean-handed man who offered you the pouch at the inn. You point him out to the first watchman, scroll in hand. They nab him at the corner. The optio thanks you and asks if you'd like to work for them.
opt_spy_known_face.text: You spot the northerner in the crowd
opt_spy_read.fail: The seal breaks badly and it's obvious someone opened it. You leave it where it was anyway, hoping no one links the mess to you.
opt_spy_read.journal: I opened a scroll that wasn't mine in an empty square. What I read, I won't tell. Not even here.
opt_spy_read.partial: You get through half before nearby footsteps force you to snap it shut. The seal ends up a little crooked, and half the message makes no clear sense.
opt_spy_read.success: You break the seal with a surgeon's fingers and reclose it without a trace. What you read wasn't meant for you, but now you know it anyway. You keep quiet, and the scroll where it was.
opt_spy_read.text: You open it for a second, just to see what it is
opt_spy_return.fail: The guard post happens to be empty today. You carry the scroll a longer stretch than you wanted, ever more uneasy about whatever you're holding.
opt_spy_return.partial: The guard takes a while to decide whether the find is his business or another post's. You end up waiting while two officers argue jurisdiction.
opt_spy_return.success: The officer on duty takes the scroll with sudden seriousness and thanks you with a gesture that says more than his words. Whatever it was, it's not your problem anymore.
opt_spy_return.text: You hand it in at the first guard post you find
opt_stealth.fail: A dry branch snaps underfoot. "There! In the trees!" You end up explaining to the centurion why an honest messenger avoids checkpoints.
opt_stealth.partial: The detour exists, but it's all thorns and loose stone. You reach the other side scratched, your pride half intact.
opt_stealth.success: You slip through the brush like one more shadow of dusk. When you rejoin the road, the checkpoint is behind you and no one saw a thing.
opt_stealth.text: You skirt the checkpoint by a side path
opt_storm_ridge.fail: No storm this time, and you get cocky. A stretch crumbles under your sandal and you slide down on your backside, hugging the package. You reach the bottom scraped but whole. The mountain remembers you too.
opt_storm_ridge.journal: I crossed the rockslide by the ridge. After that storm, a few still stones don't scare me.
opt_storm_ridge.partial: The ridge holds, though a loose stone makes you dance one long second over the void. Your body remembered the storm before you did. You get across, knees protesting.
opt_storm_ridge.success: The ridge is narrow and the wind pushes, but you've crossed a pass with the sky falling on you. This is a stroll. You're down the other side before the muleteers finish arguing about the old road.
opt_storm_ridge.text: You take the ridge, like that stormy night
opt_subura_whistle.fail: You whistle well, but the boy is new and no one taught him the signal. He keeps running. An old woman on a balcony points the way, and ten minutes later you find him counting your money. He hands it back looking offended.
opt_subura_whistle.locked: Only those the Subura respects know that signal.
opt_subura_whistle.partial: The whistle carries, but the boy hesitates: he knows the signal, not your face. He comes halfway, tosses the purse at your feet and vanishes. One coin short. The price of not being known on sight yet.
opt_subura_whistle.success: Two short notes and a long one. The boy stops dead mid-alley, turns, takes a good look at you and walks back holding out the purse. "Didn't know you were one of ours." Now half the block knows.
opt_swim.fail: A sunken log strikes your legs and for an instant it's all water and panic. You leave the river without knowing how. The package... better check it.
opt_swim.partial: The current drags you farther downstream than planned. You crossed, yes, but now you must walk back along the bank, chilled to the bone.
opt_swim.success: The water is freezing and the current pushes, but your arms know their work. You climb out dripping, the package dry above your head like a trophy.
opt_swim.text: You swim the river, package held high
opt_take_bribe.fail: When the man finishes, you notice the seal didn't close properly. You got paid, yes, but now you deliver a letter that screams it was opened.
opt_take_bribe.journal: I let a stranger read someone else's post for a pouch of silver. The seal was intact in the end. I wasn't, quite.
opt_take_bribe.partial: He reads the letter, but the seal ends up... convincing, not perfect. With luck, no one looks twice. With luck.
opt_take_bribe.success: The man reads fast, memorizes, and refolds the letter with a surgeon's fingers. The seal isn't even damaged. The pouch is nicely heavy. What your conscience weighs is your business.
opt_take_bribe.text: You take the pouch and look away for a minute
opt_take_letter.fail: His recipient turned out to live at the far end of town, past two wrong doors and a dog with opinions. You came through, but the favor cost a fortune.
opt_take_letter.journal: I carried a fallen colleague's delivery along with mine. That's what the Guild is, even if he's from another network.
opt_take_letter.partial: You carry both deliveries, though the detour costs you dearly in time. Your colleague swears to repay it. Ankles heal; debts of honor don't.
opt_take_letter.success: You deliver both letters and go back for him with a carter friend. By sunset every messenger on the road knows your name. That coin never runs out.
opt_take_letter.text: You take his letter — today him, tomorrow you
opt_tax_dodge.fail: A farm watchdog gives you away halfway. You return to the tollhouse escorted by its barking and end up paying double for the shame.
opt_tax_dodge.partial: The field's mud slows you more than expected and you lose a sandal in the attempt. You reach the other side one foot bare, your dignity muddied.
opt_tax_dodge.success: The freshly plowed field hides your steps better than any excuse. You rejoin the road three hundred yards on, sandals dirty and the toll still in your pocket.
opt_tax_dodge.text: You skirt the tollhouse through the field
opt_tax_patron.fail: The collector knows the house... and owes it money. He holds you up out of pure spite until his superior arrives, who knows whom to stay on good terms with. You pass with apologies, and late.
opt_tax_patron.locked: No patrician lends you their name yet.
opt_tax_patron.partial: The name works, but the collector wants it in writing. You show him the commission letter; he reads it twice, sniffs it, and finally lets you pass. A quarter hour to confirm you weren't lying.
opt_tax_patron.success: You say the house's name like someone telling the time. The collector rubs something off his tablet with his thumb, seals your load without looking, and even wishes you a good trip. Some family names outweigh any toll.
opt_tax_patron.text: You name the patrician house that hired you
opt_tax_pay.fail: The collector finds a new tax he invented this very morning. You pay twice for the same crossing and learn that wax can be rewritten.
opt_tax_pay.partial: You pay, but the collector takes forever to record each coin, as if he mistrusted numbers. You leave free and bored.
opt_tax_pay.success: You pay without a face and the collector, surprised to argue with no one for once, even marks the shortest road on his tablet. A true rarity.
opt_tax_pay.text: You pay the full toll without arguing
opt_tax_permit.fail: The safe-conduct is from a guild that ceased to exist two years ago. The collector laughs, not unkindly, and charges you the full toll for the cheek.
opt_tax_permit.partial: The collector studies the safe-conduct a long while, comparing it with an old one he keeps. In the end he lets you pass, not without noting the delay.
opt_tax_permit.success: The collector recognizes the messengers' Guild seal and needs nothing more. He gives you an almost respectful wave, and the way is clear.
opt_tell_varus.fail: Varus is in a meeting and you have to wait. When you finally tell him, your window of daylight is closing. "Run," is all he says. The important part got said.
opt_tell_varus.journal: I told Varus about Claudius before going. If this goes wrong, at least I won't sink alone.
opt_tell_varus.partial: Varus frowns a long while. "I don't like it. Go anyway — better inside than out. But this stays between us." His trust weighs as much as his doubt.
opt_tell_varus.success: Varus listens without interrupting, the way he listens: with his whole body. "Go," he says at last. "Listen more than you talk. And remember who taught you to walk these streets." You leave the barracks lighter.
opt_tell_varus.text: You go in and tell Varus everything
opt_temple_cooperate.fail: While they search your bag, they find the real offering in another traveler's hands. It gets sorted out, but you lost a whole half hour to other people's suspicions.
opt_temple_cooperate.partial: They check every pocket twice, uneasy at finding nothing. They let you go without a clear apology, but at least without chains.
opt_temple_cooperate.success: The search is quick and clean: your bag holds only what it should. The priest apologizes with exaggerated formality and blesses you, just in case.
opt_temple_cooperate.text: You stay and let them search your bag
opt_temple_flee.fail: You run and slam right into a temple guard coming to see the fuss. You end up explaining your hurry with less conviction than you'd like.
opt_temple_flee.partial: You escape the group, but a worshipper spots you later in the square and remarks loudly that you "ran funny" outside the temple.
opt_temple_flee.success: You vanish into the crowd in the forecourt before the priest's finger finishes pointing. No one follows you. Neither does your conscience, much.
opt_temple_flee.text: You slip away before they point at you
opt_temple_identify.fail: You point at the wrong person and the real thief uses the confusion to escape. The priest eyes you with more suspicion than before.
opt_temple_identify.partial: Your hunch is half right: you point at someone who was only hiding stolen bread, not silver. Still, it clears you of the original charge.
opt_temple_identify.success: You noticed before anyone the odd bulge in another traveler's tunic. You point it out calmly and the priest, grateful, clears you of all suspicion at once.
opt_temple_identify.text: You calmly point out the real suspect
opt_thief_friend.fail: The distraction half works: you get through, but a legionary saw you leave the alley. Best stay away from here for a few days.
opt_thief_friend.journal: The boy with the purse repaid the favor at the patrol. In Rome, no one forgets.
opt_thief_friend.partial: The boy guides you over the market's low rooftops. You nearly fall twice, but it works. Before leaving he says: "Now we're even."
opt_thief_friend.success: It's the boy you didn't chase. Without a word, he tips a crate of hens into the middle of the checkpoint. In the chaos, he leads you down a passage only street kids know. You're already through.
opt_thief_friend.text: A small figure waves at you from an alley…
opt_toll_paid.fail: The group is new and your name means nothing to them... until a rider arrives with the password. You lost a while, but the network worked.
opt_toll_paid.partial: They're slow to place you, and there's an ugly moment, hands on hilts. Then someone remembers and it all eases. You pass with your heart pounding.
opt_toll_paid.success: The oldest of the group narrows his eyes and knows you. "That's the one who paid the toll. Let him through." No one else touches you. In this world, a word is worth more than a sword.
opt_toll_paid.text: "Ask your boss about the one who paid the toll."
opt_traveler_cart.fail: The cart loses a wheel half a league on. You end up pushing on a swollen ankle, both of you laughing at the absurdity. Still, you didn't walk alone.
opt_traveler_cart.journal: The traveler I helped on the road picked me up in his cart when my ankle gave out. Rome is smaller than it looks.
opt_traveler_cart.partial: The cart is loaded to the top, with room only between the amphorae. You ride cramped, whole and grateful: it's more than you had a minute ago.
opt_traveler_cart.success: It's the man you bandaged a few weeks ago. He asks nothing: climbs down, lifts you onto the cart and drives the mules on. "You gave me an afternoon. I give you two leagues." The ankle rests, and so does the deadline.
opt_traveler_cart.text: A cart pulls up beside you and its driver knows you…
opt_truth.fail: The guard calls his superior. You lose several minutes explaining yourself.
opt_truth.partial: The guard hesitates, but lets you through after checking the seal.
opt_truth.success: The guard knows the name and waves you through, no more questions.
opt_varus_protocol.fail: The protocol says one thing and your nerves another: you miscount the lines and have to start over. You reach Tiro's late, the seal barely warm. Varus will know everything anyway; Tiro may too.
opt_varus_protocol.journal: Varus had told me what to do if a Claudius letter opened by itself. I did it. Trusting early saved me from choosing at night.
opt_varus_protocol.partial: You follow Varus's protocol to the letter, though the wax he gave you is old and the seal comes out dull. It passes Tiro's glance; he's sleepy. The copy of the names is already on its way to the network.
opt_varus_protocol.success: Varus told you on the first day: "If it opens, don't read it: count the lines and remember the names." You count, you remember, you mend the seal with the wax he gave you for exactly this. Nobody at Tiro's notices a thing.
opt_varus_protocol.text: You do what Varus told you to do in this case
opt_veteran_jump.fail: A sixty-year-old veteran catches your belt midair with one hand. "Discipline, lad." He sits you down with them until the argument ends.
opt_veteran_jump.partial: You jump, but snag your cloak on a ploughshare and tear it. A veteran yells something about Caesar's army. You keep going, cloak well ventilated.
opt_veteran_jump.success: You jump the first plough, dodge the second and you're across before anyone turns. The shouts behind you aren't for you.
opt_veteran_jump.text: You jump the ploughs and go on
opt_veteran_mediate.fail: Your proposal unites both sides: against you. Who do you think you are, where'd you get that idea. You leave red-faced, with an extra detour.
opt_veteran_mediate.journal: I mediated between veterans and an old landowner. Neither was happy, which is how you know it was fair.
opt_veteran_mediate.partial: The veterans agree, the old man doesn't. They move one plough so you can pass anyway, more from fatigue than conviction.
opt_veteran_mediate.success: You propose they harvest together this year and let the surveyor decide the rest. Both sides think, spit and shake hands. They clear the road for you like a tribune.
opt_veteran_mediate.text: You propose splitting this year's harvest
opt_veteran_wait.fail: The surveyor doesn't come: he sent word for tomorrow. The veterans decide no one moves until then, you included. They let you go when they get bored.
opt_veteran_wait.partial: The surveyor arrives late and measures twice. The veterans win by a hand's breadth and the old owner leaves in tears. You pass with a lump in your throat that isn't yours.
opt_veteran_wait.success: The surveyor arrives with his groma and his patience, measures, drives in a new boundary stone, and everyone goes quiet. The veterans pull the ploughs and share their posca. Tempers, for today, hold.
opt_veteran_wait.text: You wait for the surveyor with them
opt_vote_burn.fail: A tavern keeper tries to save the ledger from the fire and burns his hand. There's shouting. In the end the ledger burns and the night ends with a bandaged hand and an odd silence.
opt_vote_burn.partial: Half applaud and half protest: the ledger was their insurance too. You burn it anyway. Lucius puts a hand on your shoulder. He wrote it; he lets it go.
opt_vote_burn.success: Lucius brings the ledger from Livia's and sets it on the table. You throw it on the hearth without a word. Two hundred names turn to smoke. Nobody applauds: you hear twelve people breathe for the first time in weeks.
opt_vote_burn.text: You propose burning the ledger before all
opt_vote_posta.fail: The proposal splits the table and two tavern keepers storm out, slamming the door. The ten who remain accept. Ten of twelve isn't everyone, but it's enough to start.
opt_vote_posta.journal: I proposed the Ox become a Guild way station. If the Appia tavern keepers work for the network, the network protects them. They voted yes.
opt_vote_posta.partial: Half distrust the Guild, the other half distrust you. They argue until dawn. In the end they vote yes, with conditions. Lucius smiles: that's how things get voted on for real.
opt_vote_posta.success: You explain the idea: if the inns on the list give Guild couriers a bed and soup, Varus protects them. An arrangement everyone understands. They vote with their jugs: twelve thumps on the table. The Ox is now a way station.
opt_vote_posta.text: You propose the Ox as a network way station
opt_vote_split.fail: The pages get mixed up and two tavern keepers take the wrong one. They have to be tracked down the next day. It works, a day late and with a lot of wine.
opt_vote_split.partial: They divide it, but some pages hold two inns' names and nobody agrees. It ends in a game of dice. Odd, but it works.
opt_vote_split.success: You cut the ledger page by page and give each their own. Let each guard their own name. They like it: nobody has everything, everybody has something. Lucius keeps the last page, his, in his apron.
opt_vote_split.text: You propose each one takes their own page
opt_wait.fail: Right when your turn comes, the guard changes. Everything starts over. The sun moves across the sky and you're still in the same line.
opt_wait.partial: The inspection is slow and thorough. A bored legionary asks you too many questions. You lose most of the afternoon, but you come out clean.
opt_wait.success: You wait in line with the patience of an ox. The centurion checks your cargo, nods, and even points out the shortest road. "Those who wait hide nothing," he mutters.
opt_wait.text: You wait for the inspection to finish
opt_wait_dog.fail: The guard takes ages. You lose time, but you get there.
opt_wait_dog.partial: The guard takes his time but finally shows up.
opt_wait_dog.success: The guard appears, scolds the dog, lets you in.
opt_wait_dog.text: You wait patiently for the guard
opt_wait_shift.fail: The relief never comes: today the beggar is pulling a double shift. You end up going in by the sacrificial door, among the bleating of lambs that know their fate. The smell never leaves.
opt_wait_shift.partial: The shift change takes longer than expected, and waiting while doing nothing is an art you haven't mastered. A vendor offers you chestnuts three times. You finally get in, hungry.
opt_wait_shift.success: At the eleventh hour, the beggar-who-doesn't-beg gets up and another comes to replace him. In the thirty paces it takes them to cross, the steps go blind. You're already inside.
opt_wait_shift.text: You wait for the "beggars" to change shift
opt_wait_storm.fail: The "shelter" turns out to be home to a family of bad-tempered boars. Between the scramble and the rain, you lose more time than you thought.
opt_wait_storm.journal: I waited out the storm in a hermitage. Varus says a dry package beats a fast post.
opt_wait_storm.partial: The shelter is barely a rock ledge. You come out numb and half soaked, but the package stayed dry against your chest.
opt_wait_storm.success: You find an abandoned hermitage with its roof intact. While the world falls apart outside, you dry your things by a small fire. The storm passes; you go on.
opt_wait_storm.text: You find shelter and wait it out
opt_walk_proud.fail: Three steps from the top, you tread on the hem of your own new livery and the stumble draws giggles from two scribes. Rome is a theater and today you were the clown. The delivery goes well; your pride, bruised.
opt_walk_proud.partial: Your high chin lasts until halfway up, where a former consul looks at you like a stain on his toga. You finish the climb dignified but sweaty. Inside, at least, the letter speaks for you.
opt_walk_proud.success: You climb the steps as if you owned them. The murmurs change tone: from mockery to question, which in the Senate is a promotion. "Claudius's new courier," you hear. New. Courier. Claudius's. Three words, three chains, a future.
opt_walk_proud.text: You climb up the middle, chin high, as Claudius said
opt_wanted_face.fail: The post chief is out and no one wants to decide. You sit a long hour on a bench while the watchman eats. At last the chief arrives, looks at you and says: "Not him." That simple, that late.
opt_wanted_face.journal: They wanted me for the temple theft. I came forward and explained, and they believed me. Running back then was a costly mistake.
opt_wanted_face.partial: They hold you an hour while they check your story with the temple. Once it's confirmed, they let you go with a warning: next time, stay and explain.
opt_wanted_face.success: You come forward, head high, and tell the temple story in full detail. The watchman writes, checks with his chief, and finally rubs out the sketch with his thumb. "The thief was someone else. We caught him a week ago." You could have spared yourself the fright.
opt_wanted_hood.fail: A hood in broad sunlight is the most suspicious thing on the road. They stop you, pull it down, compare. An hour of explaining to a watchman who's decided you're guilty until his chief says otherwise.
opt_wanted_hood.partial: You get through, but the watchman sees your back and something nags him. He shouts "Hey!" as you round the corner. No one follows. This time.
opt_wanted_hood.success: You stick close to a wood cart and pass crouching while the watchman studies a fat merchant with a similar nose. On the other side, you breathe. Still a suspect, but far away.
opt_wanted_hood.text: You pull up your hood and slip between the carts
opt_wanted_witness.fail: The priest is away on pilgrimage. His assistant doesn't know you. You end up explaining everything to the watchman anyway, half an hour lost in between.
opt_wanted_witness.partial: The priest remembers you but won't walk. He gives you a signed tablet. The watchman reads it warily and lets you through grudgingly.
opt_wanted_witness.success: The priest lives two streets away and remembers you well: the messenger who ran off looking innocent. He comes along, talks to the watchman, and the sketch is erased. Now you have a witness to your innocence.
opt_wanted_witness.text: You find the temple priest to vouch for you
opt_watchers_confront.fail: The man has a friend behind the milestone and the talk turns ugly. You leave before it comes to blows, but now there are two following you.
opt_watchers_confront.journal: I asked the Appia lookout who was paying him. He didn't give me the name, but he gave me the ledger's price. It's high.
opt_watchers_confront.partial: You sit and he gets up without a word. You let him go. You know he's a lookout now, and he knows you know.
opt_watchers_confront.success: You sit, take one of his figs and ask who pays him. He chokes on his. He says he doesn't know the name, only that they pay well to know where the ledger sleeps. You get up and he doesn't move. He got the message.
opt_watchers_confront.text: You sit down next to the fig man
opt_watchers_field.fail: You get lost in identical olive groves and come out right in front of a lookout. He salutes you with a fig. He saw you, and you know it.
opt_watchers_field.partial: The fields are muddy and a vineyard dog chases you to the stream. You reach Aricia, but with your sandals caked in mud.
opt_watchers_field.success: You leave the road at a bend and cross vineyards and ditches to the first houses of Aricia. The milestone men keep watching an empty road.
opt_watchers_field.text: You cut across the fields to Aricia
opt_watchers_pace.fail: You go so slow, so natural, that a cart catches up and blocks your way for half an hour. The lookouts see you the whole time, stuck behind the cart.
opt_watchers_pace.partial: You keep your pace, but the fig man gets up and follows you a long stretch. He tires before you do. You arrive with a tense back.
opt_watchers_pace.success: You walk like any courier, neither hurrying nor slowing. The milestone men get bored: they see nothing odd. At the seventh, there's no one.
opt_wedding_cut.fail: They take you for part of the procession and someone shoves you into the middle of the dance. Escaping the party takes longer than waiting would have.
opt_wedding_cut.partial: You cut through the crowd, but bump into a slave's tray of wine. You come out the other side with a stained tunic and several stares.
opt_wedding_cut.success: You weave between dancers and guests with quick apologies and quicker steps. You're out the other side of the procession before anyone notices your hurry.
opt_wedding_cut.text: You slip through the crowd to cross faster
opt_wedding_greet.fail: The bride's father knows you're nobody from the family, and the party halts for an awkward moment. You apologize and cross quickly, amid other people's laughter.
opt_wedding_greet.partial: The greeting works, but someone asks which family you're from. You improvise a name and leave before the question comes again.
opt_wedding_greet.success: You congratulate the bride's parents with just the right formality. They take you for a distant guest and even clear you a path of honor through the dancers.
opt_wedding_greet.text: You greet the family as if you'd been invited
opt_wedding_wait.fail: The procession stops so long you start becoming part of the scenery. The groom's drunk uncle insists on reciting the family's full genealogy.
opt_wedding_wait.partial: The party stops right in front of you for an impromptu toast. You wait with the cup they offer you, unable to say no.
opt_wedding_wait.success: You step aside and the whole procession passes, with music and flying nuts. Someone tosses you a flower for no apparent reason. You go on in a better mood.
opt_wedding_wait.text: You step aside and let the party pass
opt_wolf_fire.fail: You fall asleep past midnight and the fire dies on its own. You wake at dawn, heart pounding, fresh tracks a yard from your blanket.
opt_wolf_fire.partial: The wind puts the fire out twice and you spend the night feeding it with shaking hands. You greet dawn exhausted but whole, with firewood to spare.
opt_wolf_fire.success: The high fire keeps the pack at bay all night. At dawn only tracks remain around the camp, a perfect circle of curiosity and respect.
opt_wolf_fire.text: You build a fire and wait for daylight
opt_wolf_read.fail: You mistake old marks for fresh ones, and the shortcut you choose brings you too close. You back away slowly, unhurried, heart in your throat.
opt_wolf_read.partial: Your reading is half right: you avoid the pack but not a nervous fox that follows you, growling, for a good while.
opt_wolf_read.success: You recognize the signs: fresh tracks, marks on the bark. The pack hunts downriver, not here. You cross the stretch calmly, almost curious about your own craft.
opt_wolf_read.text: You read the ground and find where they aren't
opt_wolf_run.fail: In your flight you lose the trail and circle the same stand of trees three times before finding the way out. The pack, it seems, was only watching.
opt_wolf_run.partial: You run and trip on a root that nearly costs you the package. You reach the clearing with scraped knees, but the howls already sound far.
opt_wolf_run.success: You run the wooded stretch at the speed of your own fear, which turns out to be quite fast. You reach the clearing without looking back once. The howls stay behind too.
opt_wolf_run.text: You hurry on without looking back
opt_wreck_guard.fail: You doze off in the sun, and when you open your eyes the chest is still there, open and empty. Someone has left you an amphora of wine beside it, as an apology.
opt_wreck_guard.journal: I guarded a shipowner's chest on a beach full of looters. Nobody asked me to.
opt_wreck_guard.partial: You guard the chest, but the locals take everything else. The shipowner's agent arrives and thanks you for the chest with the face of a man who lost a ship.
opt_wreck_guard.success: You sit on the chest and glare at anyone who comes near. In the afternoon the shipowner's agent arrives, opens it, checks everything and notes your name for a future reward.
opt_wreck_guard.text: You guard the chest until someone comes
opt_wreck_survivors.fail: You search the rocks and find no one, only the ship's dog, who follows you wagging its tail. Now you have a dog. That wasn't the plan.
opt_wreck_survivors.partial: You find the sailor, but the sea tumbles you as you pull him out. You both reach the sand coughing, alive, each thanking his own god.
opt_wreck_survivors.success: Among the rocks you find a sailor clinging to a mast. You pull him out and leave him by a fire. He tells you the ship's name, which all of Ostia will want to know tomorrow.
opt_wreck_survivors.text: You search the rocks for survivors
opt_wreck_take.fail: A harbor guard sees you with the amphora and makes you return it and give a statement. You lose time and your name as an honest courier.
opt_wreck_take.partial: The amphora weighs twice what you thought and slows you the whole stretch. When you arrive, you open it: it's garum, and half rotten.
opt_wreck_take.success: You shoulder an amphora of wine like any local and walk on. What the sea brings, the sea gives. The wine turns out to be Chian, the good stuff.
opt_wreck_take.text: You take an amphora and move on
place.La Loba Dorada — taberna sin carte: The Golden She-Wolf — tavern with no sign
real_01.lore: Your first official delivery. The port of Ostia expects trade documents before the day's close.
real_02.lore: The Via Appia takes you into the heart of Campania. Beware of bandits in the wooded stretches.
real_03.lore: You cross the Alps to reach Gaul. A route reserved for seasoned messengers.
real_04.lore: A short errand to Tibur, among summer villas and the cool murmur of waterfalls.
real_04.package.0: An invitation to a summer dinner
real_04.package.1: A personal errand for a magistrate's villa
real_05.lore: The Temple of Fortune at Praeneste awaits a message that can't be a day late.
real_05.package.0: A sealed offering for the temple
real_05.package.1: A priest's letters to his family in Rome
real_06.lore: The coast of Antium, a patrician retreat, awaits correspondence that would rather not travel alone.
real_06.package.1: An urgent request from a retired patrician
real_07.lore: A short hop between Neapolis and Pompeii, on roads that smell of sea and sulfur.
real_08.lore: The Sibyl's cave awaits at Cumae. They say the roads talk there too.
real_08.package.0: A written question for the Sibyl
real_09.lore: Beneventum, crossroads of the south, needs news that can't wait for the next caravan.
real_10.lore: Among the northern marshes, Ravenna and Aquileia talk through messengers, not reliable maps.
real_11.lore: The coast between Pisae and Genua is equal parts beautiful and treacherous. Bring a cloak.
real_11.package.1: A purchase contract for ship timber
real_12.lore: Tarentum, port of the south, pays well to whoever beats the rumor there.
real_12.package.1: Shipping papers bound for the East
real_13.lore: Brundisium ships out to the East. Whatever arrives late stays on the dock.
real_13.package.0: Embarkation orders for the Legions of the East
real_14.lore: A full day's road to the frontier at Aquileia, where Rome starts doubting its own maps.
real_14.package.0: Border treaties for the regional governor
real_15.lore: Two days' road to Massilia, in Gaul. The longest route a messenger can take without asking why.
real_16.lore: The urgent-orders satchel. A fresh horse at every way station, and no one asks why the rush.
real_16.package.0: A bankruptcy notice that must arrive before the rumor
real_16.package.1: The missing signature to close a grain sale
real_17.lore: Sealed dispatches for the fleet. The whole Appia, military station to military station, a legate's safe-conduct at your belt.
real_17.package.1: The payroll of a legion waiting at the port
real_18.lore: A fishing boat without a lantern, a cargo in no register, and a captain paid to ask no questions.
real_18.package.0: A small chest heavier than it should be
real_18.package.1: Letters from a freedman to a partner nobody knows
real_19.lore: A senator's letters for his partners in Massilia. Fast ship, private cabin, and orders to deliver by hand, whether the sea likes it or not.
real_19.package.0: An olive-oil contract bearing three families' seals
real_19.package.1: A letter not to be read aloud
real_20.lore: Claudius's private correspondence, between the Senate and his villa. Pays well, and no one asks you anything; you don't ask either.
real_20.package.0: A draft speech with cross-outs in the Senator's own hand
real_20.package.1: A box of dried figs with a letter at the bottom
real_21.lore: The Tenth's post along the Appia. With the bull plaque, checkpoints open; bandits, less so.
real_21.package.0: A cohort's pay, in a box with three locks
real_21.package.1: Marching orders sealed with the bull of the Tenth
real_curia.lore: The Curia's letters heading north on the Flaminia. Every senator wants to know first; you get there before them all.
real_curia.package.0: A Senate decree with the wax still soft
real_curia.package.1: A consul's letters for the magistrates of Ariminum
real_nocturna.lore: The post that appears in no register. The Underworld pays well to those who keep quiet and walk by night.
real_nocturna.package.0: A leather-wrapped package no one explained to you
real_nocturna.package.1: A sealed box that smells of foreign incense
real_ravenna.lore: The Thirteenth's post from one side of the Rubicon to the other. The checkpoints know you; so does the river.
real_ravenna.package.0: Fodder reports for the coastal cohorts
real_ravenna.package.1: A legate's order, folded in four and unsigned
real_valija.lore: The satchel with the Guild's seal, the only one both sides let through unopened. It weighs little and is worth much.
real_valija.package.0: Letters from mothers to sons in both camps
real_valija.package.1: A promissory note between two merchants who don't speak
rest.ending_lucius_family.name: The Ox way station
s1_varus_dilemma.description: Before setting off for the villa, you pass the barracks. Varus's lamp is lit, as always. A senator has summoned you behind your commander's back. You can go in and tell him. Or you can walk on and keep this story yours alone.
s1_varus_dilemma.title: Loyalty Keeps Hours
s1_villa_gate.description: At night, Claudius's villa is a marble fortress. The note said "come alone," but not how to get in. The main gate has two guards. The service door, a cook having a smoke. The wall, old ivy.
s1_villa_gate.title: The Service Door
s2_followed.description: Since the northerner paid, you've had company: two men who cross the street when you do, who gaze into shop windows with no glass. You can't lead a tail to the temple.
s2_followed.title: Your own shadows
s2_northman_offer.description: A man with a northern accent blocks your way with surgical politeness. "Two hundred denarii. Just to see the seal. Don't open it, don't touch it." Nobody pays that to look at wax. Unless the wax says everything.
s2_northman_offer.title: The northerner
s2_temple_watchers.description: At night the Temple of Saturn has more watchers than worshippers. On the steps, a beggar who doesn't beg, a sweeper who doesn't sweep. Everyone watches without watching. The letter weighs in your tunic as if it knew.
s2_temple_watchers.title: The temple's eyes
s3_broken_seal.description: On the Tiber bridge the scroll falls and the third seal splits. You read without meaning to: "...the evidence against Petro, whose gold sustains Varus's network of messengers..." Claudius isn't cleaning up Rome: he's sawing off the branch you're standing on.
s3_broken_seal.title: The burning letter
s4_claudius_men.description: Near Petro's villa, three men with good cloaks and better swords block your way. The one in the middle smiles: "Senator Claudius regrets to inform you that your career as a courier ends tonight."
s4_claudius_men.title: Claudius's men
s4_guild_shadow.description: On the bridge, a figure leans on the rail. You know him: Marco, a network messenger who taught you the river shortcuts. "Varus knows what you're carrying," he says, no greeting. "He sent me to ask for it. Me. For friendship's sake."
s4_guild_shadow.title: A familiar face
s4_night_patrol.description: At night the city belongs to the patrols, and tonight there are more than ever: someone important pulled strings and the vigiles stop anything that walks. You can't stop.
s4_night_patrol.title: Rome after curfew
s4_rival_buyer.description: At the door of the Golden She-Wolf, a luxurious litter blocks your way. Inside, a man with heavy rings: Petro's agent. "We know what you're selling and to whom. Petro pays double for exclusivity... and triple to know who else is buying."
s4_rival_buyer.title: The counteroffer
s5_claudius_face.description: Claudius waits for you on the steps, older than last week. In Rome, losers age by defeat. He recognizes you from afar and his face doesn't change: patricians lose with the same expression they win with.
s5_claudius_face.title: The Forum steps
s5_petro_gift.description: Before you leave for the Forum, one of Petro's slaves intercepts you with a small box: "The Senator insists." Inside, a silver ring engraved with a raven. Senators' gifts are never just gifts.
s5_petro_gift.title: A patrician's gratitude
s5_senate_steps.description: The Senate steps are a parade of togas that eye you like new furniture: Claudius's livery on a network messenger's body. Some murmurs go ahead of you. Others follow.
s5_senate_steps.title: The steps of the Curia
s5_two_doors.description: First delivery: Claudius's villa. Second: Petro's. The same envelope, the Widow's same handwriting, unsigned. Your job: both receive it by hand and see your face as they read. Nobody explained that part.
s5_two_doors.title: Two doors, one message
s5_varus_cold.description: Back from the Senate, fate puts Varus in your path on the Aemilian bridge, with two of the new ones. He sees you. He sees the livery. The new ones look at the river. All of Rome fits on this bridge.
s5_varus_cold.title: The last greeting
s5_widow_toast.description: Back at the Golden She-Wolf, the Widow waits with two cups poured and the back table cleared. In the Subura, the Widow pouring your wine is a contract, an adoption and a warning, all at once.
s5_widow_toast.title: The Widow's toast
tut_01.intro: Varus, your superior in the messenger network, hands you a small sealed scroll. His eyes size you up without pretense.
tut_01.lore: "Take this to the South Gate. A simple test — I want to see how you move."
tut_01.package: Sealed note for the guard at the South Gate
tut_02.intro: Varus gives a slight nod. He seems satisfied. But his next order comes before you can catch your breath.
tut_02.lore: "Good. Now something harder. Lucius the innkeeper doesn't trust strangers — you'll have to win him over."
tut_02.package: Coded message for Lucius the innkeeper
tut_03.intro: This time Varus doesn't smile. The correspondence bears three wax seals. One of them belongs to the Senate.
tut_03.lore: "This is the last test. Senator Claudius expects this before noon. No one can know I sent you."
tut_04.intro: Varus looks at you differently now. Not as a candidate — as someone who could be useful.
tut_04.lore: "You passed the tests. This is no exercise anymore. The Legions need these orders before dawn."
tut_evt_01a.description: The South Gate guard looks you up and down. "Who sent you, boy?"
tut_evt_01a.title: The guard stops you
tut_evt_02a.description: The direct way is blocked by a makeshift market. There are two routes.
tut_evt_02a.title: Crowded alley
tut_evt_02b.description: Lucius the innkeeper stares at you. "I don't know your face. Why should I trust you?"
tut_evt_02b.title: Lucius is wary
tut_evt_03a.description: You notice a hooded man who has turned up at two different corners. Could be coincidence.
tut_evt_03a.title: Someone is following you
tut_evt_03b.description: Claudius's villa has a huge doorman who won't let you in. "The Senator sees no messengers without an appointment."
tut_evt_03b.title: The Senator's doorman
tut_evt_03c.description: Claudius accepts the message, but before letting you go he asks: "Who else knows about this?"
tut_evt_03c.title: The Senator asks questions
tut_evt_04a.description: A patrol of four legionaries blocks the road. Curfew holds after sunset.
tut_evt_04a.title: Night patrol
tut_evt_04b.description: A huge dog chained at the entrance barks wildly. The guard inside is slow to appear.
tut_evt_04b.title: Camp dog
tut_evt_04c.description: "The orders are genuine, but I need to confirm you are who you claim. Who is your superior?"
tut_evt_04c.title: The Centurion checks your identity

w_deliver5.intro: The tablets are piling up. If five go out this week, I owe you one.
w_deliver5.journal: Décimo crossed five tablets off his pile and paid me gladly.
w_deliver8.intro: Market week: everybody's writing. I need someone who won't stop.
w_deliver8.journal: Eight deliveries in one week. Décimo says he's never seen the pile so low.
w_events_success4.intro: Mercury protects those who know how to choose. Show me you're one of them.
w_events_success4.journal: Atia burned incense in my name. She says Mercury knows me now.
w_events_success4.role: priestess of the temple of Mercury
w_first_s.intro: One perfect delivery a week. It's all I ask of you, and all I'll remember.
w_first_s.journal: Varus gave me a Seal without a word. From him, that's a lot.
w_grade_a3.goal: Earn 3 grades of A or better
w_grade_a3.intro: Bet you can't make three clean deliveries in a row. If you do, I'm buying.
w_grade_a3.journal: Marco lost the bet. He paid in full without complaining, which is rare.
w_guild_routes.intro: My leg's a wreck. Can you cover the house routes for a few days?
w_guild_routes.journal: I covered Marco's routes. He thanked me in his own way: saying he runs them faster.
w_legion_routes.intro: The military post is short-handed. Carry our mail and the Gate will remember.
w_legion_routes.journal: Sexto wrote my name on the Porta Capena tablet. He says it's so nobody asks for my pass.
w_long_legion.goal: Complete a route of 8 h or more
w_long_legion.intro: Anyone can run for an hour. I want to see who lasts a whole day on the road.
w_long_legion.journal: Sexto saw me arrive muddy to the knees and laughed. Then he poured me wine.
w_long_patrician.goal: Complete 2 routes of 8 h or more
w_long_patrician.intro: I have relatives far away and letters that won't wait. I need legs that don't tire.
w_long_patrician.journal: Fulvia's letters went far. She paid without looking at the bill.
w_patrician_routes.intro: My husband trusts anyone. I don't. Carry the villas' mail and we'll see.
w_patrician_routes.journal: Fulvia received me in the atrium, not at the servants' door. It's a start.
w_resolve6.intro: My husband used to say the road tests you six times a week. Tell me if he was right.
w_resolve6.journal: I told Cornelia what happened on the road. She cried a little, then laughed at the bit about the bridge.
w_underworld_routes.intro: I won't ask what you carry if you don't ask whose it is. Two trips, and we're friends.
w_underworld_routes.journal: Rufo paid me in coins from three different mints. I didn't ask where from.
